On XX/XX/year> my wife made a XXXX purchase of shirts from a charity using our Chase Freedom XXXX card. The amount was $92.00. On XX/XX/XXXX, I noticed a $10.00 transaction that simply said " TRANSACTION FEE '' on my account. I inquired and was told that was the fee they charged for " Cash-like transactions '' which is what they consider XXXX, apparently. They agreed to remove the $10.00 fee as a " one-time courtesy ''. It is absurd that a $10.00 fee on a $92.00 purchase is even allowed, as this is almost an 11 % fee simply for using a competing service to Chase 's XXXX service. 

I then found out that in addition to the $10.00 fee, they have coded this $92.00 as a cash advance transaction. I called to inquire about how to pay off the cash advance portion of my balance, as it was subject to daily interest of almost 30 %, and was told that I can not simply pay off the cash advance portion. In order to stop the daily usurious interest, I must pay off my entire balance, for both purchases and cash advances. It does not matter that I automatically pay off my entire balance every month, they are going to be charging me daily for the cash advance portion, and I can not make a payment directly to the " cash advance '' portion of my balance. 

I went to the branch to dispute with a live person, but was told that all credit card business was only handled through their outsourced customer service phone line. 

This seems unfair. If they are going to separate out a specific balance to be charged a higher interest rate, do I not have the right to make a payment specifically to that part of the balance? I accept the responsibility for not keeping up to date with the fine print of my credit card agreement, which they can change on a whim, but this arbitrary rule makes it difficult for people to manage the interest they are charged when hit with an unexpected " cash advance '' that was no such thing.

TRANSFER OF FUNDS FROM XXXX TO JP MORGAN CHASE, XXXX. 

XX/XX/XXXX - I decided to close my account with XXXX in the XXXX and transfer the funds to my JP Morgan Chase account in the XXXX. The balance in my account was XXXX I called XXXX and asked what exchange rate they would give me and they said $1.00 = XXXX. The spot rate at the time was $1.00 = XXXX. I then called Chase Bank customer service and spoke to agent XXXX at XXXX. I asked her the same question and she told me $1.00 = XXXX. I confirmed that I would get the spot rate and she said yes. 

XX/XX/XXXX - I initiated the transfer in UK for conversion in the US. 

XX/XX/XXXX - the funds were credited to my account in the sum of $41000.00, which represented an exchange rate of $1.00 = XXXX. The monetary difference between the rate that I was quoted by XXXX and the actual rate used was $980.00. 

XX/XX/XXXX - I made several phone calls to customer service to try and resolve the issue but got nowhere. XXXX of the agents even transferred me to XXXX  XXXX XXXX! I then went to my local branch in XXXX XXXX, CA and met with XXXX XXXX. XXXX told me that the funds were converted into US dollars in the UK which was incorrect. I think he was trying to shift the blame onto XXXX. XXXX then contacted the Branch Complaint Escalation XXXX and I was told that I would get a call within XXXX hours. 

XX/XX/XXXX thru XX/XX/XXXX - I had not heard from the Complaints Group so I called XXXX XXXX times. He did not pick up the phone and there is no ability to leave a voicemail. 

XX/XX/XXXX Finally, I got a call from XXXX XXXX in the Complaints Group and I explained everything, including the exact time and day that I had spoken to XXXX, the agent who told me that I would get the spot rate. She told me that she needed some time to investigate. I spoke to her again a few days later and I asked her if she had found the recording of the phone call with XXXX. She confirmed that she had found the recording and had listened to it. I heard nothing further from XXXX before I left on a XXXX trip to XXXX at XXXX end of XXXX. 

XX/XX/XXXX - A secure message was sent by XXXX XXXX XXXX Chase app saying they had been unable to contact me and that if I still wanted to speak to her that I should call her phone number and quote the case number that was assigned. 

XX/XX/XXXX thru XX/XX/XXXX - I left XXXX voicemail messages for XXXX but none of my calls were returned. 

XX/XX/XXXX Fortunately, I found a general number for the Branch Complaint Escalation Group and left a message for someone to call me back. 

XX/XX/XXXX I did not get a call back, so I left another voicemail message on the general line and later that day XXXX called me back. I again explained everything that had happened and gave her the case number. I asked if XXXX had left the Bank and, after checking, XXXX told me that she still worked at Chase. I asked why she had not returned any of my calls, but she did not know why. XXXX said she would investigate my case and get back to me in XXXX to 7 days. 

XX/XX/XXXX - XXXX left me a voicemail and I returned her call later that day. She told me that nothing could be done. She said that the bank always charges a " spread '' on foreign transactions. I pointed out, again, that a Chase agent had told me I would get the spot rate. She apologized and repeated that nothing could be done. I then asked if there was an arbitration process and she said yes but I would need to hire a lawyer to contact their legal department. I said that I wasn't prepared to spend money on a lawyer and that I would go through Small Claims Court. She said I would need a lawyer for that so why not go through arbitration. I explained that lawyers are not permitted in Small Claims Court. 

XX/XX/XXXX - In a last-ditch effort to avoid litigation I went into my same local branch, explained the situation and asked if there was anything that could be done. The banker told me that the manager was out of the office but would be back on Monday and that he would have the manager call me on Monday or Tuesday. I never received a call. 

XX/XX/XXXX- I investigated the small claims process and discovered that I needed to put my claim in writing which I did on XX/XX/XXXX, letting them know that I would file a Small Claims Action on XX/XX/XXXX. I received a response saying that my message would be shared with the appropriate department. I left on a XXXX trip to XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX and, assuming there was no settlement, I planned to file a Small Claims action. 

I have spent a considerable amount of time trying to resolve this issue. I have been passed around from department to department, my calls have not been returned and, I feel, Chase has not acted in good faith. If I end up going to court, I plan to seek punitive damages.

text:
I made a purchase with a Chase credit card. They offered and I accepted an interest-free 18 month extended payment My Chase XXXX. After XXXX payments they told me I had paid off the plan, despite the fact that I still have a significant balance on this purchase. 

I asked why this happened and they said it was because I received a credit of more than the balance and it was applied to my loan, thus paying it off. This credit was for a purchase that was canceled within minutes of the charge, and clearly should have been applied to that purchase. However buried within the terms of the loan are terms that say credits are first applied to the loan. 

I feel this is deceptive, as the net effect, and XXXX sure it is not lost on Chase, is that it effectively pushes the loan terms from low or no interest to the maximum credit card rate if the purchaser does not have the cash on hand to pay off the loan balance. This is particularly insidious as most are unlikely to remember for 18 months that they cant have any credits applied to the card account. Furthermore it negates any budgeting that one might have done while taking that payment plan into account. 

This sort of hidden up charging of interest rates should be banned. And if not banned the consumer should be given the choice of how a credit is applied to their account.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am filing a formal complaint against Visa for their gross mishandling of a dispute related to charges from XXXX XXXX XXXX. Despite clear evidence of fabricated documentation and serious misrepresentations by the merchant, Visa overturned a previously resolved dispute in my favor, resulting in significant financial harm and emotional distress. 

Summary of the Complaint : Acceptance of Fabricated Documentation : Visa accepted documentation from the merchant that was clearly erroneous and unrelated to my transaction. The documents included another individuals name and address, incorrect service dates, and a forged signature. This should have been identified as fabricated during Visas review process, yet it was inexplicably accepted as valid. 
Misrepresentation by the Merchant : The merchant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, misrepresented themselves as a moving company when they were actually operating as a broker. This crucial information was never disclosed to me, leading to a significant misunderstanding of the services I was engaging in. Visas acceptance of their documentation allowed this misrepresentation to go unaddressed.

Unjustified and Inflated Charges : I was provided with an initial estimate by the merchant, which was later doubled without any justification. Despite providing evidence of this price gouging, Visa still sided with the merchant, demonstrating a lack of thorough investigation and disregard for fair consumer treatment. 
Overcharging for Supplies : I was overcharged for moving supplies that were either not used or incorrectly categorized, leading to inflated costs. Visas review process did not properly address this, further exacerbating the financial harm I suffered.

Failure to Provide Agreed Services and Missing Items : The merchant failed to provide the agreed services, including unpacking at the destination, and several valuable items were missing upon delivery. Despite providing detailed evidence of these failures, Visa ignored these issues, leading to an unjust decision against me.

Impact on Me : Visas acceptance of fabricated documentation and their failure to properly investigate this dispute have caused me significant financial loss and emotional distress. This experience has severely undermined my trust in Visas ability to protect consumers from fraudulent practices. 
Requested Resolution : I am requesting that the CFPB investigate this matter thoroughly. I seek a re-evaluation of my dispute, expecting that Visa will correct

its mistake and refund the disputed amount. I also request that the CFPB ensure Visa implements more rigorous review processes to prevent such failures in the future.

I am prepared to provide any additional information or documentation the CFPB may require to support this complaint. 

Thank you for your attention to this serious matter. 

Sincerely, XXXX

text:
I was a First Republic checking account customer. When Chase purchased First Republic, I automatically became a customer of Chase. This transition occurred approximately XX/XX/year>. The checking account product I've had since this transition is Chase 's Premier Plus Checking, the comparable account they offered me based on my First Republic account status at the time of the acquisition. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a letter titled " Important information regarding the recent transition of your account ( XXXX ) ''. 

The letter states : " Dear Valued Customer, to better meet your banking needs, we have re-evaluated the recent transition of your First Republic account. As a result, we will change your account to a new Chase account with additional features and benefits on XX/XX/year> ''. 

The new account is identified as " Chase XXXX Checking ''. 

The letter continues : " If you change your account to another account type before XX/XX/year>, you will stay in the account you select and you can disregard this letter. Otherwise, you will change to ( Chase Sapphire Checking ) ''. 

Nowhere in the letter does it say I have the option to keep my previous checking account, the account Chase supplied to me following the First Republic acquisition. In fact, the only two options suggested by the language above are a. ) I accept the change to Chase Sapphire, or, b. ) I change to another account. 

It should be noted that the Chase Sapphire account requires a much higher requirement to avoid a $ 25 Monthly Service Fee. The daily minimum starting balance ( of the account or linked qualifying investments ) is $75000.00 to avoid the monthly fee. My current account features a requirement of $15000.00 in order for Chase to waive the monthly service fee. 

After determining that Chase was not eliminating the Premier Plus Checking account I currently have, I called Chase customer support to say I simply wanted to keep the account I currently have and that I found the letter to be highly deceptive, as it failed to offer the option of maintaining my current account status. At this point, customer support told me that in order to keep my current account and make NO CHANGE to my current customer status, that I need to visit a Chase bank branch and speak with a customer representative. 

Believing this couldn't possibly be true, I called again and spoke with a different customer support agent. The second agent also told me that I must visit a bank branch in order to make NO CHANGE to my current checking account. I requested to speak with a supervisor. The supervisor told me the agents were correct. I notified the supervisor that I live in rural XXXX XXXX ( CA ), and that the nearest Chase branch was at least a XXXX minute XXXX XXXX. She acknowledged that requiring a customer to visit a bank branch for no reason whatsoever was unreasonable, but that this is Chase policy. I told her I refuse to comply, and will be filing a complaint. She told me she " would submit a back office ticket '' and that I would receive a call from Chase within two hours.

Approximately 20 minutes later I received a call from a fourth Chase agent. However, this agent notified me that he was unable to assist as he is in the " Chase Retail Research '' division. It's clear the supervisor devised the " submit a ticket '' ruse simply to get me off the phone. 

I strongly question the legality of requiring a customer to visit a bank branch to simply keep their current account status. Further, I find the letter that I received from Chase to be highly deceptive as it clearly suggests ( through omission ) that simply maintaining my current account status is not an option. Please note the above mentioned use of " change your account to another account type ''. 

This type of deceptive marketing and account management is utterly reprehensible. I will be closing my Chase account as soon as I can and will actively share my experience so others can appreciate the depths to which Chase management has sunk. 

Shame on Chase.

text:
I am writing to formally address the unlawful closure of my Visa XXXX card, which I have recently discovered. This action, taken without proper notice or justification, is not only a breach of our agreement but also a violation of federal regulations, specifically those under Regulation Z.

As previously communicated, my account is subject to an ongoing billing error dispute, and I have exercised my rights under 12 CFR 1026.13 ( d ) ( 1 ). This regulation clearly prohibits you from treating any portion of the disputed amount as delinquent while the dispute remains unresolved. Closing my account while it is under dispute is an adverse action that directly violates this regulation, as it penalizes me for withholding payment on a disputed amount. 

Under 12 CFR 1026.13 ( d ) ( 3 ), you are prohibited from restricting, limiting, or closing my account in retaliation for exercising my rights to dispute billing errors. The closure of my account, without resolution of the dispute or proper legal basis, constitutes a retaliatory action and is therefore unlawful. This action has caused significant financial harm, disrupted my access to credit, and further exacerbated the ongoing dispute.

Federal regulations, including the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), require that I be provided with adequate notice before any adverse action, such as account closure, is taken. This notice must include the specific reasons for the action and the steps I can take to remedy the situation. I have not received any such notice, nor have I been given the opportunity to address the purported reasons for the account closure, making this action unlawful. 

The unlawful closure of my account may result in inaccurate information being reported to credit reporting agencies, potentially leading to violations of the California Consumer Credit Reporting Agencies Act ( CCRAA ). If any negative information related to this closure is reported, it will further compound the harm caused by your actions and may subject Chase Bank to additional legal liability.

Closing my account without just cause or due process is a breach of the Cardmember Agreement, as well as a violation of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing inherent in all contracts. This breach undermines the trust and confidence that forms the foundation of our relationship and exposes Chase Bank to potential legal action for damages. 

Failure to promptly address and rectify these issues will leave me with no choice but to escalate this matter to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ( OCC ), and potentially pursue legal action to seek redress for the damages caused by Chase Bank 's unlawful actions. I expect your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to a swift resolution.

text:
I applied for a home loan with Chase which was approved. As we worked thru the process and reviewed the home inspection results, there were some issues that needed to be fixed, one being some foundation work. I ended up negotiating a $16000.00 seller credit because of the issues needing to be fixed and the seller not wanting to pay out of pocket to fix those items before closing. My realtor told me to confirm with the lender that the $16000.00 seller credit would actually be applicable as closing as there are generally some restrictions on how much seller credit a buyer can get at closing. I emailed my loan officer, XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>, and explicitly asked if there was a maximum seller credit that I could receive at closing, and I specifically mentioned that I had negotiated a fairly substantial $16000.00 credit and wanted to make sure I wasn't exceeding the seller credit cap. His reply was " The maximum contribution you can receive is 6 % of the purchase price ''. The purchase price of the home was $430000.00 so according to XXXXXXXX XXXX reply, I was clear up to $25000.00 in seller credit. On XX/XX/year>, as the loan proceeds to underwriting, I get an email from XXXX that the seller credit ( $16000.00 ) plus lender credit ( $1500.00 ) in total is more than the closing costs and by law, I can not apply offset more than the closing cost using credits. Essentially, what they ended up saying was that I can not receive cash back on a purchase or use credits to reduce my down payment. At this point, after having accepted a seller credit that I needed to use to pay for foundation repairs, I was told either the seller credit is reduced ( meaning I whatever credit remains after offsetting closing costs ) or I find a way to use the credit in the loan. I ended up having to escrow homeowners insurance ( which I never do ) and then apply $6900.00 of the remaining seller credit to buy down the interest rate just so that I didn't completely lose the seller credit I negotiated. In the end, I got stuck having to pay an additional $6600.00 out of pocket for the foundation work after the loan closed. That foundation repair bill was supposed to have been offset by the seller credit. If I was properly advised that seller credit could not exceed closing costs, I would have forced the seller to fix the foundation issue and not taken on the burden of that cost myself. I was misled by my lender and deem this to be complete negligence as they are responsible for making sure I am provided accurate information, especially when I explicitly ask a simple, straightforward, and critical question. I am fighting to get cash back from Chase to actually pay for the repairs, but they have been taking their sweet time " reviewing the case ''. To make matters worse, 2 days before closing, Chase tells me that they can not close the loan because they came across an amendment that was on file for weeks stating that I needed the seller to have a licensed electrician visit the property and properly label the electric wires. In the end, seller didnt do that because we agreed that would be something I handled in the $16000.00 credit. That amendment was never executed but was always available to Chase to review. They didnt bother to do their due diligence and then put me in a tough spot the night before closing ( after I tried to fight back on the request ) as I had to find a licensed electrician to spend 5 minutes labeling wires. That cost me $300.00 out of pocket. Completely ridiculous and incompetent team that I was made to work with. 
They need to own up to their mistake an offer compensation. I asked for $7000.00 to help offset the foundation repair I had to pay for out of pocket along with the $300.00 I had to pay an electrician at the last minute.
sub_issue_raw: Closing disclosure or other related disclosures

Pursuant to TILA 15 USC 1641 ( f ) Treatment of servicer ( 1 ) In general A servicer of a consumer obligation arising from a consumer credit transaction shall not be treated as an assignee of such obligation for purposes of this section unless the servicer is or was the owner of the obligation. ( 2 ) Servicer not treated as owner on basis of assignment for administrative convenience A servicer of a consumer obligation arising from a consumer credit transaction shall not be treated as the owner of the obligation for purposes of this section on the basis of an assignment of the obligation from the creditor or another assignee to the servicer solely for the administrative convenience of the servicer in servicing the obligation. Subject : Complaint Against CHASE CARD SERVICES for Violations of XXXX XXXX, Public Law XXXX, UCC Provisions, Federal Regulations, U.S. Codes, and Unlawful Closure of Accounts Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I am filing this formal complaint against CHASE CARD SERVICES for numerous violations of my rights, including but not limited to : failure to honor lawful payment instruments, improper retention of securities, violation of XXXX and holder-in-due-course laws, breaches of federal regulations and U.S. Codes, unlawful closure of accounts, and potential theft, fraud, language fraud, and securities fraud. Detailed Summary of Violations : Failure to Honor Securities and Lawful Payment Instruments : I tendered lawful payments using securities and negotiable instruments provided by CHASE CARD SERVICES, such as bills, statements, equity checks, bearer bonds, and coupons attached to the statements. This provision mandates that any obligation is discharged to the extent of a payment made by a negotiable instrument unless that instrument is returned or dishonored. Their retention of the securities without action violates my rights as both a creditor and holder of the instruments. 
Unlawful Closure of Accounts and Definition of " Accounts '' : It is important to clarify that the term account inherently means a place for deposits and withdrawals, not a static or limited financial agreement. As such, CHASE CARD SERVICES unlawfully closed my accounts even after I had discharged the related debts through the lawful tender of securities. These accounts, by their nature, should be considered open-ended credit plans, which should not have a predetermined limit. Under my unlimited right to contract, as protected by the U.S. Constitution, I am entitled to maintain these accounts without arbitrary closure, particularly after meeting my financial obligations through lawful payments. 
The attempt to impose artificial credit limits or close my accounts after the debt was discharged is unlawful. Showing limits on an open-ended credit plan, as CHASE CARD SERVICES has done, is illegal and contrary to both the terms of open-ended credit and contract law principles. Their action constitutes a breach of XXXX XXXX concerning the resolution of debts through accord and satisfaction and violates my constitutional right to contract freely without interference.

CHASE CARD SERVICES has used deceptive or unclear language that obscures the nature of my rights and obligations, particularly in regard to the use of lawful money and the nature of the securities provided. By misleading me about the status of the accounts and payments, they are potentially engaging in fraudulent misrepresentation under 18 U.S. Code 1341 ( Mail Fraud ) and 18 U.S. Code 1343 ( Wire Fraud ). 
Violation of Holder-in-Due-Course Laws : As the holder of the securities and negotiable instruments I tendered, I am entitled to the protections and rights outlined in UCC XXXX. Violation of U.S. Codes and Federal Regulations : By refusing to process the private instruments I provided, unlawfully retaining my securities, and denying my right to claim them, CHASE CARD SERVICES has violated various U.S. codes, including 12 U.S. Code 411, which governs the issuance and use of lawful money. The improper handling of these private instruments suggests potential violations of 15 U.S. Code Chapter 41- Consumer Credit Protection. 
Failure to Discharge Debt Under the Emergency Banking Act and Gold Clause : According to Public Law XXXX ( Emergency Banking Act ) and HJR XXXX, all debts must be discharged upon the tender of lawful money. I am writing to formally request the issuance of IRS Form XXXX for an alleged debt that you charged off and reported to the credit reporting agencies. According to the information provided in my credit report, this debt has been categorized as " charged-off '' and, as such, I am seeking clarity on the tax implications of this action, as well as confirmation of the cancellation of the debt. 

Legal Definition of Charge-Off A charge-off occurs when a creditor treats an account as uncollectible and writes off the outstanding balance as a loss for tax purposes. Under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ), when a creditor determines that a debt is unlikely to be collected, the debt is charged off, effectively removing it from the creditor 's active receivables. This action signifies that the creditor has made the decision to cease further collection efforts through their internal process. Under IRS regulations, any forgiven or canceled debt of $600.00 or more may be considered income to the debtor and requires the creditor to issue a XXXX form, documenting the cancellation of debt. 

Request for XXXX Issuance Since this debt has been charged off, I am requesting that you fulfill your legal obligation by issuing a Form XXXX, which reflects the cancellation of this debt. This form is necessary for me to address any tax obligations with the IRS, should the cancellation amount be considered taxable income. According to IRS guidelines, creditors must file a Form XXXX when a debt of $600.00 or more has been canceled or forgiven, and you must provide a copy to the debtor. 

Accuracy of Information under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), it is your responsibility as a creditor to ensure that all information you report to credit reporting agencies is accurate and complete. Continuing to report a " charged-off '' debt without acknowledging the cancellation of the debt or issuing a XXXX XXXX result in inaccurate reporting, which violates this provision of the FCRA. Any inaccuracies that affect my credit report must be rectified immediately to prevent damage to my credit standing. 

Given that you have written off this debt and no longer expect payment, it is important that you comply with the reporting requirements under federal law by issuing Form XXXX and providing me with a copy. This will serve as confirmation that the debt has been canceled, and I will be able to properly address any related tax implications. 

Request for Immediate Action Please issue and send me XXXX XXXX within 30 days of receiving this letter, in compliance with your legal obligations. Failure to do so may result in the filing of complaints with the IRS, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), and other regulatory agencies, as well as legal action for violations of the FCRA.

If the debt has not been canceled or forgiven, I request a written explanation and clarification of the current status of this alleged debt, including a full accounting of the balance and any further collection activity. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving Form XXXX within the specified time frame. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX

Throughout the process I was informed that more than XXXX application was submitted for review, which was inaccurate, but caused considerable difficulties for the representatives of the bank trying to process the correct application ( on one respective call I was told contradictory information about whether a correction could be made on the existing application or an entire new application would need to be created and submitted. ) Throughout the process of opening the line of credit account the bank and its representatives apparently initiated a process of, what they termed colloquially a hard credit pull on at least three separate occasions, that Im aware of. Ive been reliably informed that the very act of performing a so-called hard credit pull, just once, may have a negative effect on ones credit worthiness score, let alone three or more times. So, the very same entity making a decision on my creditworthiness ( credit score ) was potentially, negatively affecting said credit score over a several weeks period as a result of their own errors, omissions and incompetence. Based on that very same score a computer based system and/ or a banker makes a decision what annualized percentage rate ( APR ) I should be given. This rate was allegedly, needlessly set higher, then it would have been otherwise, had the credit issuer maintaned the proper systems and or properly trained staff in place to process the application correctly the first time it was submitted.

Upon discovering the charges, I rushed to a Chase branch, where I was redirected to the Fraud Investigation Department ( XXXX ). However, I was initially unable to file a claim due to a system update. After multiple attempts, I finally filed the claim on XX/XX/XXXX, and was told I would be reimbursed within XXXX business days if the investigation was not resolved. After significant delays, I was informed that my claim was denied, with Chase stating the transactions were made using my device. 

I am appealing this decision based on critical evidence that was overlooked, as well as conflicting information provided by Chase Bank representatives. 

Supporting Information : Device Log-In Timing : My computers kernel-power logs ( attached ) show my device first booted on XX/XX/year>, at around XXXXXXXX XXXX  This means my device was not in use prior to that time, making it impossible for any earlier transactions to have been made from my device. 

Browser History : My browser history ( attached ) confirms that I attempted to log into my Chase account at XXXXXXXX XXXX  However, I was blocked by a device attestation message ( also attached ), preventing me from successfully logging in. 

Secure Messages : I have attached secure messages ( not emailed to me ) from the Chase Bank app showing that two employees, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX, were added to my account as payees without my knowledge. These messages state that the additions were made by an authorized user on my account. However, during a phone conversation, a Chase representative explicitly told me that I am the only authorized user on this account. This presents a serious inconsistency in Chases handling of this case and suggests a breach of account security. 

Conflicting Information : Chase Bank has provided conflicting information at every step. On XX/XX/XXXX, I was told the money would be credited within a few hours, but the funds never arrived. When I followed up, I was told there was no definite time for reimbursement. 

Conclusion : It is clear that unauthorized actions were taken on my account before my device was in use, and I was blocked from accessing my account after attempting to log in. The claim denial based on device matching is flawed, especially given that I was the only authorized user on the account, and these fraudulent payees were added without my consent.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding my recent experience at a Chase Bank branch in XXXX, TX, on XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX  XXXX As a long-standing Chase customer, I have routinely completed significant transactions, including cashing and depositing checks up to $50000.00, at various Chase branches in XXXX, TX . Brief summary : I was confused by my terms of service regarding interest on a credit card with a balance transfer balance on it. As a result, I have been paying extra interest charges through no fault of my own ( other than not being able to read the agreement and understand it better than the people that work for the actual company ) and the company even after reviewing the calls ( or at least saying that they reviewed the calls ) where I was clearly given incorrect information says that they dont owe me a fix. 

XX/XX/XXXX I called Chase to ask what would happen if I made purchases on my card that had a balance transfer on it. I was told that I would have to pay 1 month interest on the purchases no matter what but that if I paid it off immediately then it would go towards the balance with the highest interest rate ( the new purchases ) and then I would basically only pay one month of interest. 

XX/XX/XXXX I noticed I was getting charged interest every month for the purchases even though I paid them off as soon as the transactions cleared and called to find out what happened. I was told by an account specialist ( somebody who presumably knew more than who I spoke to in XXXX ) that the last representative explained it wrong and that the interest would happen no matter what even if I paid off the full amount. They said they would waive the interest and that I could call back to continue to have the interest waived. I said that didnt sound right and said surely there was some amount I could pay today that would go towards the balance with the highest interest rate and make it so I was only paying interest on the balance transfer. She told me over and over that that is not how it works and I just need to keep calling to have the interest waived. I reluctantly agreed. 

XX/XX/XXXX I call after a few months to get the interest waived assuming there are at the very least notes on my account. The rep ( another account specialist ) says that the last account specialist was completely wrong. He says he cant waive the charges and he can only ask somebody to review the calls. I accept and wait. 

XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX The letter says they cant remove all the balance transfer fee and interest charges of the previous months ( which isnt even what I asked for I only asked for a few specific charges from XXXX to XXXX for the PURCHASES specifically to be removed ) and that everything that happened was fine according to the agreement that I signed. There was also nothing in the letter that even indicated that the calls were actually listened to because it stated nothing about the conversation. It just says the charges are legitimate so we deny your request. It did not address the fact that I had been given incorrect information by the employee and left the call thinking the issues was resolved when it was not through no fault of my own. 

XX/XX/XXXX XXXX call Another account specialist ( the 3rd one Ive spoken to ) finally explains to me exactly what went wrong. I paid the transactions off before the statement processed and so it didnt count towards the balance I thought it would count towards. Ok fine maybe that was a miscommunication in XXXX of XXXX or maybe thats just a flat-out mistake on my part. I tell them I offered multiple times in XXXX to make a payment that would have according to this employee solved the issue because it would in fact have gone towards the higher interest balance. They said that that isnt their problem. They will train the employee better but they dont owe me anything and it is not their issue to resolve because everything that happened was according to the terms of agreement. 

Im not sure how Im supposed to understand the agreement when multiple of their own employees dont seem to understand how it works and apparently, I did understand it and offered the correct solution in XXXX but was specifically told by AN ACCOUNT SPECIALIST that it would not solve the issue. 

I also dont understand how they mess up, give me the wrong info and charge me a bunch of money that I shouldnt have to pay them and in return for me spending hours on the phone with them, the outcome is that they get info to train their employees better and I get nothing and have to pay for THEIR mistakes. 

After stating this the employee ends the call without my consent saying there is nothing more they can do and nobody else I can talk to. 

XX/XX/XXXX XXXX call I call back and speak to another account specialist who tells me the same thing, they dont care if they told me wrong, that they will train their employees from the interaction, and that they dont owe me a fix. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX letter I get the second letter in the mail which again gives no indication that the phone calls were actually listened to and does not offer any details of the call or my request. Thank you in advance for taking the time to read my letter and process my dispute case. 

I am writing to re-open a dispute that I filed in XX/XX/year> for a purchase made at XXXX XXXX. The previous dispute, which has been closed by Chase, was filed under an incorrect reason chargeback code 13.7 ( Canceled merchandise / services ). This was likely an error from the Chase representative I had spoken to when opening the dispute. I would like to re-open the dispute under the correct reason code, 13.3 ( Not as described or Defective Merchandise/Services ). 

I have attached two documents. One is the letter I sent to Chase in the initial dispute. The second is the letter I sent to Chase after they closed my initial dispute, having misunderstood the chargeback code that should have applied to my dispute. 

***Merchandise or services are not the same as your verbal description*** We were measured for 2 suits, 2 dress shirts, a winter coat, and a dress at XXXX XXXX physical store location. XXXX XXXX employees repeatedly assured us that they were certified clothing producers for XXXX and that the clothing we received would be XXXX brand and quality. They also made claims to the fabric quality, saying that the suits and coat would be 100 % cashmere wool, and the would be silk. 
When we received the merchandise a few days later, the clothing did not match the description. The clothing was cheaply made, using synthetic materials like polyester. The clothing was not XXXX brand like they claimed it would be. Additionally, the clothing fit very poorly, despite the measurements taken of us while we were in the store. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX made us sign waivers after we had paid for the merchandise in order to protect themselves from chargeback disputes. However, note that we had not received any merchandise upon signing these waivers. Please be advised that all of the photographic waiver evidence XXXX XXXX provides to Chase were waivers I had signed AFTER we paid for the product but BEFORE it was received. 

The waivers state : - I hereby acknowledge that I have chosen the styles, colors, and the quality of the fabrics myself and the products will be produced according to my size, measurements and specifications. 
- As I have made all the decisions myself, I also understand that XXXX XXXX is an independent private tailoring company and not affiliated or under influence of any brand names. 
- As all above mentioned clothes are custom made for my size, I acknowledge that XXXX XXXX maintains No Refund Policy, under any circumstances. I am happy and satisfied with my payment and merchandise Effective immediately. I also agree not to make any disputes through my bank or otherwise after this transaction - I acknowledge satisfactory receipt of relative goods and services Again, this waiver was signed immediately after I had paid for the clothing, but the merchandise had not been received since it was going to be custom made days later. This is misleading in many ways : - First, the quality of fabrics that we were shown during the sale was not the same fabric used to create the clothing. We could not possibly say we are satisfied with the purchase before we even received the products- Second, the entire time we were in the store, XXXX XXXX employees were showing us XXXX catalogs from which we could choose which style and color of clothing we wanted. I asked them multiple times, and they assured us they were a certified producer for XXXX, and that they would be making us the same clothes they produced for XXXX XXXX. Therefore everything they were saying about the brand and the quality of the clothing was a lie and used as a tactic to make us agree to a purchase. This was also the only reason I agreed to pay $1500.00 for this clothing. A non-branded custom suit from a Thai tailor costs less than $100.00. And since the waiver was given to me after I had made the payment, I essentially had no choice but to sign at that point. 
- XXXX, XXXX XXXX states a No Refund Policy and a No dispute policy. Consumer protection laws classify this type of policy as illegal, and not enforceable, especially in cases where the merchandise has been gravely misrepresented. 

- Lastly, I could not have possibly acknowledged satisfactory receipt of relative goods and services- I signed this waiver when I paid for the clothing, which was a few days before XXXX XXXX made the clothes. 

***Attempts to resolve with merchant*** After I had made the payment and left the store, I became suspicious of what had just happened. I looked up their store online and I saw many reviews online saying they were a scam operation, and that other customers received clothing completely different than what they were promised. I went back into the store minutes later to tell them I no longer wanted the clothes but they were firm in asserting their no return policy. At this point, the merchant seemed intent on keeping our money no matter what. It is hard to prove I went back to the store to cancel the purchase, but I did make a good faith attempt to cancel the purchase before they started making the clothing. 
Thank you for taking the time to consider my dispute case. I hope, with this additional information, we can come to a fair conclusion.

text:
Chase Bank used the promise of a $300.00 bonus to entice me into signing up for a checking account and reassign my direct deposits to them. While I have followed their instructions, they have refused to let me access my funds which are now deposited into the Chase account. Multiple, patient, attempts to understand the situation and work with the bank towards a solution have led nowhere. Per my understanding of my most recent of many conversations with Chases bankers there is no explanation as to why I can not access my money, and thus no way to solve an unidentifiable problem. In essence, I should accept that two of my paychecks have simply disappeared, close the account, and move on. I financially and temperamentally can not accept that. 
A few weeks ago, I received a mailer from Chase advertising a $300.00 reward for signing up and receiving direct deposits totaling more than $500.00 within the first 90 days of your account. As someone who earns very little in New York, this was a great incentive to open my second-ever checking account. I would not have opened that account if not for the offer. 

On XXXX XXXXXX/XX/XXXX, I took some time off work and quickly walked about a mile over to the Chase Bank located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. There, a staff member told me that I would require a statement from my previous bank, or other utility bill, as proof of residency ( rather than my health insurance bill which I had with me ). Since the banks would have reduced hours on Saturday and high demand, she advised me to find the offer online and open the account from home. She showed me how to navigate to the Chase Bank website and open an account there. 

On XXXX XXXXXX/XX/XXXX, I settled in and looked up the offer as it was written on the mailer. It was displayed prominently on Chases landing page and a link took me to begin the process of opening my account. Five minutes after noon, Chase emailed me that my account was ready to use. Furthermore, they had a form already pre-filled with my account information to give to my employer and make Chase the destination for my direct deposits. Just over an hour later, I alerted my employer that I would like all future direct deposits to go to that Chase account. 

I got my first hint that something was wrong when my account stopped working sometime either on XX/XX/XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX. On the XXXX of this month, Chase sent me an email saying that my account was restricted. On the XXXX, I headed to the Chase Bank at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. There, a banker told me that my account had a restriction because they needed to verify my identity. I had brought several documents including my passport, XXXX, and mail in anticipation of that exact scenario. After a while on the phone with Chases XXXX , he assured me that all should be well. I tried logging on again and my account appeared to be working. Unfortunately, that was short-lived. 

Later that day, I knew I should have received my paycheck as a direct deposit, and yet the account still showed a balance of $0.00. I returned to the XXXX XXXX Chase and saw a different banker. She also connected me to XXXX who told me that my account was closed-pending and that she could not process the direct deposit. At that point, I told her that another banker had just addressed that restriction for me, and fortunately, he was within my line of sight. I waived him over and he spoke briefly to her, and they agreed to call in another department that handled the restriction. There, I underwent an extensive verification process with multiple pop quiz-style questions to identify me ( What color is your XXXX XXXXXXXX, etc ). 

Finally, the phone banker told me that I was once again verified, but there was no direct deposit, which directly contradicted the banker Id just spoken to on the phone who said there was a direct deposit that could not be posted because of the restriction. To me this was the largest red flag that there was essentially no accessible holistic accounting record, at least to do with me, at Chase Bank. Every time an issue arose I would have to start explaining to someone who not only had no idea but had no other way of knowing what else was happening with my account. That pessimistic outlook turned out to be unfortunately prescient. Both bankers told me that the deposit would soon reflect on my phone within a day or two and there was nothing else to worry about. 

Indeed, my balance soon began to show my direct deposit. I thought after three attempts and perhaps as many hours I had finally settled my affairs with Chase and could begin to use my money. Since my rent was due by the end of XX/XX/XXXX, I used the night of the XXXX to set up a recurring monthly XXXX with my roommate beginning then and again on the last day of every month. Chase emailed me at XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX saying they could not process my XXXX. At this point, I had tired of Chase and knew this would mean going back to the bank, being assured that I was verified, before suffering the same trouble. I was beginning to panic and despair. 

I missed my rent payment on the XXXX because of Chase Bank. The XXXX was equally consequential because failure to pay my electric bill would amount to voiding my payment plan, meaning my power would be turned off unless I could pay nearly what I make in XXXX months all at once. At this point, nearly all my money was tied up at Chase. 

On Monday, I took time off work to go to the XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXXXXXX Chase branch again. There, I was once again put on a phone with XXXX of the banks tele-staff. He spoke to me for perhaps XXXX minutes and then put me on hold for nearly fifteen. 

At some point on the XXXX, my Chase debit card arrived in the mail, so I hoped that I could withdraw the money and quickly pay my bills. When I got to the ATM, it asked me to verify by email, which I did, and then told me that it could not process the withdrawal and to call a given number. I called the number and the banker told me that my account was once again on close-pending and that nothing could be done. By the time I got home from the ATM, ConEdisons app was displaying a large red notice demanding that I pay my entire balance in full. 
None of this would have happened if Chase actually authenticated my account when they said they did, or let me know that they couldnt, or at any point put a notice for other bankers so that I did not have to explain the same story and listen to bankers do the exact same thing that had not worked. 

I understand that folks in finance may find financial precarity alien. But for those of us in service, minimum wage, and hourly jobs when you have your money is as important as if you have it. I make just enough to get by. Chase Bank has now put me in a financial predicament that will set me back months all because they wouldnt authenticate an account after XXXX ( XXXX ) different follow-ups despite insisting they had already done so in a majority of those visits.

Before leaving I opened the envelope to see the receipt but there was no receipt. I asked if she could give me a receipt for my transaction and she refused. I then stated again that I wanted a receipt and again she refused she was not going to give me a receipt that there was no receipt which is extremely odd. She said mentioned something about the $10.00 fee again but that does not explain or has anything to do with my wanting a receipt. This is extremely worrying that a transaction involving money would generate no receipts and that upon asking for XXXX they would blatantly refuse to comply which is why I am reporting them accordingly. I had to leave but have since tried to call customer service but they are completely useless, the agent did not know what to do in fact I'm not sure he understood what I was asking. To activate this service you go to your chase account, look through your purchases and some of them will have an indication that they are eligible for pay over time. The doctor sent me info for a company called XXXX XXXX that provides XXXX % APR loans for medical purchases but I looked at the reviews and they were scathing. I need to know if I can use this service in this way or if I need to arrange for another payment option such as XXXX XXXX or another bank. I called Chase and asked for this information, at first they said " Oh we understand why you want to know, unfortunately there is no way to know in advance if a purchase will be eligible '' this was unacceptable to me so I spoke to an account supervisor. She said the same thing. When I asked her " Well it can't be random these determinations have to be made according to a policy. '' She said " It is random sir, we even don't know thats why we tell people to never expect a purchase to be offered eligibility to that pay over time feature. '' I even asked, since I will have XXXX identical charges of $2000.00, if XXXX of them is offered pay over time if it will be guaranteed the other ones will as well, provided that the vendor is the same, the customer is the same, and the total amount does not exceed the credit limit of the card? The supervisor said " Its not a guarantee, I've seen it where people in this situation are given pay over time for some of these, but not all, and sometimes none. '' I said I'd like to file a complaint because this kind of opacity in offering what is essentially a loan isn't above board. I filed a complaint. Now I am reporting this to you because of the following concerns : XXXX. Lack of consumer transparency into financial services XXXX. Any time a financial services company says determination is " random '' or algorithmic, it is a recipe for discrimination and price fixing XXXX. The fact that customers cant make financial decisions with all the facts ahead of time is a guarantee that some people are going to misinterpret the tool and get trapped in bad financial predicaments XXXX. There is a legal definition of a loan, there are legal requirements for conditions of loans. I am concerned that these pay over time options are essentially loans, but the idea that they are being offered after purchase makes them able to fall outside of the traditional definition of a loan and thus skirt legal requirements for loan conditions. XXXX. On the whole it seems pretty shady and I trust that professionals in the CFPB will have the experience and expertise to extrapolate why this practice is problematic for consumers.

text:
In late XXXX all four of my Chase XXXX XXXX had an offer of $100.00 after spending $500.00 or more booking through Chase travel online. 

I added the offers for all four cards planning to book flights and lodging for a trip next year. The offer was set to expire on XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/XXXX I used XXXX of the cards with the offers activated to make purchases online through Chase travel of $500.00 ( XXXX ) and $530.00 ( prime card XXXX ). Both of these honored the terms laid out on the offer details. 

On Saturday XX/XX/XXXX I did not receive the credit yet and could not see the offer listed any longer on the two cards I used, so I called Chase Customer Service. The representative informed me that she did not see the offer on the cards at all. Fortunately, I screenshotted the offer for the Chase sapphire card to send to a friend and had it in my records. However, she did not see any such offer offered or activated on that card. I explained that I otherwise would not have booked through Chase travel if it were not for this offer. I was then transferred to Chase travel to get a refund for the two purchases totaling $1000.00, but they informed me it was too late to cancel without a penalty. 

I researched online and this is not the first instance of this occurring. It turns out other Chase customers have issues receiving credit for offers they have added, and the offers disappear before they are honored. 

Through a post documenting this by another customer, https : XXXX? XXXX I was able to call the XXXX XXXX office phone number. A representative reported that she saw that the offer on my sapphire card ( XXXX ) but that it was not offered or added to my prime Visa card ( XXXX ). I know this is not true because I double and triple checked before I booked that it was there even if I don't have a screenshot to prove it for the prime Visa card. In addition, on my chase online banking platform, both my sapphire card and prime XXXX card did not have the offer visible any longer, but my freedom and freedom unlimited continued to have the offer advertised since I did not use them yet. Why are the offers offered to all four cards I have and gone from the two cards I used the offer on? Of note, I made the huge mistake of being honest with her and telling her that I screenshotted the offer added to my card to a friend to inform him of the offer existing, and did not screenshot the one for my prime Visa card because I did not anticipate needing to do so for proof purposes. This was probably a convenient excuse to say the offer was never added since she knew I did not have proof for my prime card. 

I asked her to honor the credit from these two offers, but she said there was only proof that one was added when I know for a fact it was added to both. 

I believe the offer was a bait and switch to attract customers to book, and as soon as they are out of the window for a refund, the offers are removed from the card and the customer is gaslit into thinking they made a mistake and the offer was not present in the first place.Again, this is not the first time for this to happen ( see XXXX post linked above- as the customer did not screenshot his offer either, but it honored eventually after multiple complaints ). 

I have attached this offer in pictures below. 
These practices are shady for such a big credit card company and I would like them to be held accountable for future transactions. I also bank with XXXX XXXX and they usually send an email immediately after an offer is honored confirming eventual receipt of the credit. Chase has no such policy and it is based on trust which is obviously not warranted as seen in this deceptive situation of removing offers after the customer is already baited to book through their platform. 

Specific offer details are copied and pasted below. 

Earn $100.00 cash back on your Chase XXXX purchase when you spend $500.00 or more, including taxes and after any discounts. 

One place to book, so many places to go. Earn and redeem points for hotels, flights, car rentals, activities and more at chasetravel.com. 

Offer expires XX/XX/year>. Offer valid one time only. Offer only valid on purchases made directly at chasetravel.com. Offer valid online only. Offer not valid on purchases made using third-party services or a third-party payment account ( e.g., buy now pay later ). Complete payment for your Chase XXXX purchase must be made by XX/XX/year>. 
This offer is only eligible on bookings made through Chase XXXX. 

Disclaimer Chase is only responsible for posting the statement credit to your account based on the data it receives from its third-party service provider. It is possible that a merchant may split your purchase into multiple transactions. In this case, you may only receive your statement credit on the first transaction amount. If this occurs, please call the number on the back of your card. The statement credit will appear on your statement within 14 business days of Chase 's receipt of this information. 

If you purchase a subscription service, your card may be billed for automatic renewals at recurring periods without further notice from the merchant. This offer will not apply to such renewals once the offer expires or is fully used.

On XX/XX/2024, I used this credit card to rent a vehicle from XXXX. The rental period was from XX/XX/2024 to XX/XX/2024. Unfortunately, during this rental, a minor scratch occurred on the vehicle on XX/XX/2024. 

Upon returning the vehicle to XXXX on XX/XX/2024, I submitted the necessary acceptance report, fully aware that the CDW benefit on my Chase credit card should cover the damage costs.

text:
Chase issued XXXX balance transfer checks on two of my Chase issued credit Cards. I deposited the Chase issued check, account had enough credit available, and Chase returned their own check causing my checking account to be overdrawn. First attempt via the call enter was useless. Next step was a visit to the local branch. I spoke with a CSR they called both Chases credit card center and the deposit checking team to be told the checks need to be negotiated inside the branch and the CRS had to call the credit card division to obtain an approval code. Nothing ion the material provided by Chase spoke of these requirements. 

Since the check was with Chase processing and they could not use the original check to issue the approval code I used another check on a separate Chase credit card account to deposit. The CSR obtained the approval code wrote on the face of the check and deposited it. The next day that check was also returned by Chase continuing the overdraft on my account in the amount of $5500.00! Back to the same branch I went for a second time to try and resolve the issue. The CSR looked at my account and said the funds would be available in the next 24-48 hours. Today I received a text message from Chase that my account was overdrawn. The same CSR that assisted me the first time I went to0 the branch assisted me again today. Only after being persistent, did he get to a Credit Card supervisor who said Chase DID NOT issue me any checks on the one credit card when clearly, I has the letter and additional check in my possession and the second check that was returned was issued to the account that they claim never had checks issued on it. Only due to my insisting to speak with the credit card supervisor did she tell me that Chase was having a SYSTEMIC internal issue with the convenience checks it issued and all of them are being returned. They never had the presence of mind to let their STAFF ON THE FRONT LINES AT THE BRANCJED KNBOW OF THIS ISUUE! 

Now they stated they will credit back any NSF items I paid electronically but my Mortgage and other bills will be reported to the credit reporting agencies as delinquent. 

Chase stated this is a SYSTEMIC issue and therefore more consumers will be facing the same issues I did. To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : This complaint concerns Chase Auto Finance 's deliberate violations of my rights under multiple federal laws, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), and Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). Chase has engaged in egregious and deceptive practices, including unauthorized credit inquiries and inadequate disclosures, violating my right to privacy and consumer protections. I demand immediate action, compensation, and punitive sanctions against Chase to ensure this type of misconduct does not persist.

1. Deceptive Pre-Screening : Bait-and-Switch Tactic Chase 's Just For You pre-screening offer was a fraudulent bait-and-switch that enticed me into applying for an auto loan under false pretenses. The language used in the pre-screening offer falsely led me to believe I was pre-approved for a loan, only for Chase to later deny my application. This deceptive practice, which wasted my time and damaged my credit score, demonstrates a clear violation of consumer trust.

Chase 's failure to honor the reasonable expectation they set through their deceptive pre-screening process is fraudulent, and I demand that the CFPB impose severe sanctions to prevent this manipulative behavior in the future. 

XXXX. Unauthorized Credit Inquiry : A Gross Violation of Privacy Chase 's actions show complete disregard for my privacy rights. By pulling my credit report without providing me with a clear and conspicuous opt-out option, and failing to inform me of the specific terms before conducting the inquiry, Chase has violated FCRA 604 ( a ), which governs permissible purposes for obtaining a consumer report.

The right to privacy is fundamental, and Chases unauthorized inquiries into my credit history are a clear violation of my rights. Under FCRA 616 and 617, I am entitled to statutory damages of $1000.00 per violation. Given the multiple unauthorized inquiries Chase made on my credit report, I demand full compensation for each of these breaches of my privacy. 

XXXX. Lack of Transparency and Disclosure : Intentional Concealment Chase 's lending practices are not just opaquethey are deliberately deceptive. The application process failed to disclose any minimum credit score requirements or clearly explain the criteria for loan approval. This lack of transparency violates TILA 1026.17, which mandates clear and conspicuous disclosures in all consumer credit transactions.

Chase has created an application process designed to lure consumers into applying for credit without the necessary qualifications being known upfront. Their systemic failure to disclose critical lending terms is an intentional strategy to trap consumers in a cycle of unnecessary credit inquiries, which harms their creditworthiness. This is a direct violation of TILA and must be met with harsh penalties.

4. Baseless Denial of Discrimination : A History of Bias Chases attempt to brush aside my concerns about discrimination is both offensive and deeply flawed. The CFPB should conduct a thorough investigation into Chases discriminatory practices and hold them accountable under ECOA and Regulation B, which prohibit discrimination in any aspect of a credit transaction.

Introduction : Im submitting this complaint against Chase Bank due to a mishandling of my mobile check deposit and misinformation from their representatives, which led to serious financial disruption. 

Complaint Details : On XXXX, I deposited a $ XXXX paper paycheck via Chase 's mobile check deposit feature. To my surprise, Chase placed a 12-day hold on the deposit. This delay was unacceptable, as I rely on these funds for essential expenses. 

I contacted Chase immediately to cancel the mobile deposit due to the unreasonable hold. The Chase advisor informed me that it couldnt be canceled and that Id need to wait it out. When I explained that waiting wasnt an option, another representative suggested I deposit the check at a different bank instead, claiming this would resolve the issue. I followed their guidance but decided to double-check with Chase, only to find that this was incorrect advice. Rather than taking responsibility, Chase then tried to blame me, accusing me of negligence. 

To make matters worse, Chase restricted my account, preventing access to my funds until the hold period was over. This restriction has now disrupted my autopay transactions, leading to even more financial complications. Every action I took was based on Chase 's instructions, and I am left to deal with the fallout due to their mismanagement. 

Impact : This situation has left me without access to my paycheck for nearly two weeks, impacting my ability to meet critical financial obligations and causing significant frustration. I relied on the bank 's advice, only to be left in a worse position. 

Resolution Requested : I request immediate release of my funds, removal of any account restrictions, and a review of Chases policies and training regarding mobile deposits and customer advice. Additionally, I would like compensation or fee reversals for any costs incurred due to their mishandling of my deposit.

text:
I. Introduction I am submitting this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank due to significant issues regarding my account, which have led to financial hardship, including eviction. The bank 's actionsor lack thereofhave not only impacted my creditworthiness but have also resulted in severe consequences for my livelihood. This complaint seeks to hold JPMorgan Chase accountable and requests your intervention to rectify these issues.

II. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and Disclosure Failures : Upon opening my account, I was required to provide my Social Security number and other personal information. Since that time, I have not received adequate disclosures related to the status of my account, including insurance claims, 1099-C forms for canceled debt, or details regarding any securities associated with my account. 
I request that JPMorgan Chase disclose any insurance claims, FDIC reports, and evidence of any alterations made to my account or related checks, including the specifics of any hacking incidents. 
Negative Impact on Credit Report : The lack of accurate reporting has resulted in negative marks on my credit report, which have prevented me from accessing necessary credit facilities. This has had a profound effect on my ability to secure housing and has contributed directly to my eviction.

Discriminatory Practices : I believe that the treatment I have received from JPMorgan Chase has been discriminatory. If there is evidence that other customers have been treated more favorably under similar circumstances, this could indicate a violation of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) and the Fair Housing Act. 
Failure to Address Errors : In a recent correspondence from Vice President XXXX XXXX, it was acknowledged that there are errors related to my account that need correction. Notwithstanding this acknowledgment, no remedial action has been undertaken following XXXX 's efforts to rectify these errors, thereby perpetuating the adverse effects on my financial standing. 
XXXX. Legal Basis for XXXX XXXX CFPB was established to ensure that consumers are treated fairly by financial institutions. Under the following regulations, I assert my rights as a consumer : XXXX XXXX XXXX Reform and Consumer Protection Act : This act provides the CFPB with XXXX authority to enforce consumer protection laws and ensure that consumers have access to accurate information regarding their financial products. 

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : This law requires that consumers have access to accurate credit information and provides a framework for disputing inaccuracies. The failure of JPMorgan Chase to rectify negative reporting related to my account constitutes a violation of the FCRA. 

Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) : This act prohibits discrimination in lending. If JPMorgan Chase has engaged in discriminatory practices regarding my account, they are in violation of this act. 

LEGAL VIOLATIONS Constitutional Violations : The actions of the Defendant may constitute violations of the due process rights enshrined in both the U.S. Constitution and the Michigan Constitution, particularly if adequate notice or opportunity to address negative account reporting was not provided.

Securities and Exchange Commission ( SEC ) Violations : If the Defendant engaged in securities transactions that lacked proper disclosures or failed to comply with SEC regulations, this may constitute unlawful conduct subject to regulatory action.

Code of Federal Regulations ( CFR ) Violations : The Defendant 's actions may be in violation of relevant provisions in the CFR governing banking practices and consumer protection, particularly with respect to disclosure requirements. 

Fiduciary Duties and Common Law Breaches : The Defendant has a fiduciary duty to act in the best interests of its clients. Any failure to manage the account prudently or to rectify errors could result in a breach of this duty under common law. 

Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Violations : The Michigan UCC governs secured transactions and indicates that the Plaintiff, as a creditor, holds a perfected security interest in the collateral as described in the Security Agreement. The Defendants disregard for this agreement could expose them to liability under UCC provisions.

IRS Forms 56 and 56F Compliance Issues : The Defendant has been provided IRS Form 56 and Form 56F, indicating the establishment of Power of Attorney. Failure to recognize the authority granted in these forms constitutes a breach of fiduciary responsibility.

TRUST AND DEBTOR-CREDITOR RELATIONSHIP The Plaintiff asserts that the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is identified as a debtor and that XXXX XXXX , in his capacity as Power of Attorney, is the creditor with legal rights to collect on the debts owed. The Security Agreement purportedly covers all future debts and is supported by the collateral 's value. 

The Defendants failure to honor the fiscal forms and POA authorizations supplied by the Plaintiff undermines the trust and estate 's legal standing.

IV. Importance of Resolution The resolution of these issues is critical not only for my financial well-being but also for the integrity of the banking system. A failure to address the errors associated with my account could set a dangerous precedent for other consumers who may face similar issues. Ensuring accountability within financial institutions is vital for maintaining public trust and promoting fair lending practices.

Michigan Consumer Protection Act ( MCPA ) MCL 445.901 et seq. : The MCPA protects consumers from unfair, deceptive, and misleading practices in trade and commerce. If Chases practices can be shown to violate this act, it could serve as a basis for a claim of misleading behavior. 
Michigan Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) MCL 440.1101 et seq. : The UCC governs commercial transactions in Michigan, including the sale of goods and secured transactions. Provisions related to the good faith requirement in commercial transactions and the obligation to act with reasonable care may support claims against Chase regarding their handling of the depository agreement.

Michigan Truth in Lending Act MCL 493.1401 et seq. : While primarily aimed at loan transactions, if the depository agreement includes terms related to credit, this act may impose requirements that Chase failed to meet, leading to misleading practices.

Michigan Debt Collection Practices Act MCL 445.251 et seq. : This act regulates debt collection practices and may apply if Chases actions in managing the account are construed as deceptive or unfair, particularly in how they report the principal 's credit history.

Michigan Revised Judicature Act MCL 600.2919 : This law addresses the liability for wrongful acts and could support claims regarding harm caused by Chases actions.

Michigan Administrative Code R 205.121 et seq. : These rules outline regulations concerning financial institutions, including prohibitions against unfair or deceptive acts in the context of consumer financial services.

Fiduciary Duty Principles The concept of fiduciary duty requires banks to act in the best interests of their clients. Any breach of this duty, such as failing to properly manage an account or adequately disclose terms in a depository agreement, could lead to claims of liability.

Tort Law Principles Under common law, a party can be held vicariously liable for the actions of its agents if those actions occur within the scope of employment. If employees of Chase engaged in misleading practices or failed to uphold their duties under the depository agreement, this could expose Chase to vicarious liability.

Remedies and Enforcement MCL 445.903 : This section of the MCPA provides for remedies, including the ability for consumers to seek damages, which could be applicable in a case against Chase.

Summary These laws could serve as the foundation for challenging the fairness and legality of JPMorgan Chase 's depository agreement.

V. Request for Action I hereby request that the CFPB investigate this matter thoroughly. Specifically, I ask for : An investigation into JPMorgan Chases management of my account, including the handling of disclosures, insurance claims, and reporting practices.

Assistance in rectifying any inaccuracies in my credit report that stem from the banks mismanagement.

Recommendations for corrective actions that JPMorgan Chase must take to address these issues and ensure compliance with consumer protection laws. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response and assistance in resolving these serious concerns.

Chase advertises that their XXXX XXXX XXXX includes both Lost Luggage Reimbursement and Baggage Delay Insurance when their card is used to purchase an airline ticket. The airline gave us a very limited compensation ( i.e., not even enough to cover the very stressful situation that happened to us during a family vacation ).
