text:
In XX/XX/XXXX, I visited a restaurant and gave my card to the waitress to pay for my tab. My order totaled $44.00. A few days later, I noticed that the waitress had not only charged my card for my order but had also charged it again for $120.00. This second charge was not authorized by me, as I never made a purchase for that amount. 

Upon noticing the unauthorized charge, I immediately contacted my card issuer, Chase Bank, to report the issue. I used the Chase app to go through the prompts provided and answered the questions to the best of my ability. However, the app did not allow me to provide an explanationonly to follow the predetermined options. Chase deactivated my card, which I felt was excessive at the time, but I assumed it was part of their standard process. They credited the $120.00 back to my account and informed me they would conduct an investigation. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, I was shocked to discover that the $120.00 charge had been reinstated to my account. When I called to inquire about this, I was told that Chase had determined it was not fraud because my physical card was used to make the purchase. This response was both surprising and frustrating. Just because someone has physical possession of a card does not mean the charge can not be fraudulent. Cards can be stolen, used without permission, or even misused by someone like a waitress who could have let others rack up a tab and charged it to my card ( for reference, I am not saying thats what happened ). The fact that it took me days to even notice the transaction underscores the point that it could easily have gone undetectedthat, by definition, constitutes fraud. 

Chase then informed me that I should have disputed the charge instead, claiming that it was likely an error by the waitress rather than fraud. I fail to understand how Chase can determine the waitresss intent. Regardless, the bottom line remains : the charge was not mine and should not be my responsibility. 

I attempted to explain this to the representative, but instead of assisting me, I was condescendingly lectured on the definition of fraud. When I asked to dispute the transaction, I was told that since I had initially filed a fraud claim, I would now need to write a letter explaining the situation and send it by mail. This is unacceptable. Why should I have to go through the extra step of writing a letter when I followed the process Chase outlined? When I asked to speak with a manager, the call was abruptly disconnected. 

Since then, I have contacted Chase multiple times to resolve this matter. Each time, I have been placed on hold for excessive periods when requesting to speak with a manager, told that I couldnt speak to a manager, or received callbacks from the back-end team with no notes or resolution. Meanwhile, the requirement to write and mail a letter remains unchanged. 

This is an unacceptable way to treat a long-standing customer. I have banked with Chase for years, but this experience has completely eroded my trust in your services. As soon as this matter is resolved, I intend to close all of my accounts with Chase and share on my social media platforms. I think people should know how Chase treats their customers.

text:
To : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Subject : Urgent Complaint Regarding Misapplied Wire Transfer and Mishandling by JPMorgan Chase Bank Dear CFPB Representative, I am writing to file a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . regarding a serious case of misapplied international wire transfer and the banks failure to provide timely or effective resolution. 

On XX/XX/year>, I initiated an international wire transfer of USD $25000.00 from my personal account ( ending in XXXX ) at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, to my personal account ( ending in XXXX ) at JPMorgan Chase Bank, XXXX, Connecticut, intending to use the funds for my tuition payment. 

Unfortunately, I mistakenly entered an incorrect digit in the recipient account number, which caused the funds to be deposited into the account of another Chase customer. 

Upon discovering the error the following day, I immediately visited my local Chase Bank branch to report the issue. A staff member assured me that such cases are typically resolved by returning the funds to the originating bank account and advised me to wait patiently. I also promptly contacted XXXX customer service via phone ( XXXX ) and informed them of the error. They responded that they would closely monitor the situation and cooperate with the recovery process. 

However, after several weeks of follow-up with both banks, the funds were neither returned to my XXXX account nor credited to my Chase account. Nearly a month later, JPMorgan Chase informed XXXX that the funds had been credited to another individuals account and had already been completely withdrawn. I was told that Chase was attempting to contact the recipient to recover the funds but offered no specific timeline or assurance. 

Throughout the following months, I continued to make phone calls and inquiries to both Chase and XXXX, repeatedly requesting updates and urging XXXX to issue formal communications to Chase Bank. Eventually, in late XXXX, Chase informed XXXX that the funds could not be recovered and suggested that I pursue the matter directly with the unintended recipient. However, they refused to provide any information about this person, citing privacy laws. 

It is deeply troubling that JPMorgan Chase Bank processed a high-value international transfer without verifying whether the account number matched the recipients name. I believe this is a critical failure of banking due diligence and a violation of consumer protection principles. 

Therefore, I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate JPMorgan Chase Banks conduct in this matter, including : Failure to verify the consistency between the account number and account holder name ; Delayed and ineffective response after being notified of the issue ; Refusal to assist in fund recovery or disclose information necessary to pursue legal action. 

This situation has caused me significant financial loss and emotional distress. I sincerely hope the CFPB can assist in holding the bank accountable and help facilitate the return of the lost funds. 

Thank you for your time and attention.

I am filing a complaint regarding a round-trip airline ticket I booked through Chase Travel ( via Chase Ultimate Rewards points ), scheduled for XX/XX/year> on XXXX XXXX  XXXX 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Chase Travel to request a change to only the first leg of the itinerary. I was told that because the ticket was Basic Economy, no changes or cancellations could be made. I was advised to hold onto the roundtrip itinerary, with no mention of further consequences.

What I was not told and what Chase Travel failed to disclose is that skipping the first segment would result in the automatic cancellation of the return flight, per American Airlines ' policy. This is a material consequence of the itinerary and should have been disclosed at the time of my inquiry.

Because Chase Travel did not inform me of this, and actually suggested I retain the roundtrip, I was denied the opportunity to make an informed decision. I could have rebooked entirely or purchased a separate outbound ticket to preserve the return leg.

Chase Travels failure to inform me of this policy despite my clearly stated intent to change only one segment amounts to a deceptive omission, particularly given their role as a financial institution offering travel booking services. I believe this merits investigation for unfair or deceptive practices affecting consumer rewards programs and travel services.

text: I recently opened Chase First Banking accounts for each of my children. I first opened my daughter 's account yesterday and then opened my son 's account today. I was able to fund my daughter 's account with a transfer from my account ; however, I am unable to transfer funds into my son 's account. I have been on the phone with Chase two separate times today. The first call I was only told that their site must be down in some way and to give it some time. The second call I was told by one representative that this was a known issue with Chase First accounts. From there I was transferred to a supervisor who opened a ticket for me and I was told that I can expect to hear from someone in about 2-3 business days. How is this in any way acceptable with financial matters? Further, I have since done some research online and this is indeed a very well-known issue with Chase First accounts. I see posts regarding this same problem dating back over two years! As a federally regulated banking institution, how on earth has the known issue not been resolved in that time frame so that consumers stop having the problem. It sounds as though it's very common to have to call multiple times, be transferred between various departments, and the only way to really resolve the issue is to be lucky enough to get a representative who is not only familiar with it, but who also has the authority to assist in resolving it. I didn't entirely come up with the idea of opening these accounts on my own. As someone who already had existing accounts with Chase, I received communications advertising this as a XXXX XXXX XXXX account for children. It was advertised as being very easy to set up if you already had accounts with Chase. They should not be advertising this as being in any way " easy '' when they have known issues that prevent you from actually transferring money between accounts. Right now I can not fund my son 's account- not via the app or the website. I can transfer funds into my daughter 's account, but only from the website, not the app. From my understanding of the situation based on posts made by others who experienced the same problem, there is an issue with the Transfer Agreement in relation to these accounts and what Chase needs to do is deactivate and then reactivate it in order to reset account transfer functionality. Unfortunately, this is not something I can do on my own- it must be done with customer service assistance from Chase.

text:
To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally request assistance regarding an unresolved matter involving my account with Chase Bank. 
Earlier this month, my Chase online banking account was compromised by fraud. Unauthorized transactions occurred, including the theft and unauthorized redemption of my Chase credit card reward points. Upon investigation, Chase restored the stolen funds from my checking account but has refused to reinstate the stolen credit card reward points. 
These points were earned through legitimate use of my account and represent a contractual benefit. Their unauthorized use was part of the same fraudulent activity that affected my bank funds. Given that Chase acknowledged the breach and returned the stolen money, it is both reasonable and fair to expect that the reward points, equally part of my account value, should be restored as well. 
The total of XXXX points represents approximately $1300.00 in base redemption value, based on Chases standard XXXX point = $0.00 cash equivalent rate. These points were earned through tens of thousands of dollars in legitimate spending. The XXXX points were split across two Chase credit cards, approximately XXXX on one and XXXX on the other, representing years of legitimate use. If redeemed through Chases travel portal or transferred to partners, they could be worth $1800.00 or more. This is not a negligible loss. The refusal to return them after a confirmed account breach leaves me without full restitution. 
The stolen points were fraudulently redeemed in the form of 16 XXXX gift cards sent to my email address without my authorization. I did not request, redeem, or benefit from these gift cards. They were automatically filtered to my spam folder and remain untouched. I do not own any XXXX products, nor have I ever used XXXX gift cards. It is obvious, without a shadow of a doubt, that this redemption was part of the same fraudulent activity that affected the rest of my account. I have retained the emails as evidence and can provide them upon request. 
I reported the fraudulent activity promptly, cooperated fully with Chases investigation, and followed all instructions provided. Despite these efforts, Chase has declined to fully resolve the matter, leaving me with a partial recovery that does not correct the harm done through no fault of my own. 
At this point, I am seeking external assistance, having exhausted internal channels. I respectfully request your help in advocating for the complete restoration of what was taken during the breach. 
I am submitting this request to the following offices : Chase Executive Customer Relations Ohio Attorney General XXXX XXXX Consumer Protection Section Office of my State Representative XXXX XXXX Offices of XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ( OCC ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I am happy to provide further documentation, including case numbers, correspondence with Chase, and evidence of unauthorized activity, upon request. 
Thank you for your time, attention, and assistance in helping resolve this matter fairly. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

In XX/XX/year>, I deposited some checks into my Chase checking account. The checks were reimbursement from my retirement plan provider for overcontributions. Chase 's account system flagged the checks as irregular deposits and put holds on them. I called Chase to try and get the holds cleared. They told me they needed to contact the maker of the checks to clear them. I was told this wasn't a big deal and once the maker cleared the checks, the hold would be lifted, and the checks would be deposited into my account. I called Chase 2 or 3 times to follow up on the status of the checks to see whether they had been cleared.

Chase has a policy where they will close a checking account if they are unable to clear a held check within 10 days. No one from Chase ever told me about this policy when I had called to inquire about the checks. Rather, I logged into my Chase account one day and saw it was empty. I had no idea Chase had closed my checking account. I thought I had been the victim of fraud. I frantically called Chase to try and figure out what was happening. It was only then that I was told that my account had been closed because the checks had not been cleared within 10 days. They told me they were unable to get a hold of the maker of the checks. I called my retirement account provider and got a hold of someone in less than 5 minutes. I was able to put the representative from my retirement account in contact with Chase, and the checks were finally cleared.

However, my account had already been closed, and it took Chase a few days to reopen the account. And after the account was reopened, it took a few days for me to transfer funds from an outside savings account into my Chase checking account. We used that Chase account to autopay our bills. Because the account was closed for a few days and then had $0.00 in funds for a few days, many of those payments didn't go through so we were hit with late fees or returned checks fees. Luckily, most of our creditors waived the late fees and returned check fees. However, it took hours of calls to clear those fees. Also, there was one $40.00 returned check fee from XXXX that XXXX refused to waive. Chase refused to provide any type of reimbursement for that $40.00 fee. 

In the end, I'm very disappointed that no one at Chase ever told me my account would be closed if the held checks weren't cleared within 10 days. I called them several times, and no one told me this. So, I was completely caught off guard when my account was closed. I'm also disappointed Chase didn't do anything to help reimburse me for the $40.00 returned check fee. I think Chase shares some of the blame for it.

I check my CHASE Checking Account daily. Today, XX/XX/year>, I checked my account and discovered that $24000.00 was permitted to be withdrawn from my checking account without my authorization. I never received any fraud alert, etc. from CHASE asking me to approve or decline the transfer. I immediately went to a local CHASE bank whereby I was informed that I had been " hacked '' by individuals in XXXX and XXXX. I demanded an immediate return of the funds whereby CHASE said that they'd need up to 10 days to investigate. This is unacceptable and should have never happened in the first place. I should've, at least, received a call from CHASE before ANY money was transferred, yet alone almost $25000.00.

text:
I am writing this letter to file a formal complaint against Chase Bank for its predatory and unlawful practices. I have been a customer with Chase for several months before opening the business account. On XX/XX/XXXX, I deposited XXXX XXXX Treasury checks into my business account. The receipt said the funds would be available by XX/XX/XXXX. The banker who assisted me showed me how to call the number XXXX to have the funds lifted. I called on XX/XX/XXXX, the agent told me the checks had to be verified by the IRS. 

I called into the provided Chase phone line on XX/XX/XXXX. The agent mentioned there was absolutely nothing wrong with the account, the funds just needed to be verified. The agent said I needed to call the IRS to verify that the funds are not being held on their end. From there, the agent told me to call back with the IRS on the line, and they could verify the funds to get the hold lifted. I called the IRS using the phone number XXXX, which is provided on the XXXX Treasury XXXX provided with the checks. I was able to get an agent from the IRS, and she confirmed that there were no holds or anything on their end that would prevent the bank from releasing the funds. The agent allowed me to call the number provided by Chase to verbally confirm the funds for them. The chase agent got on the line and was extremely agitated that the IRS was on the call. Despite what the previous Chase agent mentioned, he said they had to call the IRS on their end and said the IRS agent on the line wasnt necessary. The IRS agent mentioned that there were no issues on their end with the funds, and this is on XXXX end before exiting the call. The chase agent proceeded to say that the funds werent the problem. The account was restricted because it was a new account, and they were waiting for the back office to lift it. He said they had until XX/XX/XXXX, to release everything, but the funds could be released before then. According to the XXXX Funds Availability Act, under the XXXX Accounts ( XXXX ( a ) ), an account is not considered new if each customer on the account has had, within XXXX calendar days before the account is established, another account at the bank for at least XXXX calendar days. As previously mentioned, I have other accounts with Chase that have been established over 30 days. 

I had a company event scheduled in XXXX predicated on the guarantee that Chase provided that my funds would be released on XX/XX/XXXX. My vendors were lined up, and the event was scheduled to begin on XX/XX/XXXX. Every agent previously mentioned that the funds would be released on XX/XX/XXXX. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, before my workers and I flew out to XXXX, and the guy said everything would be released on XX/XX/XXXX, but I might have to call in to lift the restriction. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, the funds were released into the account. Seeing the funds in my account, I proceeded to create a wire transfer to secure the payment owed to my main vendor. Chase denied my wire and immediately restricted my account again and completely locked me out of the app. At XXXX AM, I went to the branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, FL XXXX. The banker reached out to the same phone number provided. The agent on the line said there was a XXXX wait to reach the IRS, and they told me I needed to get the IRS on XXXX phone and call in with them. The banker told me to try again on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX AM. 

I called the IRS using the phone number XXXX and got an agent in XXXX minutes. I told her the scenario, and she allowed me to call the chase line again. The agent got on the line and reconnected to an escalation XXXX. The agent said they couldnt accept the IRS agent on the phone, and they had to call from their end. He said they had to make sure that the funds were payable to me. He asked the IRS agent for the phone number for them to use to call back in. She provided the number XXXX. The agent called, and I remained on hold for over XXXX minutes before the call dropped. I didnt receive any call back from Chase or that agent. I called the line again, and the previous agent claimed they couldnt reach a live person with the number provided. I provided the phone number XXXX, and the agent said it wasnt a number registered to the IRS. I said the number is on their website. She said their system doesnt go by websites, but it goes by public record. I provided the number XXXX, which the previous agent had. She tried to call and said she couldnt reach a live agent. I requested that she create a three-way call so I could try to reach an agent. She tried twice, but due to the feedback on the phone line, the IRS automated system couldnt hear the responses and hung up the phone. I asked if there was a website or API that they used to verify XXXX Treasury checks. The agent said, No, we need verbal confirmation from the IRS that the funds can be verified and payable to you. She got agitated and rushed me off the phone and said I needed to call the IRS to see how they could get in touch to a live person. 
I called the IRS using the number XXXX and figured out the sequence to get to a live agent. The agent I was speaking to said she didnt understand what else the bank could need to verify the funds. She suggested taking the treasury letters to the bank. Around XXXX PM, I went up to the branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX. XXXX XXXX was able to help me tremendously. XXXX scanned in the XXXX Treasury letters. From there, he called into the back office line to get an agent. That agent received verbal confirmation from the IRS and verified the funds, she verified I was the business owner, she requested the restriction on my account be lifted. This phone conversation took approximately XXXX hours. They said the restriction should be lifted within XXXX minutes, and they will notify me when it is completed. I went back to the branch after an hour, and my account was still restricted, and by this time, nobody wanted to further assist because it was time for the branch to close. They told me to give it overnight to resolve. 

On the morning of XX/XX/XXXX, my account was still restricted. I called into the chase line around XXXX XXXX XXXX, and the supervisor I spoke with said the account reinstatement request was submitted yesterday but the request was denied due to an address change that caused the account address not to match the check address. She was willing to help because she could see in the notes that the address change was required by a banker. She mentioned that they had already verified the legitimacy of the checks. She said she had to verbally verify the funds with the IRS, she asked what the checks were for, and asked other questions that were mentioned the day before to verify the funds. She couldnt get an IRS agent on the line, so she said it might be too early and to call back later. I went into the branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX. I was assisted by XXXX XXXX, and he called the back office and got the agent XXXX. XXXX said the account reinstatement request was submitted yesterday, and everything was verified with the IRS. He mentioned that the account reinstatement was denied but it wasnt simply due to the address on the account. He said the higher office that processes these requests wont accept a verbal confirmation from the IRS ; they want to see documentation. He said it takes XXXX business days for them to receive. The XXXX Treasury letters were uploaded to the system, but they havent been added to the account. They told me to give it XXXX business days to receive the uploads and put in another request to have the account unrestricted. 

According to the Expedited Funds Availability Act, General Rules ( XXXX ( a ) XXXX ( c ) ), XXXX Treasury checks must receive next-day availability. Even for large deposit checks, under the new account exceptions, at least $5500.00 should be released the next day and the XXXX business day for the remaining portion of the deposit. None of the regulations of this act have been followed by Chase Bank when it comes to my account and many others. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a formal complaint with the XXXX office, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, a representative from the XXXX office contacted me to say that they would investigate this issue. On XX/XX/XXXX, the same representative reached out to say that Chase didn't accept XXXX Treasury letters and blamed the IRS for not verifying the funds. Despite getting verbally verified by the IRS in front of a banker and on the recorded line with a Chase back office representative, I'm still being told that the funds aren't verified, even though they have already been fully processed into my account. The representative had no further explanation other than to say they were going to continue to see what they could do. 
This whole ordeal has jeopardized my business partnerships, caused unnecessary mental and emotional distress, lost time, and a financial loss for my company. As I write this letter, the issue is still not resolved, and I continue to get the runaround. Even when my funds are released, I still have to pay vendors, and no work was accomplished because of the unethical practices of Chase Bank. I opened my business in XXXX, I have never had such a horrific experience with a bank since Ive been operating my business. This is a small business, and this has been detrimental to the daily operation of my business. The bank employees I spoke with admitted that this happens all the time, and funds have been held for XXXX or more days. Several employees said it was weird what was happening with my account but they didnt have the power to do anything. Every employee I spoke with, had different instructions for the same processes. The initial hold was meant to verify the funds but nothing was done to ensure that the money for my company was released in a timely fashion. I was never once asked to submit the XXXX Treasury letters at any point in the verification process. 

The system Chase Bank has in place is flawed and jeopardizes the lives of their personal and business customers. A simple XXXX search will show numerous customers who had their accounts locked without receiving their money. There needs to be an investigation into how these accounts are being mishandled and the lack of accountability/urgency in the fund verification process.

text:
XXXX weeks ago ( on XX/XX/XXXX ), we were notified that our XXXX credit cards open with Chase were closed and that we would receive a letter in the mail in XXXX business days containing more information. 

XXXX of our accounts ( Chase Sapphire Reserve ) has been open with Chase for a little over XXXX years ; the other account ( Chase Freedom ) has been open with chase for XXXX years. 

We reached out to Chase immediately after the accounts were closed, and were informed that we could not take action until we received the letter in the mail. The letter arrived last Friday, XX/XX/XXXX ( see copy of letter attached ) and referenced that our accounts were being closed " because of rewards misuse ''. We reached out to Chase 's Complaints and XXXX XXXX, who informed us that the card had in fact been closed due to inappropriate rewards activity, and that the account was also labeled/identified as " An account which is not to be reopened ''. 

When discussing the issue with Chase, we referenced the rewards fraud describer below which occurred during XXXX XXXX ( we identified the fraud in XX/XX/XXXX and reported the issue and activity to Chase ). Chase acknowledged that there are steps that we could take to formally appeal the accounts being closed ( restarting the processes which we had originally undertaken ; i.e. calling the number on the back of the card, submitting an inquiry via our secure message center, or sending a letter to a XXXX XXXX XXXX appeals ). Given that the Chase individual we spoke to today ( XX/XX/XXXX ) advised that the account has been tagged as an account Not to be reopened, we do not intend to re-pursue the issue through the same channels weve already undertaken. 

In XXXX of XXXX, we noticed that our rewards balance within the Chase Rewards Portal had decreased materially from the balance that is typically carried there. For the duration of the past XXXX years weve had these cards open with Chase, XXXX let points accrued during the year and then recoup them when going on family vacations. Upon reviewing the activity within the account, we noticed that points had been being used to purchase XXXX gift cards and were being sent to an email that was setup which mirrored closely the personal email linked to our account ( our email registered on the account is XXXX ; the email that it appears was receiving credit cards was XXXX ). We reported the issue to Chase upon discovering it, which resulted in XXXX receiving a new username/login/security settings/etc. After a couple of weeks or so, Chase refunded us the points that the perpetrator had fraudulently moved to gift cards. 

In light of the fact that we identified the fraud which occurred on our account and reported it to Chase upon discovering it, we are somewhat dumbfounded that the only response weve received as to why the account has been closed is because of rewards misuse. Not only did Chase not have the appropriate controls in place to monitor/detect such activity on the account ( i.e. XXXX factor authentication, review of non-primary new-email linked to gift card redemptions with rewards points, significant point values being used for gift cards, etc. ) but upon our discovery of the issue, their response is to close the account of a XXXX customer with no record of any prior issues. 

Given that Chase did not have the necessary controls in-place and operating to detect the fraud ( i.e. two-factor authentication on the account, alerts/reviews when adding a non-primary email address as the recipient of gift cards/monetary distributions from rewards accounts, automated reviews/alerts of significant gift card rewards redemptions, etc. ), it seems shocking that their response would be to simply close the accounts of a ten-year customer. These XXXX accounts have an average age of XXXX years and a combined credit limit of $100000.00 across them, XXXX data points which greatly affect our XXXX XXXX. 

Had we known at the time of establishing these accounts, that Chase would hold us liable for XXXX instance of fraud occurring on the accounts and wipe out XXXX years of exemplary customer activity and historywe wouldve never put our faith and credit history in their hands. The XXXX reserve card is Chases premium offering, carrying significant annual feesand despite paying those fees and being an extremely loyal customer to XXXX chosen to abandon our relationship and hold XXXX liable for fraud occurring outside of our control, to our detriment.

To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as a formal rebuttal to the response provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank related to extensive fraud claims on my XXXX XXXX XXXX account ending in XXXX. 

Despite Chases claim of having investigated these transactions, their response lacks any verifiable evidence or detailed forensic documentation to support the conclusion that the charges were authorized. Their denial is legally insufficient under multiple statutes and their own marketing assurances. 

I. Chases Findings Contradict Their Own XXXX Liability Policy Chase openly advertises a XXXX Liability guarantee for unauthorized charges, as detailed in their customer agreement and on public marketing materials. Yet, they continue to hold me liable for dozens of transactions I reported as fraud and for which no proof of my participation has ever been provided. Their response fails to reconcile this contradiction. 

XXXX. Legal Violations Committed by Chase 1. Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) : - Chase failed to conduct a proper investigation.

- Chase continues to report the charges as valid without providing receipts, video, or authentication data.

- Chase imposed continued liability on transactions reported within two billing cycles for many caseswell within the statutory dispute window.

2. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693 ) : - My timely disputes limit liability to $50.00 if reported within 60 days.

- Chases refusal to recognize this and repeated denial of fraud disputes constitutes a breach of EFTA protections.

3. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1691 ) : - The closure of my account, particularly after initiating fraud disputes, may constitute retaliation for asserting my rights and violates the ECOA 's adverse action notification requirement.

III. False Claim of Delayed Reporting Chase attempts to evade responsibility by asserting that I 'delayed reporting. ' However : - Fraud was reported multiple times, across different years and cards ( e.g., XXXX, XXXX, XXXX ). 
- Many of the same transactions were previously reversed and later rebilled, demonstrating repeated and confusing handlingnot inaction by me. 
- Chase ignores their duty under the FCBA to re-investigate disputes when new evidence is submitted or prior responses were inadequate. 

IV. Failure to Provide Evidence or Transparent Investigation Chase has : - Refused to supply any forensic documentation, - Failed to produce transaction-level investigation notes, - Relied solely on internal system codes such as 'chip read ' or 'card presented " to deny claims both of which can be simulated via cloning or malware without consumer knowledge.

V. Demands for Immediate Redress I respectfully demand the following : 1. Full removal of all disputed transactions and reversal of associated fees/interest.

2. Restoration of the closed account or a clear, lawful explanation under ECOA.

3. A complete copy of all investigation materials, including : - Video surveillance ( if available ), - Geolocation data, - IP address logs, - Terminal ID and merchant confirmations, - Evidence of card presence validation, - Chain of custody for disputed charges.

4. Credit bureau corrections of any negative marks arising from the unresolved charges.

5. Compensation for interest and late fees on charges I did not authorize.

VI. Summary Chases latest response continues to reflect a systemic failure to honor federally mandated consumer protections. I urge the CFPB and other agencies to take enforcement action, compel documentation, and ensure Chase is held accountable for retaliatory account closure and their disregard of anti-fraud protections. 

I am concurrently working with The XXXX XXXX XXXX to assess federal civil claims. This includes relief under FCBA, EFTA, ECOA, and related statutes. 

Please contact me in writing for any further information.

I have reason to believe Chase is violating the expedited funds availability act. After doing some research and reading through many XXXXXXXX XXXX, it appears Chase is intentionally holding check deposits and not making funds available as outlined in EFAA law. 

Law summarized below : Statutory holds can be placed on almost any deposit ; under this type of hold, the bank must make the first $200.00 of the deposit available on the next business day after the deposit is made, the second $600.00 available on the second business day after the deposit is made, and the rest on the third business day. 

Large deposit holds are placed when the total of deposits made in one business day is more than $5000.00. The availability rules for the first and second business day after the deposit are the same as for a statutory hold, but on the third business day, the bank must make $4800.00 of the deposit available, with any remaining amount made available on the seventh business day after the deposit. 

New account holds are placed on deposits made to accounts that are less than 30 days old. These holds are lifted on the ninth business day after the deposit. 

Exception holds are used for accounts that have been frequently overdrawn, or when banks have reason to suspect that a deposit is legitimate. In rarer cases, they may be used if the bank branch suffers a power outage or a computer system failure. In most cases, however, exception holds are used when an account has been overdrawn for at least six business days out of the six months prior to the deposit, or at least two business days if the account has been overdrawn in an amount more than $5000.00. An exception hold may be placed if the bank suspects that the check is fraudulent or wont clear. It may also be placed on an instrument that has been previously returned for insufficient funds. Exception holds are lifted on the seventh business day after the deposit is made.

Breach of Contract Bank-customer relationship governed by deposit agreement Implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing may have been violated Legal Authority : California Commercial Code 41014505 and case law on depositor-bank relationships C. Bus. & Prof. Code 17200 Unlawful, unfair, or fraudulent business practices Potential claim : Banks process was deceptive or unfair F. Key Evidence to Collect Deposit records and account statements Check copy ( front and back ) showing endorsement Bank communication ( letters, emails, internal notes ) Proof of available funds notice and subsequent reversal Evidence of damages : Denied access to money Missed payments, evictions, fees Medical or psychological records ( if emotional distress is claimed ) 4. However, after sending all the documentation they said at the begining and not receiving a clear response as to why the check delivery process wasn't moving forward, I contacted my lawyer to be properly informed of the process. The bank told me that the check had to be sent directly to XXXX and requested a notarized letter making this request, along with a certified translation and an apostille. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX and they said that Chase had already sent the check to XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again to request the check tracking number because it had not yet arrived in XXXX, but I did not have good reception and I wrote down the number wrong and I could not track it. 
Even so, they told me to wait untilthe end of XXXX, which was the maximum shipping time. 
However, since the check hadn't arrived, I called again on XX/XX/XXXX and got the tracking number. When I tracked the package, I realized it had been in customs for over XXXX weeks, so neither XXXX nor Chase informed me that they required additional information from customs to release the shipment. I contacted XXXX, and after providing the requested information, they sent the check to my home address. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, the check arrived at my home address, and I realized my last name was misspelled. Both on the XXXX package label and in the letter from the bank, it said " XXXX, '' which should be XXXX. So on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX, I called the bank to inform them of the error they had made and that I couldn't cash this check. They told me to call back in XXXX days for a solution. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, and they told me the process involved requesting the forms for a new check, so I made this request over the phone. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, and they told me everything was in order but it was still being processed. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, and they told me the forms had been sent and everything was in order, that I should wait. I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, saying I still didn't know anything about the process. They informed me that I should wait for the forms, sign them, and return them by mail again. I mentioned that I was not happy with paying for the forms shipping to United States if it had been the bank 's mistake. The supervisor, XXXX, said there was no other solution and that they couldn't give me a tracking number. She didn't even tell me which shipping company had sentmethe documents, so I can't confirm whether they sent me the forms or not. 
I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, and they told me they didn't have a tracking number or any way to track the forms. They told me to wait until the end of the month, and if they still hadn't arrived, to call Chase again to see what they could do. 
I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, and they again told me they had no way to track these documents ; I could only request the forms again and wait for them to arrive this time.

I don't understand why they won't give me information to track the forms, since sometimes parcel carriers require additional information to release the packages. Otherwise, they can remain in warehouses for weeks, as happened with the check.

text:
Regarding Chase Bank 's response dated [ XX/XX/XXXX ] to CFPB Case Number [ XXXX ] The response to Chase 's XXXX is as follows : Chase 's justification for seizing the New York XXXX XXXX XXXX is disputed. While the XXXX Account XXXX is referenced, it should be noted that state law supersedes the agreement 's terms. 
Chase 's characterization of the tax refund as a " voluntary payment '' due to the authorized ACH setup is inaccurate. Authorization of direct deposits does not equate to authorization to seize a state tax refund to cover a charged-off debt, especially when these funds are protected by New York XXXX XXXX XXXX 
Chase 's mention of bringing the account to zero for systematic charge-off does not justify seizing funds exempt from collection under state law. 
Furthermore, Chase 's claim of being " not able to remove the credit and issue you a refund '' is unacceptable. If funds were improperly taken, there is a legal obligation to return them. 
Chase 's reliance on the XXXX Account XXXX is misplaced. The deposit agreement copy I was given when I open a chase secure checking account in XXXX mentions the use of deposits for overdrafts and setoff rights ( XXXX XXXX  ). However, the " Rules Governing Your Account '' on page XXXX states : This agreement, all accounts and services provided to you, and any dispute relating to those accounts and services are governed by federal law and, when not superseded by federal law, the law of the state where your account is located. '' Since the account is in New York, New York XXXX law applies. New York 's Exempt Income Protection Act ( EIPA ) protects certain income types, including state tax refunds, from XXXX or freezing by creditors like Chase. This protection overrides the deposit agreement 's terms, particularly concerning legally protected funds. 
Chase 's action of taking the New York XXXX tax refund to cover a charged-off debt, despite XXXX protections, violates consumer rights. Applying funds to a charged-off balance is a form of debt collection and is subject to state laws. 
It is maintained that Chase 's actions were unlawful, and the New York XXXX tax refund should be returned. The CFPB is requested to investigate further and compel Chase to return the seized funds.

We discovered that on XX/XX/XXXX, JPMorgan Chase Bank placed our company on the XXXX XXXX  list under Reason Code 14 : Identity Theft. We reached out to XXXX at XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX and then XXXX replied back the same day on XX/XX/XXXX given the detailed reason for Reaso Code 14 : Identity Theft. XXXX stated the reason for being placed on the XXXX by JP Morgan Chase Bank was, " We located a business that could be considered a match ... owners can check with other processors that may be able to authenticate their identity and are okay onboarding their merchant account. ( see attached document with email from XXXX XXXX ) '' According to XXXX 's response JP Morgan Chase Bank placed us on the XXXX  because they believe someone else other than XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX signed up for the merchant service with JP Morgan Chase Bank on their behalf. This designation is completely false and has caused immediate and severe disruption to our business operations and reputation. It also will cause our other merchant service company to terminate our account with us, as JP Morgan Chase Bank did, thus enabling us from further processing credit cards as a company as a whole. This will severly damage our business and staff. 

This violates : UDAAP ( DoddFrank Act 12 U.S.C.5531 & 5536 ) 12 U.S.C . 5531 ( a ) The Bureau may take any action to prevent a covered person from committing or engaging in an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice in connection with any transaction with a consumer for a consumer financial product or service.

12 U.S.C. 5536 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) It shall be unlawful for any covered person to engage in any unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice.

Why this applies to Chase : By placing your business on XXXX  under a false identity theft claim, without evidence, and refusing to respond to your requests, Chase may have : - Misrepresented a material fact - Deprived you of due process or transparency - Caused actual financial harm ( inability to process transactions, loss of reputation ) This aligns with UDAAPs legal tests : - Unfair : caused substantial injury - Deceptive : misleading or false claims - Abusive : taking unreasonable advantage of your lack of power or knowledge 2 ) Deceptive Practices under FTC Act 5 ( 15 U.S.C. 45 ) Though banks fall under CFPB oversight, they may also face scrutiny under Section5 of the FTC Act, which prohibits : unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce Assigning a false identity theft designation without basis or notification is : - Potentially deceptive, misrepresenting the facts - Likely unfair, because it harms your business and may not be avoidable by you Moreover, Section 5 ( n ) defines an unfair practice as one that : causes or is likely to cause substantial injury to consumers not reasonably avoidable by consumers themselves. 

When we onboarded with Chase Merchant Services, we submitted and signed a full merchant services application. This included our verified Social Security Numbers, our EIN, and all supporting documentation for XXXX XXXX XXXX. We are providing you with proof that we are indeed XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX and that we intended on signing up with JP Morgan Chase Bank for merchant services ( see proof of Identificaion, picture of us holding our identification, Chase Merchant Service Contract with our names and signatures which shows our intention to sign up with JP Morgan Chase Bank Merchant Services, both Owner 's Passports and the XXXX Email we received on XX/XX/XXXX ). Both authorized business owners XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX provided government-issued identification. Chase approved our account, confirming that both our identity and our business were legitimate. 

Communication with JP Morgan Chase Bank On XX/XX/XXXX, we formally contacted Chases XXXX  Inquiry Team ( Case ID : XXXX ) and requested : A full explanation of the XXXX listing and reason code, along with any documentation used to support the identity theft claim as well as the origin of the claim ( e.g., a customer complaint, verification error, or third party ) We also requested guidance on how to remove our company from the list, and the opportunity to provide counter-documentation. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, Chase responded with a single sentence : Your merchant account name XXXX XXXX XXXX with merchant ID # XXXX was added to XXXX  due to Identity Theft. The decision was final and we are unable to process for XXXX  removal. 

We immediately replied that same day, formally disputing the listing and requesting a proper review of the case. We stated that the decision lacked transparency, due process, and supporting documentation. We also requested a full response within 10 business days, which we feel was more than fair. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, we sent a final reminder to the XXXX Inquiry Team, noting the continued silence from Chase and giving them a deadline of XX/XX/XXXX, before we escalated the matter to the CFPB. 

As of XX/XX/XXXX, we have not received any response from Chase since XX/XX/XXXX. 

We are requesting that Chase Merchant Services remove our business from the XXXX  list immediately. Any failure to comply will result in XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX to take further legal action for damages and losses. We also request a formal investigation into JPMorgan Chases negligent handling of this matter, particularly their unwillingness to provide documentation or respond to multiple professional and reasonable requests. This lack of response to a matter so critical to our operations has caused significant financial harm and operational disruption. This is a time-sensitive situation, and we urge immediate action.

On XX/XX/year>, JPMorgan Chase said that one of my accounts is past due. However, I confirmed with customer service that the account is current. 

Additionally I sent a check on XX/XX/XXXX from XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX notified me that the check has not been deposited.

JPMorgan Chase Bank filed a lawsuit against me in XXXX XXXX, Florida ( Case # XXXX ) and obtained a final judgment for $5500.00. 

My credit report shows the account was charged off and closed in XX/XX/XXXX as a profit and loss write-off. This usually indicates the account was sold or transferred to a third party, which would mean JPMorgan Chase no longer had legal standing to collect or sue on the debt. 

Despite this, Chase proceeded with the lawsuit through their attorneys ( XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ), resulting in a judgment. This appears to be a false representation of ownership and legal authority, which may violate the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), specifically : 15 U.S.C. 1692e Prohibits the use of any false, deceptive, or misleading representation in connection with the collection of any debt.

1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) Specifically forbids misrepresenting the character, amount, or legal status of any debt.

1692e ( 10 ) Bans using any false representation or deceptive means to collect or attempt to collect a debt.

Suing a consumer on a debt you no longer legally own qualifies as a misrepresentation of the legal status of that debt which courts have ruled to be a direct violation of these FDCPA provisions.

Additionally, I signed a settlement stipulation under emotional stress, without counsel, and without a full understanding of my legal rights or the fact that I could dispute ownership and demand validation of the debt.

I also submitted a written response to the court through the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal on XX/XX/XXXX, objecting to the claim and asking to be heard. However, the court issued a Final Judgment on XX/XX/XXXX, without acknowledging my filing or giving me a fair hearing which amounts to a denial of due process.

I respectfully request the CFPB investigate whether JPMorgan Chase : Misrepresented their legal right to collect on or sue for this debt Violated FDCPA protections by suing on a debt they may have sold Failed to properly validate ownership before taking legal action Denied me the ability to fairly dispute or respond to the claim in court I have attached screenshots of my credit report showing the charge-off and account closure as supporting evidence.

Before Chase acquired XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, I was a long-time client of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX My accounts had terms that included no monthly fees and no minimum balance requirements. When my accounts were transferred to XXXX, those same terms were honored and remained unchanged for over a decade. 

However, without my knowledge or consent, Chase changed my account types between XXXX and XXXX of XXXX, transitioning my savings account into a checking account which carries monthly fees while keeping my original checking account neither of which earns interest. This change was never clearly communicated to me, and as a result, I was charged over $880.00 in fees over the years. These fees were incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic, a time when I was unemployed and financially vulnerable. 

Despite the drastic change in account terms and the financial burden it placed on me, I received no direct notice or documentation from Chase that this change would occur or had occurred. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXX XXXX., I visited the XXXX XXXX branch and spoke with a representative named XXXX. He reviewed my account history and acknowledged the issue. XXXX was able to secure a refund for 5 months worth of fees. 

Later, on Wednesday, XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXXXXXX XXXX., I called Chase customer service. I initially spoke with a representative named XXXX, who then transferred me to XXXX. XXXX added an additional 12 months of compensation, but he was dismissive and made no effort to address the core issuethat my account was changed without my knowledge or consent. When I requested documentation showing proof of any notice for the change, XXXX told me to go get it at the branch instead of offering to provide it through any formal or accessible channel. I asked to speak with a manager but was refused a proper escalation path. 

To date, I have not received adequate answers, compensation, or restoration of my original account terms. I believe this change was deceptive, unauthorized, and financially damaging, especially considering my long-standing relationship and history with these accounts. 

I request that Chase restore the original account terms, reimburse any fees charged as a result of this unauthorized change, and provide a full investigation and written explanation for the account modifications.

Date : XX/XX/year> Subject : Formal Complaint Chase Bank Wrongful Dishonor of Negotiable Instrument I am filing a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding its failure to honor a valid negotiable instrument in the amount of $81000.00, in violation of the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) and its own Deposit Account Agreement ( DAA ). On XX/XX/year>, I deposited a check into my Chase account for $81000.00. Chase failed to honor or return the check in accordance with UCC requirements and did not notify me of dishonor within the timeframe mandated by law. As a result, I suffered financial harm and am requesting relief through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. 
Under UCC 4-301, Chase, as the payor bank, was required to either pay or return the check by midnight of the next banking day after receiving it. Chase failed to return the item within that required deadline and did not issue timely notice of dishonor, in violation of both UCC 4-301 and 3-502 ( b ). Furthermore, Chase 's conduct constitutes wrongful dishonor under UCC 4-402, which holds the bank strictly liable for failure to pay a properly payable item. To date, Chase has neither returned the check nor provided a sufficient explanation, creating legal liability under commercial banking law. 
Additionally, Chase violated its own Deposit Account Agreement, which governs its obligation to process customer deposits. Nowhere in the DAA does Chase reserve the right to refuse valid negotiable instruments without formal return or notice. The agreement explicitly obligates Chase to act in good faith and in accordance with applicable banking law. By refusing to process or properly reject the item in accordance with UCC and the DAA, Chase is in breach of contract and has failed to perform in a commercially reasonable manner as required under UCC 1-304. 
As a result of this misconduct, I experienced significant financial disruption, including loss of access to over $81000.00, potential delays in related payments, and reputational damage. Chases failure to follow basic banking and legal standards places consumers at risk and violates both federal and state commercial law. I am therefore requesting the following relief : Immediate crediting of the $81000.00 to my account ; Reimbursement of any losses, fees, or penalties incurred due to Chases failure to process the check ; A written explanation from Chase regarding the basis of the dishonor or inaction ; Verification that this conduct does not affect my credit reporting ; Enforcement action or oversight by the CFPB to ensure Chase complies with its contractual and legal obligations. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text:
On XX/XX/year> I received a call with caller ID JPMorgan Chase XXXX XXXX EST and answered, had someone introduce to me as a manager. I thought it was strange since my account is not new and asked if there was any issues with my account which it did not, said there are too many scams and I can't talk and hung up. Caller ID was a bit weird too with JPMorgan together with no space, usually would say Chase Banking or something else, when I looked up on XXXX, it did not come up as Chase. 

I called Chase banking later XXXX at XXXX and the call asked for last 4 of social then immediately jumped to VOICE ID which I never heard of before today. It did not give me an option to opt out or skip, asked me to speak a sentence to start. I did not say a word. I just pressed * to skip. I had hard time reaching CSR and had an appointment so called back at XXXX. 

When I spoke with CSR to ask the call I received was from Chase and gave the phone #, her English was not very good and she could not even repeat phone # back to me properly. I had to repeat phone # few times, then she said she does not know if it's from Chase or not. I asked her to put me on hold to check which she did, then told me it was indeed Chase. I asked her what the call was for and she could not say but said the person left me a voicemail. I then told her I do not wish to have Voice ID and want to make sure it's noted I do not ever want to turn it on. She responded by saying it's ACTIVE and she'd turn it off. I asked her why would it be active since I never activated it and I have no one else on my account, she could not answer. I asked why and how it was active and when it was active. She was not able to answer any of that and when asked to transfer to supervisor, she also barely spoke English and when asked to transfer to fraud they were failing to understand basic requests to transfer. 

I went to Chase branch myself physically then asked to speak with someone in Fraud Department for internal controls. The young gentleman was also unable to answer even after speaking with " back office '' why, how, and when VOICE ID was turned on. I explained I am single, no one else has access to my phone, Internet, home, nor my account. And he also had no idea what this Voice ID was I called Chase in front of him to show him on speaker. 

I asked him to check the number I received call from and he said it was NOT Chase phone #. 

I told him it does not seem legal for Chase to not have bypass function and activate VoiceID when I never read the sentence nor spoke a word, and their records do not indicate anywhere when how or where it was activated which means their internal record keeping or technology system is broken. 

I also let him know this seems internal, it seems that scammer pretending to be Chase manager and people working with this all work together and that I used to do Internal Audit and I have license of ACAMS ( Anti Money Laundering Certificate ). 

With all of the state above, I feel bank is in violation and I also found later today upon research this scam with this number has gone on for few years and people have reported to Chase ( it even has Chase sounding background music and all ) and Chase have not done anything to stop it. You can look up by searching on google with # provided above. 

The fact scammers can call with false Chase ID for years and not get caught, the fact bank just somehow activates voice ID for customers without any actual recordings or consent and have no records of, create a whole way of internal and external fraud. 
I have also filed a shorter version of this report with FTC and ask you to take this very seriously. Scammers and voice phishing work quickly and meticulously, and are on the rise and without bank even caring about these situations for years and not having any records or answers, not only customers are not protected, they are in violation of XXXX  and XXXX XXXX XXXX.

I have been doing banking with XXXX XXXX for four years now. I recently got engaged, and my fiance has been a member at Chase Bank for a while. We decided to open a credit card, and a joint checking account at Chase, to set ourselves up financially and use the credit card for our mutual wedding expenses. On XX/XX/year>, I opened a XXXX XXXX credit card with chase bank and got approved for $9300.00 total credit limit because of my excellent credit history. On XX/XX/year>, I had an appointment with a banker, and was able to open a joint checking account for my fiance, XXXX XXXX, and myself, XXXX XXXX My fiance was supposed to come in later and just confirm his identity for the joint account within 30 days since the account was opened. 
Later that day, I wanted to set a money transfer from my XXXX XXXX XXXX, to my new Chase Checking account, because I wanted to have some money on my new account. So on XX/XX/year>, at XXXX, I received an email that my transfer was cancelled, where I saw that I made a mistake and chose the " from '' option- as my new checking account at Chase, and my " to '' option- as my XXXX XXXX checking account . Of course, it was a human mistake. My new chase account had $0.00 on it at the time. Chase Bank understandably considered it a fraudulent activity, and as soon as I got an email to call them and confirm that it was not fraud, I did so and stayed on the phone with Chase customer service for hours. Being transferred from one representative to another for extensive amount of time, I finally got instructed to call back next day, during the working hours of the Resolutions Department. So, on the morning of XX/XX/year>, I called Chase customer service line to reach the Resolutions Department. Being on the phone for an hour, I finally reached the supervisor called XXXX, who helped me unlock the account, stating that " we clearly understand you are not a wrongdoer, and it was just a human mistake ''. I thought this story was over, and communicated with my fiance that he can still go to a branch on Monday the XXXX, and confirm his identity for us to set up the account. 
Also, I think it is important to note, due to the fact that it was a weekend ( XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  ), I could not go to the bank to deposit money to my account. Due to the fact that no physical card had come to my address just yet, I also could not use the ATM to do so. 
On Monday XX/XX/year>, at XXXX XXXX, I received and email to contact Chase Bank again because my checking account got restricted. I immediately called the customer service line, and was told that Chase Bank is permanently ending their relationship with me without any explanation. That day, I decided to go to the bank next morning to meet with a banker and provide the printouts of all the emails and needed information to support my claim of innocence. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX, my fiance and I were at the Chase Bank branch to speak with a banker. We got helped by a banker named XXXX, and she got on the phone with a bank to clarify the situation for us. XXXX was also denied clarity. She said that it was their final decision since the bank " pick and chooses '' their customers sometimes. The lack of any clear explanation from Chase Bank regarding their decision to permanently terminate my account is deeply concerning, as it denies me the opportunity to address what was clearly an honest mistake. This is especially severe considering my strong financial track record, including consistent payments, a stable income, and a credit score that has remained above XXXX. I find it really hard to accept that responsible customers like myself can be treated this way. With no transparency, no clear communication, and no real opportunity to fix what was simply a human error. I didnt procrastinate or ignore the issue. I acted right away, spent hours on the phone, and followed every instruction given to me. What makes this even more disappointing is that my fianc and I had serious plans for this account. We were going to use it for our wedding expenses and future budgeting. With his long-standing relationship with Chase, and my perfect financial record, we genuinely felt confident and secure opening a joint account together. 
Thats why Im reaching out to the CFPB. I truly believe this situation deserves to be reviewed. Ive done everything in good faith, followed every step I was told to take, and still ended up being shut out without a fair explanation. Im hoping that CFPB can look into this and help bring clarity, accountability, and hopefully a resolution. Im not asking for special treatment just a chance to be heard, understood, and treated fairly. Thank you.

text:
To Whom It May Concern at the CFPB:
I am filing this complaint regarding an extensive and ongoing fraud case involving my business debit card with Chase Bank, and what I believe to be a serious failure in Chases fraud prevention, digital wallet tokenization practices, and complaint handling.
Summary of Fraud:
Over a period of nearly two years, a total of XXXX XXXXn unauthorized purchases were made from my Chase business checking account using a debit card that had previously been reissued. The fraudulent charges includeXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXMiscellaneous other charges: XXXX discovered the fraud in XXXX XXXX  after conducting a full account reconciliation.
Chases Findings and Refusal to Reimburse:
Upon contacting Chases claims department, I was told:
The charges were made using an older debit card number that had been reissued two years ago.

However, the original card remained active in a digital wallet, which Chase failed to deactivate.

New fraudulent charges were made using a newly issued card, which should have raised additional red flags.

Despite this, Chase has:
Only agreed to reimburse two charges (a small portion of the total fraud).

Refused to file claims with merchants like Amazon or Instacart (despite the fact that those companies offered to cooperate for up to 24 months if Chase made the request).

Claimed that because this is a business account, I am not protected under the same fraud protections as a consumer.

My Concerns:
Chase failed to fully deactivate the reissued debit card from digital wallets (XXXX XXXX XXXX allowing a bad actor to continue transacting even after the physical card was replaced.

Chase has shown an unwillingness to properly investigate the fraud and recover funds through merchant cooperation.

I was never informed that reissued card tokens would remain active in my wallet  this is a significant risk that Chase failed to disclose.

They are holding me responsible for unauthorized charges made after I reported the fraud, including on a new card.

Actions Taken:
Filed a police report (Report #: XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX  and other vendors, all of whom were willing to provide data to Chase if contacted directly.

Documented all charges and communications with Chase.

This experience has left me with significant financial loss and no meaningful path to recover the funds, despite my timely and comprehensive efforts to alert Chase and provide documentation. I believe their handling of digital wallet security and customer fraud claims needs regulatory scrutiny, especially where business accounts are involved.
I respectfully ask the CFPB to investigate this matter and intervene as needed to ensure fair resolution and broader compliance from Chase Bank regarding debit card fraud and mobile wallet security practices.
Thank you for your attention and support.
Sincerely,XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

text:
While visiting XXXX on XX/XX/year>, I was approached by a very friendly local who offered us a discounted tuk tuk ride to see local attractions. During the ride, we were taken to multiple tourist stops where other friendly locals engaged us in casual conversations about tailoring and suits all leading us to a tailor shop called XXXX XXXX. 

At this shop, the staff offered us beers and immediately began showing us high-end cashmere fabrics and measuring us. The environment was high-pressure and well-rehearsed. I was told Id receive custom 100 % cashmere suits of excellent quality. I paid two charges via XXXX XXXX on my Chase card : one for $460.00 and another for $61.00. It was only afterward that I researched and discovered this entire experience is a common tourist scam in XXXX involving coordinated pressure from tuk tuk drivers and local guides. 

I immediately contacted Chase and explained the situation that while I had authorized the charge, the product I would receive was clearly misrepresented and deceptive. Chase opened a claim and refunded me after two weeks. At that point, I believed the matter was resolved. 

One week after the refund, I received the suit. It was clearly not 100 % cashmere it felt cheap and synthetic, didnt fit properly, and was overall terrible quality. Because I thought the case was closed, I told my mom to get rid of it ( donated or thrown out ). 

Then, about a month after the original refund, the full amount was re-added to my card. I called Chase and was told the transaction was authorized so it didnt qualify for further dispute. I explained again that I never claimed the charge was unauthorized my issue was fraudulent misrepresentation and defective merchandise.

Im asking the CFPB to review this under the proper framework : goods not as described or merchant misrepresentation, which are covered under Visas dispute rules ( Reason Code 13.3/13.5 ) and the Fair Credit Billing Act. Chases refusal to apply those standards and only judge the dispute based on XXXX XXXX authorization is unfair and inaccurate.

Chase allowed an escrow shortage to compound silently for 7 months, then dropped a dramatic increase on me all at once. 

I feel this was a misleading and predatory handling of escrow.

I called the provided number in the notice and learned the problem was the $9000.00 check I recently deposited from a family member. This check was drawn from their account at Chase Bank, the same bank this complaint is directed to, and therefore, I believe Chase should have had all the necessary information to verify the funds or reject the check. On the call, the agent demanded I provide a phone number of this family member, to which I did. However, the agent claimed that the phone number could not be verified ( this phone number was also the phone number on my family member 's Chase account ). I provided another valid phone number for the same family member, but it also could not be verified. Despite multiple attempts with different agents, the phone numbers were consistently deemed unverifiable. I attempted this process a few more times with other agents in the following days, to no success. I also visited a Chase branch, with no success. I was repeatedly told that verifying the phone number was the only way to restrict my account. Later that I learned that Chase was using a third-party data broker to " verify '' phone numbers. It appears that this data broker did not list my family member as the owner of these phone numbers. 

[ 3 ] Throughout the process, Chase agents gave me many excuses regarding why my family member 's number was unable to be verified, such as them purchasing SIM cards from strangers. text:
In XXXX, I was the victim of wire fraud that could have been prevented had JPMorgan Chase Bank followed basic verification procedures. The transaction was related to the purchase of residential land in Florida. I selected a property that was offered by a XXXX XXXX real estate agent and initiated a wire transfer of $18000.00 from my company to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Florida. However, a scammer intercepted the communication by impersonating the title company through a spoofed email domain ( .corn instead of .com ). I was deceived into wiring the funds to the scammers personal account at JPMorgan Chase, which he had linked to the fraudulent instructions while using the correct beneficiarys name, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Despite the mismatch between the account holder name and the intended beneficiary name, JPMorgan Chase Bank still credited the funds to the scammers account. The bank later confirmed that the account holder name did not match the listed beneficiary which is a clear violation of standard wire transfer verification practices and UCC 4A-207. 

I reported the fraud to JPMorgan Chase Bank, and they acknowledged the discrepancy. However, they did not reverse the transaction or issue a refund. I contacted JPMorgans call center and spoke to a representative named XXXX, who confirmed that if a mismatch occurred between the beneficiarys name and account number, the funds would not be credited and would be refunded to the sender within 14 days. Unfortunately, I did not receive my money back. 

As a result, at that time I hired a dedicated attorney who followed up on the case until it was escalated to the local police. The police conducted their own investigation and sent a formal letter to JPMorgan Chase requesting clarification. JPMorgan replied with a letter stating that they needed additional time to investigate and would respond. Since then, they have not followed up neither with the police department, my attorney, nor with me. 

I am currently in the United States on a temporary visit, which has allowed me to reopen this matter with the seriousness it deserves. At the time of the fraud in XXXX, I was living XXXX  and had limited access to legal remedies in the U.S. I am now prepared to pursue all available legal and regulatory channels to seek redress and recover my funds. Based on this, I sent a formal letter to JPMorgan Chase Banks Wire Investigations Department, explaining the situation and requesting a refund. I gave them two weeks to respond or issue the refund. At the end of that period, I received a single phone call from the Executive Office, specifically from XXXX XXXX, who acknowledged the issue but refused to provide a resolution timeline. He gave me his contact number : XXXX, XXXX. XXXX. I waited an additional week without receiving any further communication. I called the number multiple times and left voicemails but never received a response. I then sent another letter and gave them an additional week again, without receiving any reply, feedback, or resolution. 

If no resolution is reached through your agency, I am prepared to pursue legal action based on JPMorgan Chases failure to apply standard wire verification safeguards. I am attaching all relevant documentation in support of my claim.

text:
Several months ago, I used Chase Rewards points to book a travel experience though their redemption portal. 

The experience was publicized as an XXXX XXXX for XXXX + lunch scheduled for XXXX. All was fine until the day of the experience. The tour group reached out the day prior to confirm the details -- all of which were consistent with what was advertised. 

The issue and reason for the complaint is that the experience ended up being very different. We were away from our resort for nearly XXXX hours, vs. the XXXX we were told it would be. We were not fed until dinner, which was very different than being told we would be fed lunch. 

And, the reason for the complaint is that Chase would do nothing to refund/partially refund us for this. They pointed fingers to different departments giving us the runaround on who to address it with. There was almost no follow-up -- when there was it was generic without any resolution or specific direction on who to contact. When asking to close the card associated with the issue, we were told they would address and provide points to compensate, and then that wouldn't happen. And, when we would follow-up to ask they would say there's nothing they can do. 

How is it acceptable for a company to sell a product that when paid for, and the service is not delivered as advertised, that they are not refunding customers? And, it taking me SEVEN different attempts to navigate their different departments to be given a nothing as a refund, even when they've said they would when trying to avoid me closing an account, is unacceptable. There should be * some * accountability for big companies who exercise this level of bureaucracy as a form of a deterrent.
