text:
I am filing this complaint regarding my recent application on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX for the Chase Freedom Unlimited credit card. Despite my strong financial qualifications, I was denied, and the reasons given reflect opaque internal policies that were not disclosed before applying. 

I am a veteran with 13 years of military service and hold a 100 % permanent and total XXXX rating. After leaving the military two years ago, I have worked hard to build my financial stability. My income has grown significantly. I now earn approximately quadruple what my annual income was during my military service. My credit scores are excellent : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I maintain less than 5 % utilization on my existing $87000.00 in credit lines. 

I applied for the Chase Freedom Unlimited card because of its 0 % introductory APR, intending to responsibly manage unplanned family expenses related to the recent passing of my father. To my surprise, I was denied, not due to my creditworthiness, but because of Chases 5/24 rule ( an internal policy that automatically denies applicants with 5+ new accounts in the past 24 months, regardless of financial strength ) and recent credit inquiries. The representative explicitly confirmed these were the reasons. 

My concerns are as follows : 1. Lack of Transparency : At no point during the application process was I warned that my application would be automatically denied due to this internal policy. Had I been aware, I would not have applied.

2. Hard Inquiry Penalty : The denial still resulted in a hard credit inquiry, which negatively impacts my credit score, despite Chase knowing in advance they would not approve the application due to this rigid policy.

3. Failure to Consider Full Profile : The bank did not provide a manual review option or allow reallocation of existing Chase credit lines ( I am already a Chase Sapphire Reserve cardholder in good standing ).

4. Punitive to Responsible Borrowers : I feel I am being punished for responsibly opening and managing credit cards as part of building my credit profile, despite maintaining extremely low utilization and excellent payment history. 
5. Disproportionate Impact on Veterans : As a XXXX veteran, I feel this rigid policy, coupled with the lack of transparency, unfairly limits my access to responsible credit management tools. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB review this matter to ensure : Chase provides clear disclosures upfront about internal policies ( like the 5/24 rule ) that automatically disqualify applicants, Consumers are not penalized with unnecessary hard inquiries when denials are predetermined by rigid criteria, Consideration is given for manual review when an applicant demonstrates strong financial standing and responsible credit use, especially in cases involving veterans managing hardship. 

This experience has left me frustrated and disadvantaged at a time when I most needed flexibility to manage my familys finances. I believe greater transparency and fairness in the process are warranted.

After confirming with XXXX that the vast majority of these charges were not connected to any account in my name, I realized they were fraudulent transactions dating back over two years. 

That same day, I contacted Chase to report the fraud and closed the compromised account at my local branch. Initially, Chase provided a provisional credit for XXXX of these charges, totaling $3900.00 Crucially, this initial credit did not include any of the charges that were within the 60-day window demonstrating 1 ). The bank 's initial ability to reverse older transactions 2 ). The lack of systematic handling of these chargebacks. I was told the process of being reimbursed for the remaining fraudulent charges would begin shortly. 

However, since that initial action, Chase has systematically failed to resolve this issue. Their handling of my claim has been defined by gross negligence and contradictory communication, prompting this formal complaint. My un-reimbursed losses from this fraud total $17000.00.

Chase 's failures can be summarized in four key areas : 1. Grossly Inconsistent and Misleading Communication : I have been given at least four different and conflicting dispute windows by Chase personnel. I was told verbally by one representative that the window was two years ; a branch employee said it was from the beginning of XXXX ; a formal letter incorrectly cited a 30-day " Business Account '' policy for my consumer account ; and finally, a phone representative insisted on a strict 60-day rule. When I called the number on the denial letter to ask for clarification, the representative was evasive, ignored my direct questions, and then deflected by stating the issue was under a " legal investigation '' before telling me to go back to my local branch. 

2. Incorrect Application of Rules & Reversal of a Valid Credit : After initially crediting my account for charges beyond the 60-day mark, Chase later clawed back the credit for those same charges, citing the 60-day rule they had just ignored. They also failed to chargeback the charges within 60 days. This action is illogical and deeply concerning. If the 60-day policy were absolute, the system should not have allowed the initial reversal. The system should have also picked up the charges within 60 days. By taking back this credit, Chase effectively returned properly recovered funds to the fraudster and failed to reimburse me for the charges within its stated policy.

3. Failure to Detect Obvious, Long-Term Fraud : The fraudulent charges were not random- they were a clear pattern of multiple, similarly-described debits occurring nearly every month. The repeating nature, frequency, and descriptions of these debits constitute an obvious pattern of fraud that any reasonable fraud detection system should have flagged long ago. text:
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/2025 Subject : Formal Complaint Against JPMorgan Chase Bank for Unexplained Closure of Personal Checking Account XXXX XXXX Customer Dear [ CFPB/OCC ] Complaint Review Team, I am filing this formal complaint regarding the unexplained closure of my personal checking account ( number XXXX ) by JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . on XX/XX/2025, without prior notice or explanation. This closure has significantly disrupted my personal finances, and I seek your assistance in investigating and resolving this matter. 
As a Chase customer for almost XXXX  years, with no prior issues, overdrafts, fraud reports, or policy violations, I am unclear why my account was closed. I reside at the same address as my father, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ), whose personal and business accounts were similarly closed but reopened after his appeals to Chases executive office ( Case ID XXXX ) and complaints to your agencies. I have worked in law enforcement for the last XXXX  years. The lack of notice or explanation for my account closure may violate federal regulations requiring banks to disclose reasons for adverse actions. 
I respectfully request : Investigation of Chases actions for potential violations of consumer protection laws. 
Reinstatement of my personal checking account ( XXXX ). 
A written explanation for the closure, including steps to prevent future issues. 

Attached are relevant documents, including any account statements ( if available ) and correspondence with Chase. Due to the closure, I may be unable to access recent statements, but I can provide additional information as needed. Please contact me at XXXX or XXXX. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Rebuttal to JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . CFPB Complaint ID : XXXX Chase Reference Number : XXXX To Whom It May Concern : I am writing to formally rebut the wholly insufficient and legally deficient response provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . ( Chase ) to the above-referenced complaint. While Chases letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Ref : XXXX ), makes partial admissions of their errors, it simultaneously denies any legal violation, demonstrating a fundamental disregard for their obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and a failure to conduct a reasonable investigation.

My request is straightforward : due to Chases admitted history of pervasive and willfully inaccurate reporting, the only remedy that can correct this years-long violation is the permanent deletion of this account from all credit reporting agencies ( CRAs ). The following points outline the basis for this demand : 1. Admission of Willful FCRA Violations ( 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ( a ) ) Chases response admits they have been furnishing inaccurate information for nearly five years, stating : Weve sent the updated information to the agencies for their records. The account should show : Updated XXXX  with closure date XX/XX/XXXX ; Updated XXXX  with closure date XX/XX/XXXX ; Updated XXXX to accurately reflect payment history. This is not a courtesy correction ; it is an admission of a clear violation of the FCRA, which mandates furnishers report complete and accurate information. The inaccuracies concerning the closure date and payment history are material facts that have significantly damaged my credit profile. Their failure to report accurately for years constitutes willful non-compliance. 

2. Inconsistent and Inaccurate Charge-Off Date Chase claims the account was charged off on XX/XX/XXXX. However, this date is contradicted by their own correspondence : The account was closed on XX/XX/XXXX. 
The last payment was made on XX/XX/XXXX. Standard banking practice is to charge off an account after 180 days of delinquency ( XXXX XXXX ). 
Critically, their letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, is a pre-charge-off notice, explicitly stating : If we do not [ receive payment ], we will charge off your credit card account. This proves the account was not charged off as of that date. The XX/XX/XXXX, date appears to be an arbitrary date used to artificially extend the negative reporting period on my credit file. I demand Chase provide the specific accounting ledger entry that justifies this non-standard charge-off date.

3. Failure to Provide Proper Debt Validation Chases initial response to my validation request ( XX/XX/XXXX ) was deficient. Providing only the first page of an application and internally-generated account statements does not constitute validation of a debts validity or the terms therein. Withholding the full contractual agreement under the claim of proprietary information prevented me from verifying the terms I allegedly agreed to, making their validation attempt legally insufficient.

4. Shifting the Burden of Proof in Violation of the FCRA Chases assertion that I must provide any details or documentation to support that there is an error and that they can only act if an error is proven is a gross misstatement of the law. Under 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ( b ), the duty to conduct a reasonable investigation upon receipt of a consumer dispute falls solely on the data furnisher ( Chase ). Their statement reveals a fundamental misunderstanding of their legal obligations and a refusal to abide by them.

5. Loss of Confidence in Data Integrity How can I, or any consumer, have any confidence that the data Chase continues to furnish is accurate? They have admitted to inaccuracies on fundamental data points across multiple CRAs. If the closure date and payment history were wrong, what else is wrong? The balance? The date of first delinquency? The entire account history is now irreparably tainted by their admitted negligence.

Demanded Resolution Given the willful, prolonged, and material nature of these inaccuracies, a simple update is an insufficient remedy. Chase has proven itself incapable of reporting this account accurately. Therefore, I will not accept anything less than the complete deletion and permanent removal of this account from all credit files at XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 

I expect confirmation of this deletion in writing from Chase and will verify it directly with the CRAs. If Chase refuses this reasonable demand, I will have no choice but to consider all available legal remedies for willful FCRA violations.

Thank you for your time and assistance in this serious matter.

text:
This complaint details a clear case of false advertising by Chase, in which I was induced to make a purchase on the Chase XXXX platform based on a written promotional offer that Chase has subsequently failed to honor. Furthermore, Chase 's customer service has engaged in evasive and deceptive tactics to avoid fulfilling their commitment. 
Chronological Account of Events : XXXX. The Deceptive Inducement : On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a targeted promotional email from Chase ( XXXX ) for my Chase Sapphire XXXX card ending in XXXX. The email explicitly offered me an " extra $50.00 travel credit '' as a reward for being a recent cardmember. 
The email 's language was unambiguous and designed to induce a purchase. It stated : '' On top of your $50.00 hotel credit, cardmembers who joined within the last year can now enjoy a little something extraa one-time $50.00 credit toward any purchase on Chase XXXX. '' " To redeem, just book your itinerary through Chase XXXX by XX/XX/XXXX. '' " XXXX using your extra $50.00 travel credit through Chase XXXX. '' This clearly establishes that the promotional credit is separate from and in addition to my standard annual $50.00 hotel credit. 
XXXX. Action Taken Based on the Offer : Trusting this written promise, on XX/XX/XXXX, I booked a hotel stay valued at $130.00 through the Chase XXXX XXXX. At checkout, only my standard $50.00 annual credit was applied. The promised " extra $50.00 '' promotional credit was not available and was not applied. 
XXXX. Chase 's XXXX to XXXX and Evasive Tactics : I have made multiple, exhaustive attempts to resolve this issue directly with Chase, all of which have been met with deflection and misinformation. 
Phone Calls ( XX/XX/XXXX ) : I spent over an hour on the phone with various Chase agents and travel specialists. None of them could locate the offer, and they were unable to resolve the issue. 
Secure Messages ( XX/XX/XXXX onwards and XX/XX/XXXX ) : My formal complaint through Chase 's secure message center was escalated to a " Senior Service XXXX. '' This XXXX, XXXX and XXXX, ignored the core issue. They response deliberately confused the " extra $50.00 promotional credit '' with my " $50.00 annual hotel credit benefit, '' despite the email 's explicit " On top of '' language. They directed me back to the same travel agent phone line that had already proven incapable of helping, creating a frustrating and unproductive loop. 

Deliberate Deception I believe Chase 's actions are intentionally deceptive. They lured me into using their platform with a specific, written financial incentive. When it came time to honor that incentive, their systems failed to provide it, and their customer service apparatus appears trained to confuse, deflect, and frustrate customers into abandoning their legitimate claims. This constitutes a classic bait-and-switch and is a clear violation of consumer trust. 

I have exhausted all reasonable avenues for resolution with Chase directly. I am now turning to the CFPB for assistance.

text: On approximately XX/XX/year>, I was going through my JP Morgan Chase checking account to make sure my transactions were all legitimate. I noticed a transfer of $1500.00 from my checking account to an outside account at an entity called XXXXXXXX XXXX  on XX/XX/year>, which I did not recognize. I noticed another transfer on XX/XX/year> to XXXX XXXX for $3000.00. At that point I called Chase and spoke to someone on their fraud team. As we went through my checking account together, we saw another transfer to XXXX Bank on XX/XX/year> for $3000.00, XXXX on XX/XX/year> for $5000.00 and XXXX on XX/XX/year> for $5000.00, for a total of $17000.00. I vehemently told the Chase employee that I had definitely not authorized these transfers, and she told me she would try to reverse them. A little while later, she called me back and told me she'd successfully reversed them and that I should expect my $17000.00 to be returned to my checking account in XXXX business days. The time came and went and nothing happened. I then received a letter from Chase ( attached ), telling me that they believed I had authorized the transfers and that they would not be returning my money. I again called Chase and spoke to a different person, who told me the case had been reopened, but that the reason the claim had been denied originally was because the bank could not detect any new device having been added to my account, and so assumed the transfers had to have been done on the laptop I use for banking, which is untrue. On the days of the transfers, I was at home. Anyway, a few more days went by and nothing happened, no money was returned. I then spoke to someone named ( I believe ) XXXX XXXX, who patched in another Chase employee who said that they would reexamine how the decision had been made to deny my claim. I am expecting to hear back from them today or tomorrow, but seeing as they've lied to me and have been, in my view, dragging their feet, I don't have high expectations. I have been a Chase customer for 45 years and have done a lot of business with them - a mortgage, a refinancing, day-to-day banking, etc. I would have expected a more strenuous effort on their part to restore my stolen funds. Additionally, I would like to highlight the fact that for NONE of these transfers did I receive any sort of notice or alert from the bank. And yet, when I bought a computer recently for $860.00, the charge was denied and I had to respond to a text from Chase, confirming that I had made the expenditure. But for these large dollar amounts, not a peep. My husband and I are not wealthy people, and the loss of $17000.00 is catastrophic. We recently moved and badly need all the money we have to get settled in our new home.

Chases conduct is unlawful, discriminatory, and a violation of multiple binding federal laws and regulations. This is not just a customer service issueit is a regulatory compliance failure. 
XXXX. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) & FACTA Violations If Chase relied on consumer reports ( from Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, ChexSystems, or Early Warning Services ) to deny me products, Chase must comply with 15 U.S.C. 1681m ( a ) and provide me with an adverse action notice, identifying : The reporting agency, The specific factors leading to denial, My right to a free report and dispute. 
No such notice has been provided. This is a direct violation of FCRA 615.

If Chase is itself furnishing information about these alleged checking accounts to any bureau, then under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) Chase has a duty not to furnish inaccurate information. Once notified of a dispute, Chase must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and correct/delete any false data ( 623 ( a ) ( 2 ), ( a ) ( 8 ), and ( b ) ( 1 ) ).

Under FACTA ( FCRA amendments, 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ), once I declare these accounts fraudulent/unauthorized, Chase must block the information from appearing in consumer reports unless Chase proves otherwise with documentary evidence. 
2. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) / Regulation B Violations Denial of credit or deposit accounts constitutes adverse action under 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) and 12 C.F.R. 1002.2 ( c ). Chase must : Provide a written notice of adverse action within 30 days, State the specific reasons, and Provide the name/contact of the reporting agency ( if applicable ).

Failure to do so is a violation of Reg B 1002.9. Chases refusal to provide disclosures appears to be an unlawful adverse action that blocks me from equal access to financial services. 
XXXX. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) / Regulation E Obligations If Chase claims these alleged accounts ever conducted transactions, they must be treated as unauthorized electronic fund transfers as to me.

Under 15 U.S.C. 1693f and 12 C.F.R. 1005.11, Chase is required to investigate, resolve, and correct such errors within 45 days ( 90 in limited cases ).

Continuing to associate me with unauthorized accounts without investigation constitutes a violation of Reg E and exposes Chase to liability for damages, attorneys fees, and regulatory action.

4. Bank Secrecy Act ( BSA ) / Customer Identification Program ( CIP ) Failures Federal law ( 31 U.S.C. 5318 ; 31 C.F.R. 1020.220 ) requires Chase to verify identity before opening any deposit account. 
If Chases records claim I have checking accounts, Chase must produce documentary verification used to open them : Government-issued ID scanned or copied, IP address/device fingerprint of application, Date/time stamps, Branch teller ID ( if in person ), Application signatures, audio recordings, chat logs. 
If Chase can not produce this, the accounts are either fabrications or identity-theft accounts, and continuing to hold them against me violates the XXXX recordkeeping XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX compliance. 
XXXX. Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) By blocking me from Chase products based on false information, Chase is engaging in unfair and abusive practices prohibited under Dodd-Frank 1036, 12 U.S.C. 5536. 
CFPB has explicit authority to sanction Chase for these practices.

On XX/XX/XXXX, in response to a Chase Bank bonus advertisement, I opened a checking account and a savings account at a local branch. The advertisement specified a bonus of up to $900.00 bonus with qualifying activities. It was required that a new checking account and a new savings account be opened, among other parameters which included keeping funds in the account for 90 days. The code was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

Both accounts were kept in good standing, and the appropriate requirements were met. The 90-day period ended XX/XX/XXXX, and a $900.00 bonus was anticipated being paid within 15 days after the qualifying period. 

I scheduled an on-site meeting with the XXXX, PA branch for Saturday XX/XX/XXXX to inquire about the status of the bonus. I met with XXXX at the branch, and she informed me that a $200.00 bonus was scheduled to be applied to my savings account on Tuesday XX/XX/XXXX but that she did not know the status of the remaining $700.00 bonus. XXXX advised that she would research the matter further and send a claim to the Escalation Department. 

On Friday, XX/XX/XXXX, I received a phone call from XXXX in the Escalation Department ( he probably told me his last name but I didnt make note of it ). He explained that he would further review the issue. On Thursday, XX/XX/XXXX, I received another call from XXXX, who told me that the wrong code was applied when the accounts were opened, that it was a bank error, and that the additional $700.00 bonus would be paid. XXXX advised me to go to my local branch to have them take care of applying the bonus, assuring me that they would know what to do and how to do it. Subsequently, I scheduled another on-site meeting with XXXX for Friday, XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX called me about 30 minutes before the meeting and advised that she was unaware of the conversation I had with XXXX the previous day. I suggested that she contact XXXX directly in the Escalation Department ( XXXX, ext. XXXX, case # XXXX ). XXXX said that she would do so. 

After no response from anyone, and noting that no additional bonus had been applied, I scheduled another on-site meeting with XXXX for Saturday XX/XX/XXXX. Once again, XXXX called me shortly before the meeting and advised me that she had no further information to provide but that she would continue researching the matter. 

Another week went by with no bonus paid and no further update, so I scheduled yet another on-site meeting with XXXX for Thursday, XX/XX/XXXX. Once again, XXXX called me before the meeting, but THIS TIME, she advised that she finally had an update for me : THEY WERE NOT PAYING THE ADDITIONAL BONUS because I had previously received a checking account bonus and was, apparently, ineligible for any additional bonus. 

I suggested to XXXX that I was not informed at the time I opened both accounts that the full bonus, as advertised, and as applied with the appropriate account code that I would not be eligible. 

XXXX offered to file an appeal to the decision, and I advised her that I would like her to do that but that I would be filing a complaint with the CFPB. 

I feel that I am entitled to the additional $700.00 bonus due to bank error AND misinformation.

text:
I recently discovered disturbing information that raises serious legal and ethical concerns about JPMorgan Chase Banks ( JPMCB ) conduct in reporting a charged-off account on my credit report. After reviewing their own SEC filingsspecifically their 10-K, 8-K, and 10-D disclosuresI found that JPMCB has securitized the account by transferring the receivables into a trust structure ( Chase Issuance Trust ) through a true sale. 

This means that JPMCB no longer owns the account or the right to collect or report on it. Their 10-K clearly states that once transferred to the trust, JPMCB does not retain any ownership interest in the receivables. Despite this, JPMCB continues to report the account as charged off with a balance, implying they still hold creditor status. 

Not only was I never notified of this transfer as required under 15 U.S.C. 1641 ( g ) of the Truth in Lending Act, but JPMCB also admitted in previous responses that no IRS 1099-C form was issued, which is required if a debt is truly charged off. They are effectively attempting to both claim tax benefits for the charge-off and continue to enforce or report the account which is misleading at best and potentially fraudulent at worst. 

I had no knowledge of how securitization works until recently, and I now realize that JPMCB is acting outside of its legal authority by continuing to report on an account it sold. This violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act, Truth in Lending Act, Metro 2 guidelines, and potentially IRS regulations.

Misleading promotional credit terms and false information provided by representative Date of Incident : XX/XX/year>, approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX  EST What Happened : I received a $500.00 promotional credit with my Chase Sapphire Reserve credit card for travel bookings. On XX/XX/year>, I used $170.00 of this credit to book a fully refundable hotel reservation through the Chase travel portal. 

When I attempted to book additional non-consecutive nights at the same hotel, I discovered the $500.00 promotional credit was a one-time use onlymeaning I could not use the remaining $320.00 for additional bookings. However, since I had intentionally selected a fully refundable booking option ( which was more expensive than non-refundable rates ), I expected I could simply cancel and receive a full refund of my promotional credit back to $500.00, then rebook all my dates together in one reservation. 

At approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>, I called the travel booking line to confirm this. The representative ( Employee ID : XXXX ) told me that if I cancelled my refundable reservation, my promotional credit would return to $500.00. 

When the representative checked my account to process this, she discovered I would only receive $170.00 back in promotional credit, not the $500.00. She was audibly surprised and took significant time trying to understand what happened. This demonstrated that even the company 's trained representatives don't understand how this promotional offer works. 

When I expressed confusion, the representative told me I " should have read the details '' and that " it makes sense. '' I pointed out that she herself was just surprised by the policy. She went silent and could not respond. She transferred me to an escalation department representative who upheld the policy. 

Why This Is Misleading : 1. False information from company representative : I was told my credit would return to $500.00. I relied on this statement from the company 's employee when making decisions.

2. Contradicts " fully refundable '' terms : I deliberately chose a more expensive fully refundable booking option specifically to maintain flexibility. The term " fully refundable '' means a customer can cancel and receive a complete refund without penalty. A reasonable consumer expects that promotional credit used on a fully refundable booking would return to its original amount upon cancellation, just as regular payment would. 

XXXX. Inadequate disclosure at point of booking : The promotional credit fine print states you forfeit the remaining balance if you don't use the entire credit " in one purchase. '' However, this critical information was not prominently displayed during the booking process. Because I selected a fully refundable option ( paying a premium for this flexibility ), I had no reason to scrutinize additional information about forfeiturethe " fully refundable '' designation led me to believe I maintained full flexibility with my promotional credit. 

4. Logical contradiction in policy design : The company offers " fully refundable '' booking options that cost more than non-refundable rates. Customers pay this premium specifically for flexibility and the ability to get full refunds. However, the promotional credit policy undermines this flexibility by making the credit non-refundable even when used on refundable bookings. This contradiction is not disclosed at the point of booking.

5. Company 's own staff confused by terms : The representative 's surprised reaction and initial incorrect information proves these promotional terms are not clear, even to trained employees. If company staff don't understand it, customers can not reasonably be expected to anticipate this outcome. 

Financial Impact : Original promotional credit : $500.00 Used amount : $170.00 on XX/XX/year> Current promotional credit : $170.00 Lost value : $320.00 What I'm Requesting : Restore the full $500.00 promotional credit. I was given false information by the company 's representative, I paid a premium for a fully refundable booking with the reasonable expectation of full refund flexibility, and the actual travel services have not been consumed. 

The promotional offer as currently structured creates a misleading situation where customers pay premiums for " fully refundable '' bookings but discover the promotional credit itself is not refundable, despite no clear disclosure of this contradiction at the booking stage.

text:
1. My complaint starts when I received a letter from Chase stating my account was closing. Chase stated there was concerning activity and I was instructed by Chase in writing to destroy all cards and checks associated with the accounts ( attached ). 

A. The concerning activity I attempted to appeal this decision through the CFPB to get directly in contact with the XXXX XXXX but was met with a response that their decision was remaining the same. In their response, I noticed they revised their original statement referring to it as unexpected activity when responding to my appeal ( attached ). I would like clarification on this inconsistency, as the original terminology used is associated with accusations, which brings me to the next part of my complaint ; When a Chase XXXX representative previously accused me of money laundering when discussing my personal transfers. This was documented as a complaint with Chase, and after making them aware of that statement, two Chase managers called me directly about the issue, attempting to discuss the statement that was made. Now I have received a letter from Chase, after a transfer that was performed, dated the same day, providing notice that my accounts will be closing. A transfer that was performed in accordance with Chases published guidance, and yet Chase ultimately blamed me for activity being concerning that it itself directed and encouraged.. I will be attaching Chases own How to Avoid a Fee terms ( attached ). 

B. Credit Card Fraud and Possible Identity Theft I followed the instructions in the letter directly as stated, then discarded all the material. On XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX   EST, a Chase representative contacted me to verify transaction activity and I then realized I fell victim to fraud. I explained the letter I received and having trouble destroying a metal card, but ultimately followed the instructions on the letter. The representative claims she has no idea what I was talking about and intimidated me for following instructions by Chase then later stated during the call that my Social Security number and personal data may have been compromised due my actions the very outcome that resulted from following Chases own written instructions. 

- This sequence of events reflects negligence and a deceptive practice under the Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531, 5536 ). Furthermore, because Chases instructions directly created a risk of unauthorized use of my account and personal data, this also implicates Regulation E ( 12 C.F.R. 1005.6 ), which governs consumer liability and bank obligations following unauthorized transactions.

2. Chases failure to deliver communications, including my account statements, through my authorized electronic communication channel, and the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive financial information 1. I was enrolled in Chase Banks paperless statements program, which required me to provide an email address for electronic communications.

2. My original email address was later compromised, so I updated my email address in Chase Banks online system. Chase acknowledged and confirmed the updated email, and communications have been successfully sent to the new email since then. My old email was removed from my account profile and is no longer authorized. 

- When I updated my email address, this update served as an express revocation of consent for Chase to send any further electronic communications or statements to my previous email address. Chase acknowledged this change, and the old address no longer appeared in my online banking profile.

3. After this update, I opened a new account with Chase, using the updated email address on the application. However, Chase sent communications, including statements, for this accountincluding account type, product type, balances, due dates, statement details, and the last 4 digits of my cardto my old, unauthorized email address. An address never provided for this account.

4. I did not receive certain communications and statements at any authorized communication channel, preventing me from monitoring my accounts and accessing financial records I am entitled to. 

Legal and Regulatory Basis for Complaint 1. E-SIGN Act / Paperless Agreement Violation : Under the E-SIGN Act, electronic records must be delivered in a manner that ensures the customer can reliably access them. Chase failed to deliver statements to my authorized email, violating my rights under the paperless agreement.

2. UDAAP Unfair and Abusive Practices ( Dodd-Frank Act 5531, 5536 ) : - Unfair : Chases failure to send statements to my authorized email caused substantial harm by preventing access to account information necessary for financial management.

- Deceptive : Chase represented that my email information had been updated and that all paperless statements would be sent to my authorized address, which did not occur. - Abusive : Sending sensitive account information to an old, unauthorized
email interfered with my ability to manage my finances and exposed me to potential fraud risk.

Legal basis for revoked consent A. E-SIGN Act Under 15 U.S.C. 7001 ( c ) ( 1 ) ( C ) ( ii ), consumers have the right to withdraw consent for electronic delivery at any time, and the institution must honor that withdrawal within a reasonable period.

By sending statements to the revoked address, Chase : * Ignored a withdrawn consent, and * Failed to provide effective electronic delivery as required by E-SIGN.

Under 15 U.S.C. 7001 ( c ) ( 1 ) ( C ) ( ii ), I had the right to withdraw or modify my consent to receive records at a specific electronic address. My email update and Chases acknowledgment constituted withdrawal of consent for the prior email address. By continuing to send records to that revoked address, Chase failed to comply with the E-SIGN Acts consumer consent and withdrawal provisions. 

B. Regulation P ( GLBA, 12 C.F.R. 1016.13 ) Regulation P also ties consent and authorization to nonpublic personal information sharing. Once you revoke consent, the bank must stop sending or disclosing information to that contact channel.

Under 12 C.F.R. 1016.13, financial institutions must respect consumer directions regarding disclosure and delivery of nonpublic personal information. My revocation of consent for th
e prior email address made any further disclosures to that channel unauthorized under Regulation P.

3. Violation of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ) and Regulation P ( 15 U.S.C. 68016809 ; 12 C.F.R. Part 1016 ) - The GLBA and Regulation P require financial institutions to protect the confidentiality of nonpublic personal information ( NPI ) and to ensure that disclosures are made only to authorized recipients.

- Chases continued transmission of account statements containing personal and financial details to an unauthorized, compromised email address constitutes a failure to safeguard NPI and an unauthorized disclosure under these provisions.

4. Violation of the FTC Safeguards Rule ( 16 C.F.R. Part 314 ) - The Safeguards Rule, issued under the GLBA, requires financial institutions to maintain appropriate procedures to protect customer information from unauthorized access or disclosure.

- Chases failure to prevent statements from being sent to an unauthorized email shows a breakdown in internal safeguards and information-security controls.

5. Potential Violation of the Electronic Communications Privacy Act ( ECPA 18 U.S.C. 2511 ) - The ECPA prohibits the intentional transmission of electronic communications containing personal data to unauthorized or unintended recipients. By sending confidential statements to a deauthorized, compromised email address, Chase may have violated the ECPAs prohibition against the unauthorized disclosure of protected electronic communications.

text:
Attn : Compliance Department reference Number : XXXX : I reviewed the response to my Chase credit card denial. Your statements are not accurate and do not comply with federal law. This letter is my rebuttal and demand for correction. 
When I applied for a credit card, I gave you my Social Security number, signature, and permission to access my credit report. That information has value. You accepted it and used it for your own business purposes. I received nothing in return. That is not fair. It creates a one-sided transaction that violates federal law. 
Under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 15 U.S.C. 68016809 ) and Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ) ), you had permission to use my information only to review my credit application. Once you denied my application, that purpose ended. Keeping or using my information after that violates those laws. When you denied my application, the permissible purpose that allowed you to access and use my personal and credit information ended under federal law. The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act limits how a bank may collect, use, or retain nonpublic personal information once a transaction is complete. The Fair Credit Reporting Act restricts use of a consumer report to the purpose for which it was obtained. By keeping, storing, or reusing my data after denying credit, Chase breached both laws. These statutes require that consumer data be used only for the stated transaction and then either destroyed or protected from further use. The Privacy Rule ( 12 C.F.R. 1016.10 ) under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires financial institutions to stop using or sharing consumer information when there is no ongoing customer relationship. After your denial, no continuing relationship existed, yet you kept my personal data. 
The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681m ) also prohibits further use of a consumer report after an adverse action has been taken. Once you denied credit, you were required to end all use of my report and protect it from reuse or disclosure. 

You also have a duty to protect and limit how you use personal data. That duty makes you a data fiduciary. By keeping my personal information after denying credit, you are violating that duty and unjustly benefiting from my data. If you want to keep using my application data, you must provide equal value either approve credit or compensate me for its use. Otherwise, delete all my information and remove the inquiry from all credit reports. 
Now I will address your statements one by one. 
You said the application is not related to a secured loan, securities instrument, or trust. That is misleading. Banks use consumer credit data in asset-backed and trust-related processes under Regulation AB II. Whether approved or denied, the data itself becomes part of your financial asset system and is protected by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. 
You said you did not violate any laws. Once you denied credit, your permissible purpose under FCRA 1681b ended. Keeping or using my report after that violates federal law. 
You said I agreed to the terms and conditions before applying. I did not. I applied in person, not online. No one gave me written terms or disclosures before I signed. Regulation B ( 12 C.F.R. 1002.4 ( b ) ) requires you to provide that in writing at or before application. You failed to do so. 
You said the online pricing and terms were shown before submission. That is false. I was in a branch, not online. Including that statement in your federal response is misleading. 
You said the inquiry will stay because it is accurate. Accuracy under the law means the data must show the maximum possible accuracy. Reporting a hard inquiry after the credit review ended is not accurate or necessary. 
You said the application can not be stopped or altered. That is wrong. Under GLBA 6802 ( a ), I can revoke consent for you to keep or use my information at any time. You are required to honor that.

You said you can not destroy my data. The FTC Safeguards Rule ( 16 C.F.R. Part 314 ) says you must securely dispose of consumer information once it is no longer needed. Refusing to delete it violates that rule. 
You quoted the Equal Credit Opportunity Act. You left out the part that bans practices that have an unequal effect. Keeping and using my personal information after denying credit gives you value and leaves me with none. That is unequal treatment. 
Your response ignored my rights under the FCRA, GLBA, and XXXX. I gave you consideration. You took value and gave nothing in return. That is unjust enrichment and a breach of duty. 
I am demanding that Chase either approve credit or compensate me for your use of my information. If not, delete all data tied to my application, destroy the application records, and remove the inquiry from all credit bureaus. Send written confirmation of these actions to my address within 15 days.
sub_product_raw: General-purpose credit card or charge card

I have repeatedly exercised that right by requesting, in writing, that JPMorgan Chase and/or its collection representatives provide the following documentation : The original credit agreement or application showing my signature and the terms of the alleged account ; A complete, itemized statement detailing how the balance was calculated, including interest, fees, and payments ; The chain of title and assignment records establishing Chases ownership or lawful authority to collect ; Copies of the required validation and default notices as set forth in FDCPA 809 ( a ) ; Proof of the statute of limitations confirming that the debt remains legally collectible ; and Any prior investigation results or dispute findings under FCRA 1681i . 

To date, none of these required materials have been provided. Instead, I have received only automated or template responses that do not constitute lawful debt validation. Continuing to report or attempt to collect on an account without first verifying it violates FDCPA 1692g ( b ) and FCRA 1681e ( b ) and 1681s-2 ( b ). 

The law requires creditors and furnishers to maintain and report accurate, verifiable information. Federal courts have affirmed this in multiple decisions, including Cushman v. Trans Union Corp., 115 F.3d 220 ( 3d Cir. 1997 ), Dennis v. BEH-1, LLC, 520 F.3d 1066 ( 9th Cir. 2008 ), and Clark v. Capital Credit & Collection Services, 460 F.3d 1162 ( 9th Cir. 2006 ), all holding that unverifiable or misleading credit data can not lawfully remain on a consumers file. 

By continuing to furnish or collect on an unvalidated debt, JPMorgan Chase has failed to meet its legal duties under both federal and state consumer protection laws. The ongoing reporting of these accounts has caused measurable harm to my creditworthiness, financial opportunities, and peace of mind.

All of this activity took place before the dispute meaning the cardholder voluntarily used the service, benefited from it, and later attempted to reverse the valid payments.

This is a textbook case of friendly fraud.

The cardholder participated and later misrepresented the transaction as unauthorized.

Despite this, the issuer sided with the cardholder and ignored strong evidence.

2 ) XXXX = Common Nickname XXXX is a standard, widely recognized nickname for XXXX. 
Nicknames do not invalidate authorization. 

3 ) Consistent Account Use The customer : - Logged in repeatedly - Booked onboarding calls - Interacted with support - Someone claiming fraud would not access and use the account for months.

Conclusion All evidence ( email, usage, review, cancellation ) confirms the cardholder knowingly authorized and used the service. The nickname XXXX does NOT invalidate authorization.

text:
Earlier this year, I lost my job and sought to enter into financial hardship plans with my credit card companies. I easily entered into payment plans with XXXX and XXXX XXXX where I had a reduced monthly payment based on my current ability to pay and expected duration of hardship, along with a reduced interest rate of 9.99 %. I called Chase to do the same after entering into the program with XXXX. The customer service representative asked me all the same questions : what is the nature of your hardship, how long do you expect the situation to last, and what amount do you believe you can pay right now as a monthly minimum. The customer service representative established a payment plan where $200.00 would be withdrawn, monthly, from my account. The customer service representative assured me that once I finished the past due amount of $ XXXX dollars, I would have all fees and interest charged to the card reversed. I would continue on with that payment plan and my account would remain frozen. This plan was, purportedly, to allow me to catch up on my past due payment and not drown in interest or fees. However, I have received a statement from Chase, despite being enrolled in a program where I automatically have $200.00 withdrawn from my account monthly, that I have a current due amount of $1700.00 and my account is 73 days past due. That my interest was not frozen or reduced, like XXXX or XXXX, and that I had not enrolled in a payment plan based on hardship but rather a " unique program '' where I would make payments based on the past due amount but would still be charged interest and late fees in full. This does not make sense whatsoever. A consumer is calling to enter into a financial hardship arrangement, is induced into agreeing to automatic payments with promises that there would not be fees assessed, that the program is to help them get through that hardship, only to find out that XXXX months into the automatic payments they reportedly owe $1800.00 based on interest and fees they could not afford before, at the rate as before. 

This is an act of misrepresentation by Chase to induce customers into believing they have, similar to other large financial institutions, entered into a financial hardship payment when in reality, the bank plans on keeping the interest rate the same, assessing late fees the same, and spiraling the customer into further debt. 

I have called chase twice now to resolve this issue with managers identifying with ID numbers XXXX and XXXX. I have requested the transcript of my call with the customer service representative in XXXX and was denied that information absent a subpoena. And, during my latest call on XX/XX/XXXX, the representative revealed to me that Chase does not have a verbatim transcript as would be used in court. Rather, they have a summary of the call that " reports '' what was discussed between parties, and -- despite this incomplete record -- admitted that the representative did promise a reversal of all fees.

I picked up the phone for an unknown number, I was waiting on an important phone call about the health of a pet so they got me at the exact right time. The person on the other side said, " This is the XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  office, we are calling because you didn't show up for jury duty. Is there a reason you weren't able to make it? '' and it spiraled into an elaborate scam telling me there would be a warrant for my arrest if I didn't give them $1000.00 for my bail. I haven't had any involvement with police or the courts so this scam was a perfect storm for me to fall for when I was having a stressful time. 

They said I would get the money back quick, I just had to talk to a judge real fast to make sure I wasn't a risk or under duress of some kind. There was a whole story how they had had jurors threatened in the past and being stopped from going to jury duty by someone the defendant paid. A " XXXX  XXXX '' got on the phone with me and walked me through an elaborate story about the fake case, and what I needed to do. He even provided me with a fake badge and radio number ( Radio XXXX Badge XXXX ). They said I had to pay cash at either a XXXX or XXXX  or I could use my XXXX  at XXXX. They kept me on the phone, told me I couldn't talk to anyone because the transcript would be use in the case. I didn't have $1000.00 in my account, truthfully I had negative money in my account and was waiting to be paid the next day. They said they could change it to $500.00 if the judge thought I wasn't a huge risk. He put me on hold and said that would work. I didn't live super close to a XXXX so I drove and talked to the man for a while. He gave me a speech I had to give the person at XXXX on how to proceed. He sent me a Capital XXXX bar code ( though looking at the XXXX receipt it says XXXX XXXX  XXXX, which has a lot of dead links on its site including their customer service arm ) and the teller commented, " Wow I haven't seen XXXX  XXXX do it this way before! '' and it sunk in. 

The man on the phone tried to push for more money and that's when I realized it was a scam. I hung up and went back in to the XXXX to tell them I was scammed. They were very nice, said they'd keep an eye out for this scam. They couldn't do anything more but said I should call XXXX quickly tried to stop the transaction through the XXXX app. The only option that was close was, " it wasn't me '' and I quickly put a hold on my card. I called and talked to XXXX, told them everything, and they were able to refund me. 

Cut to today, I see they reversed my claim because while being scammed and under the impression I would be arrested if I didn't send money, I still physically made the transaction. I have now filed a police report ( they wouldn't take XXXX previously because I had gotten my money back ) and I'm trying to get my claim accepted.

Summary of my complaint : I disputed multiple transactions made to an online gaming website called XXXX. This merchant failed to honor its own Responsible Gaming policy. I had permanently deleted my account on XX/XX/year> as part of a self-exclusion process, but the merchant reactivated it without my consent, allowing me to make additional purchases and deposits totalling about $7000.00 that should have been blocked according to their own Terms and Conditions. 

XX/XX/year> : I received a promotional email from XXXX and was able to log back into my supposedly deleted account and make new purchases. 

During this period, I used XXXX Responsible Gaming tools to set the following limits : XXXX time-out XXXX daily play limit $300.00 daily spending cap These limits were not enforced the platform allowed me to exceed both my time and spending restrictions. I informed the live chat and support team multiple times but without resolution. 

XX/XX/year> : XXXX emailed me stating that my account was permanently banned following my repeated complaints. 

XX/XX/year> : Despite this, the merchant continued to send me promotional emails. 

Additionally, after I began contacting XXXX repeatedly about their failure to enforce Responsible Gaming limits, the platform removed the Responsible Gaming tab entirely from my account. This demonstrates intentional disregard for their own player-protection policies. I have screen recordings and screenshots documenting my account deletion process, subsequent ability to log in again, the ignored spending/time limits, and my email correspondence with the merchant, in which they denied these failures and refused a refund. 

I used the Responsible XXXX  tools exactly as intended setting time and spending limits, and deleting my account to prevent excessive play and spending. The platform failed to enforce these protections, allowing me to exceed both time and financial limits. 

I submitted evidence to Chase showing that the merchant violated its own rules by not enforcing permanent deletion. However, Chase denied most of my disputes, stating that the charges were voluntary, even though they had previously credited me for XXXX identical transaction for the same issue. 

I believe Chase did not properly review my supporting evidence and failed to consider the responsible gaming and consumer protection aspects of the case. I am requesting that the CFPB review this matter and ensure Chase conducts a fair and consistent investigation across all disputed transactions.

XX/XX/year> Follow-up with Chase, no update On XX/XX/XXXX, I went to Chase again to ask for an update : I was told there was still no new information.

Unprompted closure notice At XXXX XXXX PST on XX/XX/year>, I received a text message from Chase stating they needed additional information from me and that my accounts were in danger of being closed.

It is a registered LLC in the United States. 

It files taxes annually and maintains proper accounting records. 

It operates in the crypto and blockchain sector, which is legal and fully reported for tax purposes.

He said Chase would send me a check at an unspecified time.

This disrupts my business during the holiday period when financial predictability is essential. 

Chase 's actions appear to be discriminatory against lawful crypto-related businesses despite full tax compliance and transparency. 

Chases lack of transparency I requested a specific explanation for the closure, and XXXX explicitly told me he could not provide any reason. 

He said only that it was to protect Chase as an institution. 

The call was recorded on their end, but I was not provided access to the recording. 

No written explanation has been provided.

A detailed explanation of how incoming XXXX and XXXX XXXX payments are being handled, including whether they are being accepted, rejected, or held. 

A specific timeline for when and how my funds will be returned. 

Assurance that Chase is not unlawfully or discriminatorily debanking customers who operate legally in the crypto and blockchain sector.

Chase refused to provide statements or balances even though they are required to. 

Funds in legitimate business accounts are being withheld with no timeline. 

This action disrupts a lawful, tax-paying small business. 

It appears to be part of a broader pattern of banks debanking crypto-involved businesses without cause. 

Chases behavior directly contradicts consumer protection standards, transparency requirements, and the CFPBs mandates for fair treatment.

To Whom It May Concern, This is a rebuttal to the previously submitted claim # XXXX, Chase Banks claim that they notified me of a credit limit reduction on my Chase Sapphire personal credit card on XX/XX/XXXX. That claim is false. I did not receive any notificationby email, mail, or secure messageon or around XX/XX/XXXX regarding any reduction to my Sapphire credit line. 

The only communication I received from Chase was after I called to inquire why my limit was suddenly lowered without notice. The representative then sent an email to me in XXXX, long after the limit had already been reduced. I have attached screenshots of both emails that clearly differentiate between : Business credit accounts ( Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) Personal credit accounts ( Chase Sapphire ) Neither email shows any notification originating on XX/XX/XXXX. 

In addition : I received no letters at my home address. 

I received no letters at my business address. 

No secure message was ever posted to my Chase online portal. 

No adverse action notice was issued as required by federal law. 

Chases retroactive email was sent only after I called and questioned the sudden reduction. 

This proves beyond question that Chase did not notify me prior to, or at the time of, taking adverse action against my account.

Federal Laws Violated 1. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) ECOA requires creditors to provide written adverse action notice whenever they : Reduce a credit limit, Terminate credit, or Make any unfavorable change to a consumers account.

Chase provided no such notice for the Sapphire reduction.

The only letter I received pertained to my business accounts, which is not compliant.

This is a direct violation of ECOA.

2. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681m ( a ) If Chase used my consumer credit report in making this adverse decision, they are legally required to notify me and provide : The name of the credit bureau used, My right to obtain a copy of the report, My right to dispute inaccurate information. 

Chase provided none of this. 

3. FCRA Permissible Purpose 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) If Chase accessed my credit report in connection with this adverse actionand then failed to notify methis access may not meet the standard of permissible purpose under the law.

This is even more concerning because no warning or documentation was ever provided.

Impact on My Credit Profile Chases unauthorized and undisclosed credit limit reduction negatively impacted my credit by : Increasing my reported utilization ratio Potentially lowering my credit score Creating instability on my credit profile Reducing available credit on a longstanding, well-maintained account This harm occurred because Chase failed to properly notify me, failed to issue an adverse action notice, and misrepresented their claim of contacting me on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Requested Action I am requesting CFPB review to require Chase to : Provide proof of any notification sent on XX/XX/XXXX ( none exists ). 

Provide the legally required adverse action notice for the Sapphire account. 

Restore my previous credit limit or provide a lawful, documented justification. 

Explain why no letter was sent to either my business or home address. 

Disclose whether my credit report was accessed and document the permissible purpose. 

Chases actions are not compliant with ECOA and FCRA, and the lack of proper notification has caused direct and measurable harm to my credit. 

The documents attached show that Chase was not in compliance. 

Thank you for your time and attention.

Chase initially credited my account but ultimately reversed the refund and denied my dispute, despite evidence that the company was not fulfilling their obligations in accordance with federal debt relief regulations.

2. A review of Chases denial of my dispute, as their decision did not take into account the TSR requirements for debt relief fees.

3. A refund of excess fees withdrawn that were not earned through actual settlements.

Company : JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.Product : Checking account / Debit cardIssue : Unauthorized transactions/ fraud What happened : I am filing this complaint because Chase improperly denied my dispute for an unauthorized transaction made with my debit card information. My relative used my card without my permission to pay his own rent. I was charged $2200.00 on XX/XX/year>. I did not authorize this transaction, did not receive any benefit from it, and I was not a party to the lease or any agreement with the merchant.

I do not know exactly how he obtained my card information, but I believe he may have taken a picture of my card at some point when I was visiting his home. He is not an authorized user on my account and has never had permission to use my card or card information for any purpose.

Chase mailed me the documentation that the merchant provided during the dispute process. None of the documents contain my name, my signature, my authorization, or any connection to me. Specifically : The lease contract provided by the merchant does not include my name anywhere. The payment records show the transaction was associated with my relatives personal account, not mine. There is no authorization form, signature, or agreement with my name on it. There is no evidence showing I approved or participated in this payment.

Despite the complete absence of my name or authorization in the merchant documents, Chase still denied my claim and classified this as an authorized transaction. This is an incorrect application of Regulation E. A transaction is unauthorized when it is performed by someone without actual authority, and when that person is not an authorized user. That is exactly the situation here.

Chase failed to conduct a reasonable investigation and ignored the fact that the merchant documents do not involve me at all. I never entered into any contract with this landlord or merchant, I never agreed to pay this rent, and the person who initiated the transfer was not authorized to use my card.

I am requesting that the CFPB require Chase to : 1. Reopen and properly investigate this dispute.

2. Reverse the denial and refund the unauthorized rent payment.

3. Refund any fees associated with the unauthorized transaction.

4. Provide a written, Regulation-E-compliant explanation of their new determination.

I am willing to provide copies of all documents Chase sent me. They clearly show the transaction was tied to my relatives lease and personal informationnot mineand there is no authorization from me whatsoever. 
Thank you for your assistance.

text:
I pay my monthly rent ( $3600.00 ) with a check via mail -- the check is made out to the same company for the same dollar amount each month. In XX/XX/XXXX, I renewed my lease and my rent increased to $3800.00. In XXXX, I spoke with my building management office about renewing the lease and they let me know that my last check ( XXXX ) was delayed in the mail but when it arrived they could see it was postmarked on time, therefore they weren't considering it late. When my XXXX check didn't post to my bank account within the first week of the month, I did not think anything of it because of prior delays. 

I spoke with the management office today ( XX/XX/XXXX ) because they mailed me a letter saying I had a late fee on my account, and I knew my checks had all been cashed since I last spoke to them ( so XXXX, XXXX & XXXX all showed as cashed on my Chase statement ). They said they never received it. After some back and forth I looked at the digital image of the check cashed on XX/XX/XXXX and saw that it was white-washed and someone had written their own name on the front of the check as the intended recipient. I wrote the check ( as I have every month since XX/XX/XXXX ) to my building management company, and they always use a stamp to endorse the back of the check. This check was tampered with and forged. The building management office told me to call my bank. 

When I spoke to my bank, they said it had been past the allotted time for me to report the fraud, and I " should have been more vigilant. '' The only information they were able to give me was that the fraudulent check was cashed at XXXX. My understanding is that XXXX would then be held responsible for reimbursement, as they cashed the fraudulent check. Chase would not open a claim and said the system was " built in a way that can not be overridden if it's been more than 65 days -- I reported it 7 days too late ). I was not asking Chase to reimburse me, I was asking them to document this as fraud so I could take a paper trail to the police. They told me I was out of luck and I should have looked to see who signed the check. Moving forward, I will do that, however, nothing seemed " off '' when I looked at my monthly transactions because it was a check cashed for the same amount I have paid every month for over a year. There were no flags. 

I then went to XXXX to get information on the account it was deposited into, so I could give the police everything as evidence. They told me they can't give me any information and that if I wanted info I would have to get the police to subpoena them. I can't get the police to do that because I can't get Chase to file a claim. 

I have never had this happen before and have been a loyal Chase client for years. I was notified of this transgression in my account today and reported it immediately. To be told I was " too late '' and " not vigilant '' is unacceptable. Neither Chase or XXXX is taking any accountability.

I have repeatedly contacted Chase : Multiple secure messages through online banking, Phone calls to the levy department and XXXX department where I left messages and received no substantive response, and Calls with the XXXX XXXX, which opened internal cases and acknowledged the overdraft-fee issue.

text:
In XX/XX/year> I used my Chase credit card to rent a vehicle from XXXX in XXXX. The rental agreement included a standard Damage Waiver / liability reduction product that is used in XXXX to cap the renters financial responsibility ( often called XXXX ). Under XXXX XXXX terms, this is a contractual limitation of liability routinely provided with the vehicle, not a separate U.S.-style collision XXXX policy. 

Without this liability reduction, I would have been personally responsible for the full replacement value of the vehicle if it was damaged or totaled. With it, my contractual liability was capped at XXXX. My XXXX auto policy does not provide any coverage outside the XXXX, its territories, or XXXX, so I had no other applicable insurance in XXXX. 

During the rental, the vehicle sustained front-right bumper damage in a private parking lot. XXXX charged me the XXXX damage excess under the contract. The total repair estimate from XXXX was XXXX, but my liability was limited to the XXXX excess, which I paid. 

I then filed a claim under the Auto Rental Collision Damage benefit associated with my Chase credit card. The benefit is marketed as providing collision damage coverage for rental cars when I pay with my card and do not have other applicable coverage. On XX/XX/year>, the claim was denied by XXXX  benefits XXXX ( XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX / XXXX ) on the grounds that I had accepted the rental agencys XXXX XXXX which they said voids the benefit. 

I appealed this decision in writing on XX/XX/year>. In my appeal I explained that, in XXXX, the Damage Waiver is a standard contractual liability limitation built into the rental structure, not a separately underwritten collision damage insurance product like in the XXXX. I also explained that : ( XXXX ) I had no primary auto coverage abroad, and ( XXXX ) by accepting the liability cap, I actually reduced the potential exposure of the credit card benefit XXXX from the full value of the vehicle down to the XXXX excess. 

After my appeal, I repeatedly called to request status updates. I was told several different and inconsistent timelines ( XXXX business days to reopen the case, plus another XXXX business days to review ), even after more than XXXX business days had already passed with no action. Eventually, the appeal was denied again for the same reason : that accepting the rental companys XXXX nullified the benefit. 

The way the XXXX is applying this exclusion effectively makes the card benefit impossible to use for international rentals in XXXX. In practice, a consumer must either ( a ) accept the standard local liability reduction product ( and then have the claim denied as XXXX accepted ), or ( b ) decline it and personally assume the entire replacement value of the car, with no primary auto coverage. Nowhere in XXXX benefit materials is it clearly disclosed that using the standard XXXX liability-limitation structure will void the advertised collision damage benefit. 

I believe this is unfair and misleading. The benefit is presented as providing collision damage coverage for international rentals when other insurance does not apply, but the XXXX applies XXXX exclusions in a way that makes the coverage practically unavailable in common XXXX rental situations. I complied with the terms as a reasonable consumer could understand them and acted prudently to limit risk, yet the benefit was denied.

text:
I am filing this complaint because JPMorgan Chase Bank closed my bank account and wrongfully kept approximately $1200.00 of my earned wages, which were deposited via direct deposit from my employer in XX/XX/year>. These funds are my salary, belong exclusively to me, and were not connected in any way to the check that Chase claimed was under investigation. Despite multiple attempts to resolve this directly with the bank, Chase has refused to return my money.

Detailed explanation of what happened : I was the sole owner of a checking account with Chase. In early XXXX, I deposited a check on behalf of another person as a favor. Chase placed that check on hold and later decided to close my account, claiming that the check was being investigated.

Even though the check did not belong to me, was not issued to me, and was unrelated to my personal funds, Chase froze my account and permanently kept the money that was inside at the time of the closure.

The funds that Chase kept were not related to the check under investigation. 
They were solely my earningsapproximately $ XXXX to me by my employer. These were direct deposits of my regular wages, deposited legally and legitimately. 

Once the account was closed, I immediately contacted Chase numerous times by phone and in person at different branches. I clearly explained that the money being withheld was my salary and that I had nothing to do with any alleged issue regarding the third-party check. Despite this, Chase repeatedly refused to release my wages. 

Why this is a serious problem : My wages are legally protected, and banks are not allowed to confiscate or retain a consumers earned income without a lawful reason. The money Chase kept was not fraudulent, was not part of any dispute, and had no connection whatsoever to the check deposited by someone else.

By holding my salary, Chase deprived me of access to essential living funds, including money needed for rent, food, childcare, and transportation. This caused me significant financial stress and hardship.

Chase has never provided a valid justification for withholding my wages. Their actions appear to violate federal consumer protection laws, including : Regulations governing unauthorized holds and account closures Rules requiring banks to release funds not involved in an investigation The basic requirement that financial institutions act fairly and transparently What I am requesting from the CFPB : 1. The immediate return of my $1200.00 in earned wages.

2. A complete written explanation from Chase regarding why they kept my salary and under what authority.

3. A full review of Chases handling of my account closure and the improper retention of my personal funds.

4. Assurance that Chase will correct this issue and prevent similar harm to other consumers. 

I am respectfully requesting the CFPBs help because I have exhausted all efforts with Chase, and the bank continues to deny me access to my legally earned money. I believe I have been treated unfairly, and I am seeking justice and the return of the wages that rightfully belong to me. 

Thank you for your assistance.

text:
FORMAL COMPLAINT Financial Institution : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . 
Product : Checking Account / Savings Account Issue : Funds not made available as promised / Deposit hold Sub-issue : Mobile deposit check processed and subsequently unpaid DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPLAINT I hereby submit this formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . for the unjustified hold and non-payment of a check that was properly deposited via Chases mobile deposit service, as well as the subsequent closure of my account, without clear, timely, or legally sufficient notice. 

On XX/XX/year>, I deposited a check in the amount of $1500.00, issued by XXXX XXXX, using Chases mobile deposit feature. The banks system confirmed that the check was received and processed, with no immediate warnings or alerts regarding any potential issues. 

Subsequently, Chase placed a hold on the funds and later marked the check as unpaid and proceeded to close my account, without providing a clear, written, or legally adequate explanation. I did not receive timely notice specifying the precise reason for the hold nor identifying the applicable exception under Regulation CC ( Expedited Funds Availability Act ). 

According to Chase representatives, I was informed that the check could not be deposited because it was allegedly considered fraudulent, which is false. Chase stated that the issue was that the check did not bear my name and that they had been unable to locate XXXX XXXX. However, I personally went to a Chase branch together with XXXX XXXX XXXX and presented all requested documentation. At that time, I was informed by Chase personnel that XXXX XXXX presence was not necessary and that all procedures would be handled directly with me. 

Later, Chase claimed they had been unable to contact XXXX XXXX through his mobile phone provider. I verified directly with him that he is on a family plan with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and that he never received any calls from Chase. I provided Chase with his phone number : ( XXXX ) XXXX. 

Chase then stated that the check could not be deposited because it was not endorsed by me, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and only bore the endorsement of XXXX XXXX. Subsequently, I was informed that as of XX/XX/year>, Chase had issued a notice stating that checks payable to third parties could no longer be processed. I had no prior knowledge or notice of this alleged policy change. 

Afterward, I attempted to cash the same check through another company called XXXX XXXX. They initially processed the check but later contacted me to inform me that the check had already been processed by Chase and that they could not proceed. As a result, they requested reimbursement of the funds, which I fully repaid, and I have proof of payment. 

As a consequence of Chases actions, I have suffered financial harm, including the inability to access funds, exposure to potential fees or overdrafts, and personal financial loss, as the check belonged to my friend and I had to reimburse him the full amount. I believe that Chase failed to comply with its obligations regarding transparency, proper notice, and funds availability, as required under federal consumer financial protection laws. 

RELIEF REQUESTED I respectfully request that JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . : 1. Provide me with a written and detailed explanation of the legal and technical reasons why the check was held and ultimately not paid.

2. Conduct a full review of my case and, if no valid exception applies, release the corresponding funds.

3. Remove any fees, penalties, or negative impacts on my account resulting from this situation.

4. Implement measures to prevent similar situations from occurring in the future.

5. Reopen my bank account that was closed as a result of this matter. 

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS ATTACHED Image of the check ( front and back ) Communications received from Chase Bank statement showing the hold or reversal Proof of reimbursement and clearance ( paid in full ) from XXXX XXXX, including receipt Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, CA XXXX Phone : XXXX Email : XXXX XXXX

Date XXXX Amount XXXX withdrawal denial By : Branch manager on grounds of the '' business day '' rule without full disclosure of said rule during withdrawal XXXX. 

1.The violation : Regulation DD which requires banks to provide '' clear and conspicuous '' disclosure of all terms and conditions that affect a consumer 's ability to use their account. 
If a bank aggregates weekend withdrawals into one daily limit but describes the limit as " daily '' then that is unfair, deceptive, or abusive discretionary acts and or or practices.

Chase banking financial institutions have failed in providing full disclosure of daily withdrawal times and scheduling of withdrawal windows. that although withdrawal windows are understood to be daily withdrawals windows ; that Saturday and Sunday are all considered to be Monday. 
Noting that this particular branch is widely aware of my dire situation and need to access account on today, a business day, I cant grasp why the teller nor bank manager wouldn't or didn't share that vital piece of info considering activity and nature of my individual situation. 

2.fund access after identity verification.

Premises : Under the Dodd-Frank Act, an act is " unfair '' if it causes substantial injury to consumers that they can not avoid. 
on XXXX between the hours of XXXX and XXXX I visited the location @ XXXX and XXXX, XXXX Florida. 
the goal was to make a withdrawal so that I may go and retrieve a new identification card for the purposes of full account access.

Chase banking financial Institution has failed in areas of transparency by repeatedly locking me out of my account despite branch management protocols and procedures of identification being established and satisfied on numerous occasions via security question presented by branch manager, as well as numerous avenues of transparency on my behalf as account owner. 

Evidence of this can be logically understood and have been presented via dates of " authorized daily withdrawals ''. 

3.Inconsistent ID policy. 
allowing withdrawals without ID on some days but requiring it on others constitutes arbitrary policy enforcement. 

under the Know your customer ( KYC ) & BSA ( bank secrecy act ) banks are required by federal law to verify identity of certain transactions. 
HOWEVER, if they have an " emergency withdrawal " policy that is applied inconsistently, I.e not informing the consumer about daily withdrawal window being lumped in on weekends.

I expect this matter to be reviewed independently and resolved without further delay. 

I am raising a new issue concerning JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s failure to maintain and provide core account records and decision documentation relating to my credit card account. 

Over multiple requests, Chase has issued conclusions about my account history, internal decisions, and account status changes without producing the underlying records that support those conclusions.
