Chases inability or refusal to produce these records raises serious concerns about record retention, internal controls, and the reliability of its account management systems. Conclusions without records are not evidence ; they are assertions. 

This issue stands independently of any prior complaints. It concerns Chases document retention and consumer access obligations, not third-party involvement or authorization

text:
Re : Complaint Against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . 
Product : Checking Account / Debit Card Issue : Fraud / Unauthorized Transactions Reference Number : XXXX Dear Sir or Madam : I submit this complaint to request review and intervention regarding JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s denial of four unauthorized ATM withdrawals totaling $1600.00 from my checking account. Chase denied these claims solely because a correct PIN was used, despite extensive evidence of criminal activity, incapacitation, lack of authorization, and my timely reporting. 

I. Background On XX/XX/year>, while traveling in XXXX, XXXX, I was drugged and robbed. My debit card, mobile phones, credit cards, and identification were stolen. I regained consciousness the following morning and did not have possession of my debit card or phone when the disputed ATM withdrawals occurred. 

XXXX. Reporting and Investigation Despite delays caused by the theft of my phones and compromise of my email account, I notified JPMorgan Chase Bank of the fraudulent activity by XX/XX/year>. I filed a criminal report by XX/XX/year>. Chase initially issued provisional credit. 
On or around XX/XX/year>, Chase reversed four ATM withdrawals while ruling other disputed transactions from the same incident in my favor. 

XXXX. Chases Denial Rationale On XX/XX/year>, I spoke with a Claims agent named XXXX and escalated to a Floor Supervisor named XXXX. XXXX XXXX stated that Chase policy treats correct PIN usage as dispositive and does not consider such transactions unauthorized. 
This rationale fails to account for coercion, incapacitation, or criminal extraction of PIN information, all of which negate actual authorization. 

IV. Transactions at Issue XX/XX/year> $530.00 XX/XX/year> $180.00 XX/XX/year> $470.00 XX/XX/year> $470.00 Total : $1600.00 V. Regulation XXXX Concerns Under Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.2 ( m ), unauthorized electronic fund transfers are those made without actual authority. Regulation E does not equate correct PIN usage with authorization, particularly where the PIN is obtained through criminal means.

12 C.F.R. 1005.6 and 1005.11 require timely notice protections and a reasonable investigation. Chase relied on automated decisioning and a categorical PIN-based policy, rather than a good-faith investigation of the facts.

VI. Requested Resolution I request that the CFPB require JPMorgan Chase Bank to reverse its denial, reimburse $1600.00, and review its internal policies for compliance with Regulation E.

text:
We are a small business that provides XXXX XXXX  in XXXX, Indiana. 

Beginning in XX/XX/XXXX, our business checking account at JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . began experiencing recurring ACH debits from an entity labeled XXXX XXXX XXXX. These withdrawals were later determined to be fraudulent. The company name used in the ACH debits does not provide health insurance services in our state, which was confirmed when we contacted the company directly.

We did not initially detect the fraud because the ACH debits appeared to resemble legitimate employee health insurance premium payments. We only became aware of the issue when our employees health insurance was canceled for non-payment, which caused significant disruption and harm to our business and our employees medical coverage. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, we contacted Chase to report the fraud, dispute the charges, and submit a complaint that Chase failed to identify or prevent repeated high-dollar ACH debits from a company that does not service our state. At that time, a Chase representative informed us that the fraudulent charges dated back to XX/XX/XXXX, and disputes were submitted accordingly. 

Shortly after, we received notifications that the majority of the disputes were denied on the basis that Chase does not reimburse unauthorized transactions beyond 30 days for business accounts, despite these being recurring unauthorized debits. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, we contacted Chase again to request information about the fraudulent ACH originator so that we could file a police report and submit a formal complaint. During this call, a different Chase representative contradicted the prior information and stated that the fraudulent charges only dated back to XX/XX/XXXX. We then submitted additional disputes for those earlier charges. 

During this call, the representative stated that Chase would not provide any identifying information about the ACH originator, which prevented us from filing a meaningful police report. When we requested to file a formal complaint regarding the contradictory information and denial of disputes, the representative attempted to discourage us from doing so, stating that nothing would change. We were eventually transferred to a supervisor, where a formal complaint was made. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, another ACH debit from the same fraudulent originator was processed, despite the prior disputes and complaints. At this point, we conducted a full review of our statements and discovered that the fraudulent debits actually dated back to XX/XX/XXXX, significantly earlier than any information previously provided by Chase representatives. 

We then visited a local Chase branch to formally complain that : Chase failed to detect or prevent repeated unauthorized ACH debits Chase provided contradictory and inaccurate information across multiple representatives Chase processed a new fraudulent debit after repeated disputes and complaints Chase refused to provide information necessary for a police report Chase made it excessively difficult to file a formal complaint The in-branch representative expressed surprise that another debit had been allowed after so many disputes and escalations and consulted supervisors to confirm Chases policies. We were informed that Chase only guarantees reimbursement for the past 30 days, and that recovery beyond that is uncertain despite the recurring nature of the fraud. 

We signed additional disputes for the most recent charges. At this point, we have multiple overlapping disputes due to inconsistent information provided by Chase. We were also informed that we would need to pay a $30.00 fee to block future ACH debits from this originator. 

Due to the financial harm, operational disruption, and loss of trust, we withdrew funds from our accounts and are in the process of closing both our business and personal accounts with Chase. 

This situation caused significant financial hardship, disruption to our operations, and direct harm to our employees health coverage. We are submitting this complaint because Chase failed to adequately protect our account, failed to provide accurate information, processed additional fraudulent transactions after disputes, and refused to provide information necessary for law enforcement reporting.

text:
CFPB, I am filing this complaint due to repeated, inconsistent, and unclear information provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding overdraft protection, overdraft practices, and the circumstances under which transactions would be paid, declined, or assessed fees on my checking account. 

Over an extended period of time, I have received conflicting explanations from Chase representatives about whether overdraft protection was available, whether my account was enrolled in any overdraft services, whether transactions would be authorized or declined when insufficient funds were present, and whether overdraft fees could be assessed. These explanations were inconsistent with each other and were not resolved through clear written confirmation. 

At no point was I provided with a clear, consistent, and affirmative explanation of my overdraft status or a meaningful opportunity to make an informed decision regarding overdraft coverage. Instead, I was left with contradictory information that made it impossible to reasonably understand how my account would function in real-world transactions. 

This inconsistency is particularly concerning because overdraft practices involve fees, consumer choice, and regulatory opt-in requirements. When a financial institution provides conflicting or unclear information about fee-triggering services, it undermines a consumers ability to manage their account responsibly and raises serious concerns about unfair or deceptive practices. 

Despite the availability of overdraft options in Chases internal policies, those options were not communicated to me in a clear, uniform, or reliable manner. Different representatives provided different explanations, and no definitive written confirmation of my overdraft enrollment status or opt-in history was offered until I raised concerns myself. 

As a consumer, I should not have to piece together critical account terms from inconsistent verbal explanations. Banks have an obligation to ensure that information regarding overdraft services and fees is accurate, consistent, and non-misleading, especially when those services can result in financial harm. 

The lack of consistent information directly affected my ability to understand : Whether overdraft protection was available or active Whether Chase would authorize or decline transactions when funds were insufficient Whether overdraft fees could be assessed Whether any opt-in or opt-out was on record for my account This confusion is not hypothetical ; it has real financial consequences. A consumer can not meaningfully consent to overdraft practices when the information provided is inconsistent or unclear.

text:
I am filing this complaint because my prior dispute with Chase was closed ( XXXX ) without a fair or independent review, and Chase failed to protect me as a consumer when I initially requested help while cognitively impaired.

At the time of the original charge, I contacted Chase and disclosed that I had a brain injury with cognitive impairment and asked for assistance to have the charge refunded. Chase did not take appropriate action or provide reasonable assistance at that time.

Later, a Chase representative issued a refund, which posted to my account. Approximately 30 days later, Chase reversed the credit, removing the refunded funds from my account. This reversal occurred without new evidence, without additional investigation, and without justification. This action caused financial harm.

Chase now claims that a merchant processor statute of limitations prevents recovery. That position is unacceptable because the statute issue would not have existed had Chase fulfilled its duty to assist me when I first contacted them and requested help while cognitively impaired. The failure to act initially is entirely Chases responsibility. 

This matter was previously submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, but the complaint appears to have been closed solely based on Chases response, without any determination of fairness, consumer protection, or consideration of my XXXX. I did not receive a final determination or explanation from the CFPB. 

I am requesting : Clarification on whether a company response alone is sufficient to close a complaint without independent review. 

Supervisory review of Chases handling of this dispute, including the improper reversal of a posted refund. 

Review of Chases failure to provide reasonable assistance when I disclosed a brain injury and requested help.

A determination as to whether Chases actions violated consumer protection standards.

Chase should not be permitted to reverse a validly issued refund weeks later and then avoid accountability by citing a statute of limitations that arose only because of its own failure to act. This file should not have been closed without proper review.

On XX/XX/year>, a direct deposit of $3700.00 was transmitted to JPMorgan Chase. Due to a data entry error, the funds were routed to a valid account number belonging to a third party, rather than my own. 

I contacted JPMorgan Chase immediately on XX/XX/XXXX to report the error. Chase representatives have since acknowledged that the account number belongs to another individual and that this stranger received my funds. 

Despite my immediate notification on the day of the transfer, Chase refused to freeze the erroneous funds or reverse the transaction. They claimed they could " do nothing '' without a recall from the sender, even though I provided proof of the error before the funds had settled. By strictly adhering to this bureaucratic requirement and refusing to act on my immediate fraud/error report, Chase knowingly allowed a third party to retain funds that do not belong to them. 

Chase had the opportunity and the notification required to correct this error or place a hold on the funds to prevent their withdrawal. Instead, their inaction has facilitated the unjust enrichment of another customer at my expense, resulting in the total loss of my $3700.00 wages. 

I have attached my phone call log on XX/XX/year> and XX/XX/year> to prove my timely action to reach out to Chase and my HR in the attachment section.

CFPB Complaint Against Chase 1. Overview of the Issue : I am filing this complaint to report that Chase Bank has contacted me directly despite my having legal representation. I have informed Chase multiple times that I am represented by my attorney, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, and have provided his contact information. Despite this, Chase representatives have continued to reach out and attempt to discuss my account directly.

2. Details of the Contact : On multiple occasions, Chase called me and, when I informed them that I was represented by counsel, they tried to continue the conversation. One representative even mentioned that any verbal authorization would only apply to that specific call and that written authorization would be needed for future contact. 
Additionally, I have been attempting to obtain my payment history from Chase, but the relevant section is locked. This is a violation of my rights under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), as I am entitled to access my payment history and related documents. 

3. Attorney Contact Information : Attorney Name : XXXX XXXX, XXXX. 
Phone Number : XXXX Email Address : XXXX Attorney Address : XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX, XXXX, Connecticut, XXXX 4. Specific Violations : Failure to Cease Direct Contact : Chase continued to contact me directly even after being informed of my legal representation, violating the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ).

Inaccessibility of Payment History : The locked section preventing me from accessing my payment history is a violation of RESPA, which guarantees borrowers the right to obtain their payment records and related documents.

5. Requested Resolution : I request that Chase immediately cease all direct communication with me and only communicate through my attorney. 
I request that Chase unlock my payment history and provide all relevant documents promptly. 
I also request an investigation into this matter to ensure compliance with RESPA and the FDCPA.

After checkout, XXXX system split the order into two transactions without my request. One portion ( $4100.00 ) was approved under the 0 % APR plan ; the second portion ( $2300.00 ) was declined due to system issues. text:
On XX/XX/XXXX XXXX charges were made on my Grifols Plasma Donor Card. XXXX of them were ATM withdrawals at a gas station in XXXXXXXX XXXX I've never visited, the $2.00 ATM fees for each of these transactions, and then $18.00 at another corner store all within the span of minutes starting at XXXX XXXX. I received no notifications of this and only found out on XX/XX/XXXX after I checked my account on a lark and found that my card was nearly empty. 

I work as a teacher in a district that operates on a four-day week, and I donate plasma every XXXX  at the XXXX XXXXXXXX donation center in XXXXXXXX XXXX. I knew these charges were fraudulent as the card never left my wallet. I called the account holder, JPMorgan Chase, to have the card cut off while I secured a new one from the donation center. I reported the amounts, sent information to their fraud department, and assumed that everything would be over in a week or so. I received a call from their fraud department later that week where they asked a few questions, told me they would continue the investigation, and not even XXXX minutes after the call ended I got an email stating that the investigation was closed and that the charges were all valid. 

After this I filed a police report with the XXXX Police Department afterwards believing that the lack of a report made them think I was trying to con them out of over $400.00. I was assigned an XXXX and it was through him that I then realized that the bank never told me what times the withdrawals took place. Once I discovered they took place at night I remembered that I had gone to work that Friday because we had the XXXX XXXX XXXX earlier that week. I told the police this error and they followed through, and within a couple of days the XXXX in charge of the investigation had evidence that someone indeed had used my card and that they had cloned it. I gathered my time cards, a screenshot of a XXXX Maps page showing the distance between where I was at XXXXXXXX XXXX  and where the ATM was, the police report, screenshots of my correspondence with the police, and even the payment data from the donation center as evidence that someone had cloned my card and compromised my account. 

Chase, on their end, has since issued multiple denials to my claims and has cycled through a repeating list of excuses as to why charges I never made were valid. They have tried to say that the PIN was entered without mistakes as proof that they were valid, but cloning a card grants access to the PIN. They tried to say I used the card afterwards as proof but I never said the card left my person and explained in the original report I didn't know the transactions even happened until a week later. XXXX of their latest excuses was that the location of the ATM was within the general area of where I was at the time, which lead to the aforementioned map screenshot showing that it would take nearly an hour in impossibly low traffic on a Friday night in XXXXXXXX XXXX of all places to make such a trip one-way let alone a round trip. 

Above all, these denials are like them saying I'm lying about the card being compromised when I already filed a police report. The fines alone for lying to the police would be far greater than the money stolen from me. 

After the first call from Chase 's fraud department it took until XXXX for them to finally answer my requests for a call back, and I missed the call because my phone was in another room while I was cleaning. It then took until today, XX/XX/XXXX, to get another call back and they hung up on the second ring. As before not even a full XXXX minutes later they said the investigation was concluded and they cycled back to the PIN number excuse again. 

Throughout this entire ordeal Chase has shuffled me over to a customer service line that can't directly contact them and have either lied to me about when the fraud department was open, claiming they aren't open on weekends when the second call came on a Saturday, to another stating that the police would have to make an arrest for them to approve the return of my stolen money. The officer in charge of the investigation has been nothing but helpful and they won't even talk to him upon request or by him emailing them. The number they call from only shuffles me back to customer service and then this starts all over again. I am now at XXXX months trying to get what is a month 's worth of donations back. The card doesn't leave my home safe anymore because I don't trust the bank to honor any disputes. 

I have provided more than enough evidence showing that my card was compromised, yet JPMorgan Chase won't speak with me in good faith, they dodge me at every turn, won't follow up on anything I provide, and the emails their fraud department sends all read the same as if they're being pumped out by AI. Everything is just pointed back to a customer service line that ranges from regretful in tone to outright disrespectful. 

I know these are all tactics meant to wear me down and give up but I can't just look away from over $400.00 being stolen and nothing being done about it. I'm a teacher, and anyone who knows the profession will tell you that we don't make much as it is. That money could pay for medical expenses, groceries, car maintenance, but JPMorgan Chase, a banking entity worth multiple billions of dollars, can't be bothered to just let few hundred go back to the person it was stolen from.

I just want my money back.

Each month, I paid my purchase balances in full. Despite this, Chase repeatedly charged purchase interest at approximately XXXX % APR, even though no purchase balance should have remained after my payments. 

Every time this occurred : I contacted Chase Chase representatives acknowledged the charge as an error The purchase interest was reversed Before making payments, I explicitly called Chase every month and asked exactly how much I needed to pay to avoid purchase interest. This explanation is : XXXX. Contradictory to what multiple Chase representatives told me previously XXXX. Inconsistent with how balance transfers work at other major credit card issuers XXXX. Not disclosed clearly or accurately at the time the promotional offer was accepted XXXX. Incompatible with federal payment allocation rules, which require payments to be applied first to higher-APR balances If purchases are paid in full, Chase can not continue charging purchase interest solely because a promotional balance transfer exists, while simultaneously claiming that payments are applied first to the highest APR balance. Had this policy been clearly disclosed, I would never have used this promotional offer, as it effectively penalizes normal card usage and defeats the purpose of a balance transfer promotion.

text:
I am filing a complaint regarding JPMorgan Chase Banks improper handling and misdirection of my settlement funds in Florida. 

I was the original named payee on a settlement check. Due to a temporary lack of valid identification, Chase permitted me to endorse the check for deposit into my sisters Chase account. Chase accepted the check, processed it, and cleared the funds. The account was later restricted pending verification of my identity as the original payee. 

Despite acknowledging that I am the original payee and lawful owner of the settlement proceeds, Chase subsequently reissued the settlement check naming my sister as the payee. This was done without my authorization, without any assignment of rights, and without a court order. 

Under Floridas Uniform Commercial Code, including Florida Statutes 673.2011 and 673.2031, negotiation or transfer of an instrument does not transfer ownership of settlement proceeds or authorize substitution of the named payee absent a valid assignment. Under Florida Statute 673.3011, I remain the person entitled to enforce the instrument.

Additionally, Florida Statute 674.4011 permits a bank to charge or pay an item only if it is properly payable. Reissuing a settlement check to an unauthorized payee does not meet this standard.

I did not assign or transfer my settlement rights to my sister. Chases actions constitute misdirection of settlement funds and improper handling of a negotiable instrument under Florida law. 

I am requesting that Chase cancel any improperly reissued check naming an unauthorized payee and reissue the settlement check correctly in my name as the original payee. I am also requesting written confirmation of corrective action. 
Chases error has caused unnecessary delay and improper diversion of my funds. I am requesting regulatory assistance to ensure this matter is resolved in compliance with Florida law.

I am submitting a complaint regarding Chase Banks handling of a credit card dispute related to an airline charge where the service provided was materially different from what was purchased due to a mechanical issue with the aircraft. 

The original itinerary was scheduled to arrive at approximately XXXX XXXX. Due to a mechanical failure, the airline rerouted the trip to include XXXX connecting flights, resulting in arrival at approximately XXXX XXXX  the same day, a delay of roughly XXXX hours. This disruption was not weather-related and was not within my control. 

Although I ultimately arrived at my destination, the transportation provided was not equivalent to the service purchased and constitutes a significant delay and material itinerary change. Chase initially issued a provisional credit, which I reasonably relied upon, but reversed the credit approximately XXXX months later without adequate explanation. 

I believe Chase failed to properly apply the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z in evaluating a materially altered service and in the timing and handling of the dispute. Mechanical issues are the responsibility of the airline and should not result in financial liability to the consumer. 

I am requesting a senior-level re-review of this dispute and reinstatement of the credit. 

My original dispute to XXXX : This was the worst airline experience of my life and a complete failure of XXXX duty of care. 

I purchased a direct XXXX XXXX flight ( XXXX XXXX  ). On the day of travel, that flight was canceled. XXXX then instructed us to take a XXXX XXXX  alternative, which was also later canceled, leaving us stranded with no viable XXXXprovided option. 

With no assistance, no timely rebooking, and no clear path home, we were forced out of pure desperation, to book a separate XXXX XXXX  connecting flight through Georgia ourselves, arriving at XXXX XXXX, more than XXXX hours late and having to call out of work for the next day. 

This was not a weather delay or a minor schedule change. XXXX failed to transport us on the service purchased and failed to provide a workable alternative. 

Compounding this, when we called XXXX the day of travel, we were explicitly told we would receive both a refund and flight credit due to the cancellations. Relying on that assurance, we made decisions under pressure. That representation was later contradicted, which constitutes material misrepresentation, a basis on which similar DOT complaints are routinely resolved in favor of the customer.

I promptly reported the issue to Chase and filed an ATM deposit error claim. Chase issued a provisional credit, then later reversed it, stating that its internal system could not locate the missing funds. 

I requested documentation and an explanation of the investigation, including how the ATM was balanced and the basis for denying the claim. Chase stated that it is not required to provide any information and refused to share documentation. 

A police incident report was filed to document the missing funds. I dispute the adequacy of Chases investigation and request reconsideration and a written explanation as required under Regulation E. Police report number XXXX XXXX Police station.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to file a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding the prolonged and unresolved withholding of my funds following the closure of my account. 

In late XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX, Chase closed my bank account without providing any clear or reasonable explanation. After the account was closed, Chase continued to hold my funds and repeatedly delayed returning the money to me. 

Since the closure, I have contacted Chase many times, both in person at branch locations and through customer service phone calls. During these interactions, I was repeatedly told that my case was under investigation. In several instances, Chase representatives falsely claimed that a check had already been mailed to me, which later proved to be untrue. Different representatives gave me completely inconsistent answers, and no one could provide a clear timeline or resolution. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a check related only to my payment account. Two days later, on XX/XX/XXXX, a Chase banker informed me in person that if I could provide proof showing that the funds in my savings account were transferred from my mother, Chase would be able to release the remaining funds. I then provided official bank PDF documentation proving that the money was transferred from my mothers account at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  in XXXX to my Chase savings account. 

Despite fully complying with this request, as of XX/XX/XXXX, I still have not received the funds from my Chase savings account in the amount of $10000.00. 

I am a XXXX, and this is not a small amount of money for me. I urgently need these funds to pay my rent and tuition. Living and studying in New York comes with extremely high costs, and Chases continued withholding of my money has caused serious and ongoing financial hardship. This situation is unacceptable. 

While Chases account terms state that the bank has the right to investigate transactions, this does not grant Chase the authority to withhold customer funds indefinitely and without justification. Nearly three years have passed, and I have still not received money that rightfully belongs to me. Additionally, Chases customer terms treat account closure and fund investigations as separate matters, and they should not be improperly combined to justify indefinite delays.

Chase has failed to provide a clear deadline, meaningful updates, or any assurance regarding the safety and return of my funds. I respectfully request assistance from the CFPB in investigating this matter and helping me recover my money.

Thank you for your time and attention to my case.

text:
NEW CFPB FILING Based on Post-Response Judicial Action Demonstrating That Chases Prior CFPB Responses Were Incomplete and Materially Inaccurate as Reflected by the Judicial Record CFPB COMPLAINT Basis for New Complaint Post-Final Judicial Action Since JPMorgan Chase Banks prior CFPB final responses, new judicial action has occurred. 

Chase and its counsel, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, filed a Motion to Set Aside an in rem judgment, acknowledging that a judgment had been signed before the summary judgment hearing occurred. The Court entered an Order setting that motion for hearing.

This judicial action occurred after Chase represented to CFPB that the foreclosure posture, accounting, and legal proceedings were valid and final. The court-signed Set-for-Hearing Order establishes that Chases prior CFPB responses were premature and inconsistent with the actual litigation posture, as reflected by the judicial record. 

Material Contradictions Established by the Court Record and Attachments 1. Chases Judgment and Foreclosure Representations Were Not Final In its CFPB responses, Chase asserted that : foreclosure proceedings were valid, no attorney errors existed, and fees and charges were normal.

However, Chases own counsel later moved to set aside a judgment that had been signed before the required hearing, and the Court set that issue for hearing.

This directly contradicts Chases CFPB representations that the foreclosure posture was settled and error-free. 

2. Lender-Placed Insurance Timeline Is Internally Inconsistent and Unreconcilable Chase states that it began providing lender-placed insurance in XX/XX/XXXX. 

Chase further states that : notices dated XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX warned of insufficient wind coverage, and a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX states that wind coverage became effective XX/XX/XXXX. 

However, the XX/XX/XXXX letter is not a lack-of-coverage warning. 
It is a purchase notice, reflecting that wind insurance had already been placed and charged. 

Chase then : purchased another wind policy in XX/XX/XXXX, backdated that policy to XX/XX/XXXX, while maintaining the XXXX policy. 

This sequence demonstrates that : wind insurance was not provided during a significant portion of the XXXX XXXX hurricane season, and Chase attempted to retroactively cure the lapse after hurricane season was nearly over. 

XXXX. Wind Policies Are Labeled as Renewals, Not Initial Placements The Assurant wind policies provided by Chase are labeled as renewals, not initial placements. 

A renewal presupposes prior valid coverage, directly contradicting Chases claim that wind insurance was newly placed due to borrower non-compliance. 

Chases insurance procurement narrative is therefore internally irreconcilable. 

4. Escrow Charges Are Derived From Invalid Insurance Procurement Escrow statements show : charges for multiple lender-placed policies, overlapping coverage periods, and retroactive effective dates.

Chases escrow accounting relies on insurance policies that : were procured using corrupted or conflicting property address data, and can not be retroactively underwritten for prior risk periods. 

Because insurance underwriting and pricing are location-specific and time-fixed, escrow charges derived from such policies can not be presumed accurate or lawful. 

XXXX. Address Responsibility Was Misstated Chase asserted that the borrower refused to provide documentation to update the property address. 

This misallocates responsibility. 

Chases own correspondence and court filings show : conflicting property addresses ( XXXX vs. XXXX ), and acknowledgment by XXXX counsel of address defects in the litigation record. 

Maintaining accurate collateral data is a servicer obligation, particularly where lender-placed insurance and escrow charges are imposed. 

XXXX. Accounting Defects Are Now Before the Court In addition to the Set-Aside-for-Hearing Order, the Defendant filed a Motion to Enforce Accounting and Insurance Prerequisites to Foreclosure , seeking only to require Chase to demonstrate : lawful insurance procurement for the correct insured property, and a fully reconciled escrow accounting. 

That motion does not address foreclosure merits. 
It reflects that Chases claimed default is not supported by reliable servicing data. 

7. RESPA Notice of Error Communications Were Mischaracterized Chase stated that the borrower declined assistance calls and later requested that calls stop.

The request was for Chase to coordinate communications through the Executive Office to avoid violating RESPA Notice of Error requirements, not to refuse assistance.

Chases CFPB framing mischaracterizes compliance coordination as borrower obstruction.

Why CFPB Review Is Required Now Chase submitted three CFPB final responses asserting that : the judgment posture was settled, insurance placement was compliant, and foreclosure proceedings contained no attorney error.

After those representations, Chase and its counsel sought judicial relief to correct the judgment itself, and the Court set that issue for hearing.

This post-response judicial action demonstrates that Chases CFPB submissions were incomplete, premature, and contradicted by the judicial record.

Wrongful removal of account access and unfair banking practices by JPMorgan Chase Bank Narrative : I am filing this complaint because JPMorgan Chase Bank wrongfully removed my access to my bank and business accounts without a valid court order, legal document, or my consent, causing significant financial harm and disruption to both personal and business finances. 

On XX/XX/2025, Chase unilaterally removed me as an authorized owner/signatory on accounts that I legally owned and had access to. At no point did I sign a valid document authorizing removal of my access, nor was there a court order granting Chase authority to make that change. The removal was based on documentation the bank stated it received, but which I did not authorize and which is part of an ongoing dispute. After the removal of my access, I have c
alled Chase multiple times and have gone into a Chase branch in person multiple times to resolve the situation, requesting explanations, reinstatement of access, and a review of the documents that Chase claims justified its actions. Despite these attempts including providing requested information and asking to speak to escalated support or a bank officer Chase has not provided a satisfactory explanation, restored my access, or corrected the account status.

Because of Chases actions, I have been unable to access funds needed to operate my business, pay bills, and manage daily financial responsibilities. This has caused financial harm, including inability to make necessary payments and disruption to business operations. 

I believe Chases actions are unfair and improper because the bank relied on disputed or improper documentation, failed to notify me properly, and failed to follow its own policies and the account agreement governing account changes. Chases actions effectively sided with another party in an ongoing business/marital ownership dispute without legal authority to do so.

Resolution sought : 1. A formal explanation from Chase detailing the specific documents, dates, and internal approvals used to remove my access.

2. Restoration of my account access or correction of the account status recognizing my rightful ownership/authorization.

3. Any appropriate compensation for documented financial harm directly resulting from these actions.

I have attached supporting documents, including communications with Chase and records of my attempts to resolve this matter.

text:
Supplemental Clarification and Requested Relief JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . has issued multiple responses asserting that it completed its investigation of disputed transactions across my credit card accounts and made final determinations regarding responsibility. However, Chases responses and customer correspondence demonstrate that only a limited subset of the disputed transactions I submitted were actually investigated, while the majority of disputed charges were never opened, reviewed, or adjudicated on a transaction-by-transaction basis. 

Despite this partial review, Chase has represented in CFPB responses and customer letters that its investigation was complete and that it determined responsibility for all disputed transactions. Chase has not explained why only certain transactions were investigated, how it selected which disputes to review, or how it can certify completion of an investigation when a substantial portion of the disputed charges were not examined. 

Chases responses rely heavily on generalized statements that services were received or made available, merchant representations that transactions were valid, and references to deposit activity or prior transaction history. These assertions are not accompanied by documentation describing transaction-level investigative steps, such as analysis of authorization, billing accuracy, device or wallet usage, merchant classification, or compliance considerations. XXXX on merchant XXXX XXXX XXXX  account activity does not substitute for an independent billing-error investigation. 

Chase has also applied inconsistent dispute classifications ( including fraud, duplicate, misrepresentation, and validation ) to transactions involving the same merchants, overlapping timeframes, and similar transaction patterns, resulting in selective credit reversals and selective designation of certain credits as permanent while denying others. Temporary credits were reversed while disputes and CFPB complaints remained pending, and four credit card accounts were closed during this period before Chase completed or documented a full, transaction-level investigation of all disputed charges submitted.

In multiple instances, Chase denied disputed transactions on the basis that a significant amount of time has passed and that the merchant was not willing to credit, without identifying when notice of the dispute was received, the applicable billing statement cycle, or why the disputes were accepted and adjudicated if they were allegedly untimely. A merchants refusal to issue a refund does not constitute a transaction-level investigation or demonstrate compliance with Regulation Z.

Additionally, Chases CFPB responses characterize the disputed transactions as online casino or gambling activity and rely on that characterization to deny disputes, yet do not explain how this determination was made, what standards were applied, or how this characterization was reconciled with the merchant classification and coding used at the time the transactions were processed. Chase has not documented whether merchant category codes were reviewed, whether those codes accurately reflected gambling activity, or how any inconsistency between transaction coding and later dispute determinations was addressed.

Taken together, Chases responses reflect selective dispute handling, inconsistent outcomes for identical merchant activity, reversal of provisional credits during active CFPB complaints, reliance on labels and merchant representations without documented analysis, unresolved merchant classification issues, and adverse account actions taken without completion of a comprehensive, documented investigation.

Because Chase has acknowledged investigating only a portion of the disputed transactions submitted, while simultaneously asserting that its review was complete and issuing final determinations, I request that the Bureau evaluate whether Chases dispute-resolution practices in this matter comply with Regulation Z ( 12 CFR 1026.13 ). Where a transaction-level investigation can not be demonstrated, correction of the account is the appropriate remedy.

text:
Product : Auto loan Company : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . ( Chase Auto ) Complaint Narrative I am submitting this complaint regarding improper servicing of my auto loan following a total loss and the resulting inaccurate credit reporting. 

Timeline of events : On XX/XX/XXXX, my vehicle was declared a total loss and was surrendered to my insurance company. 
On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, the insurance company issued payment for the vehicles market value. 
The GAP claim was initiated in LATE XXXX / EARLY XX/XX/XXXX because I was required to first obtain final refund documentation related to extended warranty and ancillary products from the original dealership. 
The dealership significantly delayed issuing these refunds and the associated paperwork, despite my repeated follow-ups. 
I initiated the GAP claim immediately after the lender confirmed receipt of the extended warranty refund and all required documentation became available. 
I did not delay the GAP claim voluntarily ; the timing was dictated by documentation requirements outside of my control. 
On early XX/XX/XXXX, I initiated a GAP insurance claim immediately after all final insurance payments were received. 
On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, I received written confirmation from the GAP administrator stating that the remaining loan balance was paid in full and that I had no remaining financial obligation. 

GAP Approval and Subsequent Conflicting Information from Lender After receiving written confirmation from the GAP insurance provider indicating that, based on the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet, the remaining loan balance would be fully satisfied and that I would not owe any further payments to the lender, I reasonably understood the matter to be resolved. 
Relying on this information, I believed the loan was effectively closed, with the remaining balance to be paid directly by the GAP provider. 

Subsequently, after contacting the lender for clarification, I was informed that I was still considered to have an outstanding balance, as the lender had not yet received the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet and certain GAP-related refunds. 
I was instructed by the lender to request that the GAP insurance provider send the required documentation directly to Chase. 

I contacted the GAP insurance provider and requested that the GAP Worksheet be sent to my loan holder. On [ XX/XX/XXXX ], I received written notification from the GAP provider stating that they were unable to successfully reach Chase and suggested arranging a conference call. 

Due to repeated difficulties coordinating communication between the lender and the GAP provider, I contacted Chase again and was advised that I could submit the required document via fax. 

I submitted the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet via fax in XXXX XXXX, using the submission method provided by the lender. 

In early XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Chase to confirm receipt. At that time, Chase confirmed that all required refunds had been received, but stated that the GAP Worksheet submission was still under review. 

As of today, despite submitting the required documentation in XXXX and following up multiple times, no updates or account changes have been made, and the case remains pending without resolution. 

Despite the above, my account was not placed in an insurance or GAP pending status. Instead, it was later reported as charged off, while the insurance and GAP resolution process was ongoing. 

Additional Context / Consumer Position I reasonably relied on written confirmation from the GAP administrator stating that the loan was settled in full. Based on this official documentation, I had a good-faith belief that no further payments were due. 

At no point did Chase provide clear written instructions advising me to continue making payments while the insurance and GAP claim were pending, nor did Chase communicate that failure to do so could result in a charge-off.

Given the extensive delays and repeated communication failures between the lender and the GAP provider, I have a reasonable belief that even if I had continued making payments during this period, there was no guarantee that those payments would have been properly credited or refunded. The remaining loan balance at the time was relatively small after my insurance paid vehicle 's market value ( remaining balance was approximately $2200.00 ), yet the account was handled as if I owed a substantially larger sum, ultimately resulting in a charge-off being reported. 
The charge-off and resulting credit reporting appear to be the direct result of servicing and processing failures, not a refusal to pay or abandonment of the loan. 

Additionally, the original dealership significantly delayed the process, as all required refunds related to extended warranty and ancillary products had to be processed through them before the GAP claim could be initiated. Despite my repeated follow-ups, these delays were outside of my control and directly impacted the timing of the GAP claim.

Impact on Consumer Throughout this entire process, I made consistent and good-faith efforts to communicate with the lender and kept them informed of all developments, including the total loss determination, insurance payments, and the status of the GAP claim. Despite this, my account continued to be marked as delinquent, with each payment reported as missed, without consideration of the ongoing insurance and GAP resolution.

As a result of this handling, the account was ultimately charged off. At the time, due to my lack of prior experience with auto loans, total loss claims, and U.S. credit reporting practices, I mistakenly believed that a charge-off indicated that the loan had been settled or closed. Once I later learned that a charge-off represents a serious negative credit event, I immediately began taking steps to dispute the status and provide the requested documentation. 
As a result of the above, my credit report reflects a charge-off that has caused significant and disproportionate damage to my credit profile, despite the loan being covered by insurance and GAP.

This was my first auto loan and first total loss, and I had no prior experience with insurance and GAP claim processing. Based on the vehicle being surrendered, insurance payments being issued to the lender, and written confirmation from the GAP administrator that the loan was settled, I held a reasonable belief that no further payments were required while the claims were being finalized.

Resolution Requested I am requesting the following : 1. Expedited review and final resolution of the insurance and GAP payoff ; 2. A written explanation detailing why my account was charged off while a total loss insurance and GAP claim were pending ; 3. Correction of all credit bureau reporting related to this account to reflect the accurate status following insurance and GAP payoff ; 4. Written confirmation of the current loan balance, which should reflect $0.00 if all payments have been properly applied. 

Account Information Lender : Chase Auto

text:
On XX/XX/XXXX, an ACH payroll payment in the amount of $2700.00 was processed from my business account at JPMorgan Chase Bank to a XXXX Bank account. On XX/XX/XXXX, a second ACH payroll payment in the amount of $970.00 was processed to the same XXXX account. At the time these transactions were processed, I was unaware that this account belonged to a scammer. The total amount of ACH payroll funds fraudulently transferred to the scammers XXXX account was $3600.00. 

Prior to these transactions, I received an email that appeared to be from XXXX of my employees requesting an update to her direct deposit information. Believing this request to be legitimate, I updated the employees banking information. I also requested a voided check for verification, which was submitted by the scammer. Based on this information, I processed payroll accordingly. 

In early XX/XX/XXXX, my employee contacted me on XXXX separate occasions to inquire about her XXXX payroll, as she had not received payment. At that point, I forwarded her the email requesting the bank update, which I had believed she sent, in order to confirm where the ACH payroll had been deposited. She confirmed that she did not send the request and that her banking information had not changed. Based on this confirmation, it became clear that the email was fraudulent and sent by an individual impersonating my employee. 

My employee then contacted XXXX Bank to determine whether the fraudulent account had been opened using her personal identifying information and to verify that she had not authorized or participated in the account activity in any way. XXXX opened a formal fraud case and provided a reference number. XXXX advised that I should contact my business bank, JPMorgan Chase, provide the case number, and request that Chase submit a Hold Harmless or Indemnity Letter in order to recover the funds. 

Upon discovering the fraud, I immediately contacted JPMorgan Chase Banks business banking department to report the incident and request assistance. Despite multiple attempts, Chase has not provided meaningful support and has continued to decline to initiate the required indemnity documentation. I also visited XXXX local Chase branch locations in person, where bankers attempted to assist me and contacted the business unit on my behalf. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, while sitting in XXXX of the bankers offices, I called XXXX Bank on speakerphone so that the banker could hear the conversation directly. During this call, the XXXX representative again confirmed, in real time, that JPMorgan Chase must initiate a Hold Harmless or Indemnity Letter in order for the funds to be returned. This information was clearly communicated and heard by both myself and the Chase banker. 

Despite this direct confirmation, the response from Chases business banking department has remained consistently inadequate. I was repeatedly told that we do not do that and it is not in our policies, without meaningful explanation, documentation, or escalation. The local branch bankers expressed frustration and indicated that they had limited authority and limited insight into centralized business processes, highlighting a significant disconnect between branch-level staff and the business banking unit. 

XXXX Bank has consistently maintained that the only pathway for recovery is for JPMorgan Chase to initiate the required indemnity documentation and coordinate directly with them. Chases business department is fully aware of this requirement. However, despite repeated requests and verification, Chase has refused to contact XXXX or initiate the necessary documentation. This refusal has prevented any attempt at recovery of the stolen funds. 

I have made repeated good-faith efforts to resolve this matter through Chases business banking department and through in-person branch visits. To date, these efforts have been unsuccessful. Chases failure to cooperate in the standard interbank recovery process has left me without meaningful recourse, despite timely reporting and clear evidence of fraud. 

As a small business owner, I relied on JPMorgan Chase Bank to provide reasonable support and advocacy in response to a documented payroll fraud and impersonation scheme. Instead, I have encountered repeated resistance, lack of transparency, and a failure to engage in the necessary procedures to attempt recovery of my funds. 

This complaint is being submitted due to JPMorgan Chase Banks continued refusal to initiate the required indemnity process with XXXX and their failure to provide adequate assistance in resolving this matter, resulting in significant financial harm to my business. Approximately 3.5 months ago, my mobile device and subsequently, my online banking profile, were both taken over by an identity thief. 

The thief opened a new credit card, added it to a digital wallet, and proceeded to make numerous fraudulent transactions. To avoid being restricted by a credit line, the thief continually transferred funds from my existing checking account to pay each transaction. 

In total, the thief transferred five figures worth of value, across multiple online banking profiles. However, whereas the other bank ( s ) automatically detected, froze, and/or reversed the fraud, Chase took no action until I appeared in person to a retail branch and began the dispute process.

After 2.5 months of near-weekly in-person visits and calls, I received confirmation in writing from Chase that, as expected, I was NOT RESPONSIBLE for the credit card opened and used to initiate the original fraudulent transactions. 

HOWEVER, when attempting to use this proof toward a refund, Chase demonstrated no regard for wanting to assist in the recovery process. Despite having my branch manager assist, the credit department insisted that I take my business to checking, who in turn insisted that I take my business to credit, so on and so on.

At this time we have exhausted the list of new departments we have been forwarded to, with none willing to take ownership or even demonstrate commonsense customer care. I have followed every standard procedure and despite promises from Chase over the months that I would receive timely callbacks from support agents, I never have. 

Provided the complete and utter failure from Chase to treat my post-innocence claims with any dignity or respect, I see no other recourse than to pursue all external options available to me. This includes escalating to governmental agencies, news media, social media, and even legal authorities. Until such time that Chase responds with something other than, file another claim, I see no reason why it should not be made known how meaningless Chase 's reputation is in the face of malicious identity theft.

On XX/XX/year>, I booked a hotel reservation through XXXX for XXXX XXXX in Washington, DC ( Booking ID XXXX ) in the amount of $440.00. I booked it for 4 nights, with a check-in date of XX/XX/year>. The room was advertised as having two queen beds. I was travelling with my family, including my XXXX child, and we specifically required two beds. That room configuration was the sole reason I made the booking. 

Immediately after receiving the confirmation email within minutes, I noticed that the reservation did not mention two queen beds. I contacted the hotel immediately and was informed that the reservation was for a single king bed room. This did not match what was advertised at the time of purchase. Because we were travelling as a family and could not use a room with only one bed, I requested cancellation from XXXX. They informed me that they would request a fee waiver and that it should be fine. Believing this was a clear error, I expected the reservation to be cancelled. This was not a voluntary cancellation due to a change of plans ; it was cancelled because the room provided did not match what was advertised and purchased. 

Since the correct room type was unavailable, I made a separate, new reservation for a different room with two beds from the same hotel. This hotel seemed to be a nice and affordable place, so we wanted to stay here. That second reservation was a completely separate booking, and I paid for it independently. The disputed $440.00 charge relates only to the cancelled reservation, which was never used. 

However, it later became clear that XXXX did not cancel the room. I contacted them many times again, and they blamed the hotel for not cooperating. 

I then spoke directly with the hotel, and it turned out they had already responded to XXXX and had issued a refund. The hotel invoice shows that the original charge was fully reversed and that the balance was XXXX. Despite this, XXXX did not pass the refund through to my credit card account. 

I disputed the charge with JPMorgan Chase Bank. JPMorgan Chase denied the dispute and stated that the transaction was valid, but each time I contacted them, I was given a different explanation. On one occasion, they stated that I had used the room. On another occasion, they said the dispute had been filed under the wrong reason and that it would be changed to service not provided as described. On another occasion, they stated it was a non-refundable purchase. Even if the reservation was non-refundable, that does not mean the merchant can provide a materially different room type than what was advertised at the time of booking. Plus, the hotel refunded them anyway. 

I contacted JPMorgan Chase multiple times, but in the end, they denied my dispute without providing a clear and consistent explanation. The bank also suggested that because I stayed at the hotel, the charge was valid. However, my stay was under a separate reservation that I paid for independently. The cancelled reservation associated with the disputed charge was never used. 

I requested clarification from JPMorgan Chase regarding why XXXX did not pass through the refund it received from the hotel and asked for documentation supporting the banks conclusion under the Fair Credit Billing Act. JPMorgan Chase did not provide the requested documentation and stated that it would not respond further. 

I believe the investigation conducted by JPMorgan Chase was incomplete because it did not properly address the documented refund or the fact that the disputed reservation was cancelled immediately and never used. 

I have attached the list of documents as a zip file that I sent to the Bank.

I am filing this complaint because Chase has failed to meet the standards of fairness and transparency mandated by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). According to the CFPBs own mission, their role is to 'ensure that consumer financial markets are fair, transparent, and competitive ' and to 'reinforce compliance with federal consumer financial laws. By freezing my funds for over 30 days, providing conflicting information through over 30 different representatives, and failing to provide a clear legal or factual basis for the freeze, Chase has engaged in practices that are both unfair and abusive to me as a consumer. 

Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) & Regulation E : The CFPB administers the EFTA, which requires financial institutions to conduct a 'prompt, reasonable, and timely investigation ' when a consumer contacts them about an account error or issue. Chase has failed to provide a timely resolution or a valid reason for denying me access to my own money.

Expedited Funds Availability Act ( Regulation CC ) : This law governs the holds banks place on deposits. Chase has exceeded reasonable holding periods without providing the legally required transparency as to why these funds are being withheld. 

The CFPB has previously taken enforcement action against institutions for 'unlawfully freezing accounts with faulty fraud detection programs and giving consumers little recourse. ' I am requesting that the CFPB exercise its enforcement authority to compel Chase to release my funds immediately and provide a full, transparent accounting of their actions.

I am a long-standing Chase customer with an excellent payment history and zero prior late payments. Recently, I added a new bank account to the Chase platform to facilitate payments. The reviewer indicated the explanation was satisfactory. 
Basis for Complaint & Adverse Impact : Despite my proactive resolution, Chase proceeded to drastically reduce my credit limits to nearly my current balances. This action effectively " maxes out '' my credit utilization ratio, which will cause immediate and severe damage to my credit score.

Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), implemented by Regulation B, creditors are prohibited from taking adverse action that is discriminatory or lacks a legitimate business justification when a consumer has met their obligations. Furthermore, as a resident of California, I am protected under the Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and California Civil Code Section 1785.25, which requires creditors to report accurate information. By forcing a high utilization rate through an arbitrary limit reduction following a technical glitch I corrected, Chase is effectively penalizing me for an error I did not cause.

This requirement was not clearly disclosed to me at the time of account opening. I was explicitly told that direct deposit alone would waive the Monthly Service Fee.

Chase has full access to the complete account history and is in the best position to determine the total number of Monthly Service Fees assessed since XX/XX/XXXX.

This assumption arises from a life event ( divorce/separation ). I am already an owner and responsible for the property and am attempting to remove my former spouse from the mortgage obligation. The loan is performing, current, and financially supportable by me alone. 
Industry practice is that a mortgage assumption in a life-event situation typically requires approximately XXXX  days for underwriting and final determination. However, Chases process has extended far beyond any reasonable or customary timeframe. 
In my case, the assumption process has now exceeded 6 months, and I have been informed it will exceed XXXX. I have been in escalation for months and it has not done anything to speed the process. 
The following issues are occurring : 1. Excessive Response Delays Each time Chase requests information or clarification, the turnaround time for review is approximately three months regardless of how minor the request is. A single underwriting question effectively restarts another 90-day waiting period even if the question is irrelevant. In my case they asked for Income from my real estate license in 2024. I did not have the license until XXXX of that year, disclosed all the information we sent and verififed with my provided tax return.. 
2. Lack of Case Review or Escalation There appears to be no assigned underwriter or decision-maker reviewing the file. Customer service representatives can not answer scenario-specific questions and can not move the file forward. Any matter outside a scripted checklist can not be addressed.

3. Failure to Provide a Reasonable Process Mortgage assumptions inherently involve non-standard situations. I am a business owner ; the property is an investment property generating steady income for over 6 years and is guaranteed from the Section 8 program. Chases process does not allow for any underwriting review that has any understanding of the property or my file in particular. As a result, the process is effectively stalled without a path to completion. If they now have everything there will be another minimum of 60 days for underwriting. 
4. Potential Consumer Harm The delay places the borrower in legal and financial limbo and prevents resolution of a divorce-related obligation. It also exposes the borrower to unnecessary risk and expense. The length and structure of this process functionally discourage the assumption of an existing loan. I have suffered loss of sleep and the inability to move on with my life as well as countless hours of filing, following up and refiling for 9 months straight.

5. Concern Regarding Constructive Denial The practical effect of these delays is to make assumption infeasible and to pressure borrowers into refinancing into a new mortgage at a higher interest rate. The bank processes new mortgages in a fraction of this time, yet assumption requests remain unresolved for up to a year or longer. I am not confident using the same processes we will ever be able to close and might not be granted the assumption because of any erroneous reasons. The property generates income from XXXX rentals and I have more than enough income to support all my financial obligations. There is no reason for the length of time for this assumption.

XXXX To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of a refinance application with JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . for my property located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, GA XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX and related file XXXX ). The refinance began in XX/XX/XXXX and concluded with a denial dated XX/XX/XXXX, after I had already been advanced to the final stages of closing. 

This matter began with my original refinance request for $40000.00 in XX/XX/XXXX. Chase evaluated the application and, citing debt-to-income constraints and related underwriting considerations, declined the $40000.00 request. On XX/XX/XXXX, Chase issued a formal Notice of Counteroffer reducing the loan amount to $32000.00 under a conventional XXXX-year fixed structure at XXXX %. I accepted this counteroffer in good faith. 

The reduction from $40000.00 to $32000.00 was based on underwriting concerns that were explicitly referenced at that time. I proceeded under the revised structure exactly as offered by Chase. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, Chase issued a Closing Disclosure reflecting the $32000.00 loan amount and scheduled a closing date of XX/XX/XXXX, with disbursement on XX/XX/XXXX. At this stage, I reasonably understood the loan to be approved under the revised terms. Insurance and escrow coordination had progressed in reliance on the scheduled closing. 

Near the end of the process, I asked a narrow question : whether adding my father as a XXXX could potentially restore the original $8000.00 reduction and allow the loan to return closer to the initial $40000.00 request. I was advised that this could be feasible. My father was interviewed by Chase. 

Subsequently, I was informed that because my father does not occupy the property, he could not be used in the manner discussed. I was then told that the refinance would need to be restarted as a new application and that I would be required to submit an additional $650.00 fee, even though $650.00 had already been paid in connection with the original refinance file. I was also informed that restarting the process could extend the timeline by an additional XXXX to XXXX months. 

I objected to paying a second $650.00 fee for a file that had already progressed to Closing Disclosure stage. After raising this concern, I was advised that the fee would be waived and the file would continue without requiring an additional deposit. 

However, the file was then restructured to include my parents as borrowers. A new Loan Estimate was issued under XXXX XXXX. XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. Additional credit inquiries occurred, and my credit scorXXXX dropped from XXXX ( as reflected in XX/XX/XXXX disclosures ) to XXXX ( as reflected in the XX/XX/XXXX credit disclosure ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, a Lock-In Agreement was issued listing XXXX borrowers. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a Statement of Credit Denial citing : Excessive obligations in relation to eligible income Property not occupied by all borrowers Cash out proceeds exceeds guidelines The denial reasons directly mirror the underwriting concerns that originally led Chase to reduce the loan from $40000.00 to $32000.00 in the XX/XX/XXXX counteroffer. Those concerns had already been addressed through the revised $32000.00 structure that progressed to Closing Disclosure. 

My complaint is not that the original $40000.00 request was declined. I accepted the counteroffer. My concern is that after issuing a formal counteroffer, advancing the file to Closing Disclosure stage, scheduling closing dates, coordinating insurance, and allowing reliance on the approved $32000.00 structure, Chase permitted late-stage structural modifications without clearly advising that doing so would trigger a full re-underwrite and potentially void prior approval. 

As a result : The loan was materially restructured after Closing Disclosure. 
Additional credit inquiries were generated. 
My credit score decreased significantly during the process. 
The file was ultimately denied under reasons substantially similar to those that had already been accounted for in the original counteroffer. 
I experienced financial and credit harm after relying on the banks revised structure and scheduled closing. 

I believe this reflects a failure to clearly disclose underwriting risk associated with late-stage structural changes and a breakdown in procedural handling after issuance of revised disclosures and a scheduled closing date. 

Requested Resolution : I respectfully request : A formal review of the handling of this refinance file and the late-stage re-underwrite. 

Clarification of why the file was permitted to reach Closing Disclosure and lock stage before final underwriting confirmation under the revised borrower structure. 

Review and remediation of the credit impact resulting from repeated inquiries tied to the reopened file. 

Consideration of reinstating the refinance under the previously accepted $32000.00 sole-borrower structure without additional fees or unnecessary credit pulls. 

I am seeking a fair procedural review and reasonable remediation for the credit and financial impact resulting from the late-stage restructuring and denial. 

Respectfully, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, GA

I moved to XXXX for work. During a trip to XXXX, I used my Chase credit card for ordinary travel-related spending. After that, Chase apparently flagged the activity as suspicious and blocked not only my credit card, but also my checking accounts. As a result, I lost access to my accounts, my online banking, and my card. 

Since then, I have called Chase customer service multiple times in an effort to verify my identity, restore access, and resolve the issue. Despite these repeated attempts, Chase has not provided an effective solution. I remain locked out of my accounts. 

What is even more troubling is that Chase has continued charging approximately $300.00 per month on my Freedom credit card ( see the attached screenshot! ), even though the card is blocked and I can not access the account online or use the card. Because I have been denied access, I can not properly review, dispute, or manage these charges. This situation is unacceptable and has caused significant financial harm and distress. 

I believe Chase has failed to provide adequate customer support, failed to restore legitimate account access after repeated contact, and allowed ongoing charges to accumulate on an account that I can not access or control. 

I am requesting that CFPB require JPMorgan Chase to : Immediately restore my access to my checking and credit card accounts, or provide a clear and workable process for doing so. 

Investigate the recurring monthly charges of approximately $300.00 on my Freedom credit card. 

Reverse any improper fees or charges assessed while I was locked out of my accounts. 

Provide a full explanation of why my accounts were blocked and why the issue was not resolved after multiple customer service calls. 

Ensure that this matter is handled promptly by someone with authority to fix it.

Chase may contact me at the email address I provide in this complaint. If this matter is not resolved promptly, I will pursue all available legal remedies.

text:
This complaint concerns two materially altered business checks totaling $14000.00 that were stolen from the mail, washed, and fraudulently deposited via mobile deposit into personal accounts unrelated to the intended vendor. These items were not properly payable under UCC 4-401.

The fraud followed the exact same pattern as four other stolen checks from the same incident, which Chase reimbursed after submission of affidavits. However, these two checks the largest amounts remain unresolved without explanation. 

My company, XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, reported this fraud to Chase on XX/XX/XXXX, after discovering that two checks mailed to a long-standing vendor had been stolen from the mail, altered ( check washed ), and deposited into accounts belonging to unrelated individuals. 

The checks involved are : Check # XXXX $8000.00 Check # XXXX $6500.00 Both checks were materially altered and deposited via mobile deposit into personal accounts. My business does not write checks to individuals except payroll, and none of my vendors deposit checks via mobile deposit. These transactions were clearly inconsistent with my companys normal payment practices and contained multiple indicators of alteration, including altered payee names and formatting irregularities. 

Importantly, four other checks stolen and altered in the same fraud incident were reimbursed by Chase after submission of affidavits, confirming the identical pattern of check washing fraud. However, these two checks remain unresolved without a clear explanation from the bank. 

Under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC 4-401 ), a bank may charge a customers account only for items that are properly payable. A check that has been materially altered is not properly payable, and banks must exercise ordinary care when processing items for payment. 

In this case, the bank failed to exercise ordinary care by honoring items with obvious material alterations and mismatched endorsements, and by allowing them to be deposited via mobile deposit into personal accounts inconsistent with the account holders payment history. 

Additionally, one of the fraudulent checks was deposited into a Chase account, meaning the bank had direct access to the receiving account and the ability to review the suspicious transaction internally. 

After months of communication, Chase requested signed affidavits, which I promptly submitted. On XX/XX/XXXX, Chase informed me that the affidavits were not on file despite prior submission, and I immediately resubmitted them that same day. Since then, I have sent multiple follow-up requests asking for confirmation of receipt and a timeline for resolution but have received no meaningful response. 

Because the vendor had not received payment due to these altered checks, my company was forced to reissue the funds, leaving our small business carrying the financial loss while the banks investigation remains unresolved. 

This situation raises serious concerns regarding whether the bank exercised ordinary care as required under UCC 4-103 before honoring these materially altered items.

I am requesting that Chase : Reevaluate the claim under UCC 4-401 regarding altered items that were not properly payable. 
Provide documentation explaining how the bank determined that ordinary care was exercised before honoring these altered checks. 
Reimburse the full amount of $14000.00 so that my company is not left responsible for losses caused by check washing fraud. 

By honoring materially altered checks that were not properly payable and inconsistent with my account history, the bank failed to exercise ordinary care as required under UCC 4-401 and 4-103. 

I would also appreciate a written explanation of the procedures used to determine that ordinary care was exercised before these materially altered items were honored.

I am submitting this complaint regarding the denial of a Trip Delay Reimbursement claim associated with my Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX credit card. 
I purchased international airfare for my family using my Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX card for an XXXX itinerary traveling from New York ( XXXX ) to XXXX, XXXX via XXXX. The airfare was charged to my Chase card, and documentation confirming the charge and ticket purchase was provided to the benefits administrator. 

On XX/XX/2025, our departure from New York ( XXXX ) to XXXX was delayed by approximately three hours due to inclement weather. As a direct result of this weather delay, we missed our originally scheduled connecting flight from XXXX to XXXX. 
XXXX automatically rebooked our family on the next available flight from XXXX to XXXX, which departed approximately twenty-four hours later than our originally scheduled connection. This resulted in an extended travel delay and additional expenses. 

The missed connection in XXXX was not an independent event. It was directly caused by the inclement weather delay of the departing flight from New York. Because the covered hazard prevented us from continuing our itinerary as scheduled and required rebooking approximately XXXX hours later, the delay meets the criteria for Trip XXXX reimbursement under the XXXX XXXX XXXX benefits guide. 

Under the Trip Delay Reimbursement benefit associated with the XXXX XXXX XXXX card, delays caused by inclement weather are listed as a covered hazard. The trip also qualifies as a covered trip because the airfare was purchased using the covered Chase credit card. 

Despite providing documentation confirming both ( 1 ) payment of the airfare with the covered Chase card and ( 2 ) a delay caused by inclement weather, my claim was denied. The denial letter stated that the covered card was not used to pay for the fare and that the delay was not caused by a covered hazard.

Both of these statements are inconsistent with the documentation that was submitted. The airfare was charged to my Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX card, and the itinerary disruption was caused by inclement weather, which is explicitly listed as a covered hazard under the Trip Delay benefit.
