text:
On XX/XX/year>, I attempted to withdraw $500.00 from an ATM located at the XXXX XXXX XXXX. The ATM approved the transaction and debited my account $500.00 ( including the ATM fee ), but no cash was dispensed from the machine. 

I immediately reported the issue to my bank and filed a dispute for ATM cash not received. My bank later denied the claim based solely on the ATM transaction log showing dispense success and completion code XXXX. 

However, the documents provided to me only show the electronic journal entry from the ATM. They do not include the ATM cash reconciliation report, cassette counts, reject bin or retract bin counts, or confirmation that the ATM balanced after the transaction. 

A successful authorization and dispense entry in the electronic journal does not prove that the customer actually received the cash. Proper investigation of an ATM cash dispense dispute typically requires reconciliation of the machines cash totals and internal bins to confirm whether the ATM was over or balanced. 

Because I did not receive the $500.00, I am requesting that the bank reopen the investigation and obtain the ATM cash reconciliation documentation from the ATM operator, including cassette counts, reject/retract bin counts, and any relevant camera review, to verify whether the ATM balanced correctly after the transaction.

On XX/XX/year>, I experienced a scam outside of XXXX XXXX 's outside of XXXX XXXX area of XXXX. Three individuals approached me requesting a $20.00 donation using a fabricated story involving the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

During this interaction, these individuals physically took possession of my phone under false pretenses and manipulated my device without my informed consent. While my phone was out of my control, they executed XXXX unauthorized XXXX XXXX transactions totaling $2000.00 ( $1000.00 each ) through my Chase debit account.

I did not knowingly authorize these transactions. My intent was, at most, to donate $20.00. These transactions were completed through deception, coercion, and misuse of my device, and therefore do not meet the definition of authorized electronic fund transfer under Regulation E.

I reported the fraud to Chase within minutes of the incident and promptly filed a police report. I also obtained identifying information, including the suspect 's vehicle license plate.

Despite this, Chase denied my claim, asserting that the transactions were authorized. This determination fails to account for the fact that : - My device was physically controlled by another individual at the time of the transaction - The transactions were induced through fraud, coercion, and deception - I did not provide informed or legitimate authorization Under Regulation E, unauthorized electronic fund transfers include transactions initiated without the consumer 's authority. Consent obtained through deception or while the consumer is deprived of control over their device should not be considered valid authorization. 

In addition, I work closely with youth in my professional role, and I am increasingly concerned about the rise of scams like this targeting everyday consumers. Situations like mine highlight the broader issue of consumer vulnerability, especially in public settings where individuals may be pressured or manipulated.

Chase publicly advertises zero liability protection for unauthorized transactions. However, in practice, when I experienced this situation and reported it immediately, I did not receive meaningful support. I was told that Chase only handles financial investigations and not criminal matters, which does not align with the level of consumer protection implied in their messagingparticularly given their position as one of the largest financial institutions. 

This situation has caused significant financial and emotional distress. I am seeking regulatory assistance to ensure my rights are upheld and that financial institutions are held accountable in protecting consumers from increasingly sophisticated scams.

text:
I am submitting a formal complaint regarding the presentation of the XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX co-branded Chase credit card during the checkout process on XXXX website. 

While booking a reservation under a time-sensitive early booking rate, I was presented with a credit card offer embedded directly within the checkout flow. This offer displayed my actual reservation price, applied a $350.00 XXXX credit, and presented a reduced total cost for the stay. The positioning, timing, and framing of this offer created a clear and reasonable net impression that applying for and being approved for the card would allow me to realize that reduced price in connection with this specific transaction. 

Relying on that representation, I applied for the credit card and was approved. 

Immediately afterward, I attempted to use the new card to complete my reservation but was unable to do so. Upon contacting Chase, I was informed that the card could not be used until the physical card is received. While I was offered expedited shipping, there remains a delay of several business days. During that time, I am at risk of losing the time-sensitive booking rate or being forced to rebook at a higher price. 

At no point during the booking or application process was it clearly and conspicuously disclosed that : The card could not be used immediately upon approval The advertised credit would not apply to the current transaction Applying for the card could result in the loss of time-sensitive pricing The only disclosure providedthat credits may post on separate statementsdoes not address these material limitations. 

This creates a misleading net impression by directly associating a specific transaction price with a benefit that can not be realized within that transaction. The integration of this offer within a live checkout flow, particularly one involving time-sensitive pricing, introduces urgency that reinforces that impression. 

When I contacted XXXX, I was advised to either book at a higher refundable rate, use an alternate payment method and attempt to rebook later, or wait for the card and assume the risk of increased pricing. I also requested that the reservation be held for a short period until I receive the card, which was declined. 

As a result, I have been placed in a position where I must either forfeit the early booking rate or incur additional cost, despite having applied for the credit product based on how it was presented within the transaction flow. 

This raises concerns regarding a deceptive act or practice under UDAAP standards, as the material limitations of the offer were not clearly disclosed and the overall presentation is likely to mislead a reasonable consumer. 

I am requesting the following resolution : That XXXX honor the original early booking rate once I am able to use the newly issued credit card, or That an equivalent adjustment or credit be provided to offset the difference I also request that this matter be reviewed for compliance, particularly regarding the presentation of co-branded financial products within time-sensitive purchase flows. 

I expect a prompt and substantive response. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text:
I am filing this complaint regarding a XXXX transaction that I reported as fraud, which my bank JP Morgan has incorrectly classified as an authorized transaction. The transaction occurred after I was the victim of a social engineering scam in which an individual impersonated a trusted family member and requested money urgently. Based on this impersonation and the belief that I was communicating with someone I knew and trusted, I sent the funds through XXXX. 

Shortly after the transaction, I realized that I had been deceived and that the individual was not my family member but an impersonator. I immediately contacted my bank to report the incident as fraud and initiated a claim. I also provided supporting information, including the phone number used by the scammer, the name associated with the XXXX account, and any available communications demonstrating the impersonation. 

Despite these circumstances, I was informed by a representative at JP Morgan that the transaction was considered authorized because I initiated it, and that the bank only covers certain types of fraud. However, this determination fails to consider that I did not authorize the transfer to the actual recipient. My authorization was based on deception and impersonation, which constitutes social engineering fraud. 

Under Regulation E, unauthorized electronic fund transfers include situations where a consumer is induced to initiate a transfer through fraudulent misrepresentation. In this case, I did not knowingly or willingly authorize payment to the individual who ultimately received the funds. My consent was obtained through deception, and therefore the transfer should be considered unauthorized under the intent and consumer protection principles of Regulation E.

I reported the incident promptly, cooperated fully with the banks investigation, and am now requesting a proper review of this claim under Regulation E guidelines. I am seeking reimbursement of the fraudulent transfer and a reconsideration of the banks classification of this transaction as authorized.

This situation involved impersonation, social engineering, and deception, and I believe the bank has not adequately applied consumer protections designed to address these types of scams. 

Regulatory guidance and consumer protection principles increasingly recognize that social engineering scams are a common form of fraud and that consumers should be protected when they are manipulated into authorizing transactions under false pretenses. Denying claims solely because the consumer technically initiated the transfer fails to account for the deceptive circumstances under which authorization was obtained.

This complaint concerns systemic violations of the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ) following a written billing error notice submitted on XX/XX/XXXX and received by the creditor no later than XX/XX/XXXX. 

The creditor failed to comply with core requirements of Regulation Z, including failure to properly acknowledge and failure to conduct a reasonable investigation under 1026.13 ( f ). Instead of performing a transaction-level billing error investigation, the creditor improperly applied a fraud-based framework, materially altering the scope of review and excluding a substantial portion of disputed transactions. 

The resulting determination is not based on a complete or reliable record. 

The creditor reported approximately $200000.00 in disputed transactions for one account, while the same account statements reflect over $420000.00 in credits and over $420000.00 in rebills processed through the account. These figures can not be reconciled. The creditors conclusions are therefore not tied to the actual account ledger. 

Across accounts, the creditor provides multiple conflicting figuresincluding a total fraud amount of $260000.00 and combined dispute totals exceeding $ XXXX are not mathematically related and can not be derived from one another or from statement-level activity. 

This demonstrates a critical failure : the creditor can not produce a single, consistent, and reconcilable dataset underlying its conclusions. 

Additionally, a substantial portion of the transactions identified in the written billing error noticeestimated at approximately 80 % were never opened, logged, or investigated. Disputes were opened only after the 30-day acknowledgment period had expired, which does not cure the initial violation. 

The creditor further claims specific financial adjustments, including a $4400.00 write-off and a $540.00 merchant credit, yet no corresponding ledger entries exist to support these figures. 

At its core, this is not a transaction-level dispute. It is a process integrity failure. 

If the creditor can not reconcile its own numbers to the account ledger, then the investigation can not meet the standard of a reasonable investigation under Regulation Z. Any determination derived from non-reconcilable and internally inconsistent data is inherently unreliable.

I received a call on Friday XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX PST. The caller ID said Chase Bank and the phone number on the caller ID was XXXX. The person on the line was a man, I think his name was XXXX. I bank with Chase so getting a call from Chase is not unusual. He told me that someone had tried to open a new Chase account under my phone number. He asked me to verify my address and phone number and that was it. He said that they closed this fraudulently created account but that I needed to talk with customer support at XXXX. He said the person who tried to open the second bank account with my information was also trying to send my money using XXXX. So he transferred me to another customer service agent. This time it was a woman and I don't remember her name. This is where I got really confused. 

She had me send " test '' payments using XXXX and XXXX. She said we are going to cancel these transactions after we're done, as they are just for verification. She had me send $490.00 via XXXX to a person named XXXX XXXX. She said XXXX was the placeholder name and number associated with management. It went through, but then was immediately cancelled by Chase. I received a legitimate email from Chase saying it had been cancelled. After we went through this process, I trusted her to go on to the next steps. Next she had me send two XXXX payments to XXXX XXXX at the number XXXX in order to verify these accounts are mine and then also to secure the accounts. I sent the two test payments in the amounts of $990.00 and $840.00. After sending the XXXX payments she told me that it would take 1-2 hours for them to be cancelled and credited back, after all of this my XXXX and XXXX accounts would now be fully secured. 

After an hour went by, I knew something was wrong. I called Chase immediately. I was told that money lost to scams cant be recovered. I told the agent the full story of what happened and how Chase had called ME. Someone presented as a representative of one of the largest financial institutions in the world called ME, and they initiated these transactions. Its not like I returned a call from a sketchy phone number. I answered a live call from Chase Bank. The agent advised that I file a claim with XXXX XXXX, see what happens and if I cant be paid back I should file a separate claim with Chase. I filed a claim with XXXX, they denied it because it was a user to user transaction and that I sent it myself. 

I called Chase back and filed a claim describing the entire story. I was told it would take 3-5 days to investigate. On that same call I was also told that I would receive a temporary credit in the amount I was claiming while the investigation was going on. This gave me some relief so I could at least stay above water while I waited to hear the results of the investigation. I never received this credit and I called multiple times asking why, the answer I kept getting is that it can take 3-5 days for that credit to be issued. 

Four business days went by and I called the claims department once again on XX/XX/XXXX and it was only then that I was told my claim was denied. They couldnt explain why I never received a temporary credit but it didnt matter because the claim was denied. They told me I had to contact the merchant. I told them there is no merchant, thats the point. I told them how I thought I was working with a Chase agent when I sent those XXXX. That agent said none of those notes were inputted with the original claim, which means six days went by where Chase didnt even have all of the information related to the claim. On this call I was escalated to a different department. I told the whole story again. The agent I spoke to seemed more understanding and totally grasped the situation. Finally I felt heard. 

However another week went by where I still hadnt received a temporary credit and I hadnt heard from anyone. Ultimately today, on XX/XX/XXXX, I was informed by letter that my claim was denied. The reason for the denial was again the fact that I participated in the scam. As far as I can tell no nuance of the story had been considered. On top of all this while waiting for the claim to be investigated I never received the temporary credit I was told I was get. Ive incurred 12 over draft feed for $34.00 after being taken for almost XXXX XXXX dollars. 

I have since called and texted the phone numbers I was scammed by. The XXXX number connects you to a phony customer service line, again, falsely saying they are Chase Bank. I imagine if you continue through the prompts it's another channel for them to take more money. I also texted the numbers for XXXX XXXX. I asked for my money back. They responded saying I needed to send $100.00 in order to release my funds. It was so upsetting. I didn't send them the $100.00. 

Tomorrow is XX/XX/XXXX and I cant pay my rent. I dont have a lot of money. I had to file for XXXX  XXXX last year. I am in the process of getting back on my feet and losing this money has derailed my progress. I was deceived while under the duress of being told, falsely, that my account had been compromised. Why isnt Chase upset that they are being impersonated and deceiving their customers? Why cant they see that my trust in them is why I followed the scammers instructions? I did not initiate this scam, I had no reason not to believe that Chase Bank was calling me, in earnest, to help me protect my account. 

All the dates I cite in the above complaint can be verified from my call history. I also intend to file a police report.

Chase Auto explicitly told me that I have 'no right to reinstate ' and is instead demanding a full payoff of approximately $9000.00. 

Under CGS 36a-785, Connecticut residents have a statutory right to reinstate a retail installment contract by tendering the past-due amount. Chase Auto is intentionally misrepresenting my legal rights and blocking my ability to cure the default.

I sent a request to this credit card company to to provide me a form 1099-C form for this account. I have viewed my credit reports on ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and it shows that is credit card company is reporting this account as changed off account. text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of my Chase Sapphire Reserve XXXX XXXX claim ( Claim # XXXX ), administered through Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

I believe the benefit language is materially ambiguous and misleading to consumers, and the claim handling process has been inconsistent, unprofessional, and potentially deceptive. 

Background of the Claim During an international trip booked using my Chase Sapphire Reserve card, my baggage was lost. My documented losses exceeded $10000.00. The airline, XXXX, reimbursed me only $2000.00. 

Under the Chase Sapphire Reserve XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the policy states : > The Lost Luggage benefit provides reimbursement for the difference between the actual cash value ( replacement cost less depreciation ) and any reimbursement provided by the Common Carrier The policy further states : > Your Checked and Carry-on Baggage each have a maximum benefit up to XXXX XXXX ( $3000.00 ) dollars per Covered Person per Trip. 

Additionally, the policy states : > This benefit is payable on an excess basis over and above any amount due from any other valid or collectible insurance or any other form of reimbursement payable by those responsible for the loss. 

As an ordinary consumer reading this language, I reasonably understood the benefit to mean : XXXX. The airline reimbursement is applied first ; XXXX. Chase then reimburses the remaining uncompensated loss ; XXXX. Chase provides up to $3000.00 in excess coverage for the remaining loss. 

Since my uncompensated loss after XXXX payment still exceeded $7900.00, I reasonably believed I qualified for the full $3000.00 benefit. 

However, ChaseXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX the $3000.00 benefit itself by the airline reimbursement and issued only approximately $910.00. 

Misleading and Ambiguous Benefit Language The benefit guide never clearly states that reimbursements from the airline reduce the stated $3000.00 benefit limit itself. 

The policy does NOT state : - that the total combined recovery from all sources is capped at $3000.00 ; - that airline reimbursements erode the policy limit ; - or that the $3000.00 is an aggregate combined maximum including carrier payments. 

Instead, the policy repeatedly uses terms such as : - difference - excess basis- over and above which strongly imply to a reasonable consumer that Chase provides additional coverage after the carrier reimbursement is exhausted. 

The ambiguity is so significant that even Chase XXXX XXXX themselves could not consistently explain the coverage. 

Conflicting and Incorrect Information from Chase XXXX XXXX When I first contacted Chase XXXX regarding this claim, the XXXX informed me that based on my losses exceeding $10000.00, I would qualify for the full $3000.00 benefit after the airline reimbursement. 

Relying on this representation, I proceeded with the claim process. 

Later, after receiving only approximately $910.00, I contacted Chase XXXX again to question the calculation. During this conversation, a XXXX named XXXX reviewed the policy language regarding : - difference - and excess basis and specifically told me that my interpretation appeared reasonable and that the claim should undergo a Second Review. 

XXXX indicated that there appeared to be a discrepancy between the policy language and the actual payout determination. 

Following his guidance, I formally requested a XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>. 

Improper and Unprofessional Handling of the Second Review After submitting the Second Review request on XX/XX/XXXX, I called again to confirm the request had been properly submitted. I was told the review was in process and that I should expect a decision within XXXX business days. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again to check on the status because I had still received no update. During that call, I was told that the review was still pending and that I needed to continue waiting because the XXXX-business-day period had not yet elapsed. 

Today, when I called again for another update, I was suddenly informed by a different representative that the Second Review had actually already been completed and denied back on XX/XX/XXXX the very same day it was supposedly submitted. 

This means : - I was never informed of the denial ; - I received no written notice, email, or letter ; - multiple representatives subsequently spoke with me as though the review was still pending ; - and I was repeatedly instructed to continue waiting for a decision that had apparently already been made. 

This handling was highly confusing, contradictory, and unprofessional. 

As a consumer, I had no reliable way to understand the actual status of my claim because Chase Benefits representatives themselves appeared unable to access or communicate consistent information. 

Consumer Harm and Requested Review I believe consumers are being materially misled by : - ambiguous and unclear benefit language ; - inconsistent explanations from Chase XXXX XXXX ; - and representations that create the reasonable expectation of additional excess coverage up to $3000.00. 

If Chase/XXXX XXXX intends for airline reimbursements to reduce the policy limit itself, the benefit guide should clearly and explicitly disclose that limitation in plain language. 

Instead, the current wording creates the reasonable impression that the Chase benefit provides up to $3000.00 of additional reimbursement after carrier compensation. 

I am requesting CFPB review of : XXXX. The potentially misleading wording of the Chase Sapphire Reserve Lost Luggage benefit guide ; XXXX. The inconsistent and contradictory representations made by Chase XXXX XXXX ; XXXX. The mishandling and lack of communication regarding my Second Review request ; XXXX. Whether consumers are being adequately informed about how this benefit is actually calculated in practice. 

I am also requesting that XXXXFederal Insurance provide a clear written explanation identifying the exact policy language they rely upon to conclude that carrier reimbursements reduce the stated $3000.00 maximum benefit itself. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

However, a few days later, Chase restricted access to my account and subsequently froze it, citing suspected fraud. I immediately contacted the branch and was instructed to communicate with the Fraud Department.

Upon contacting the Fraud Department, I was informed that the account had been restricted for internal reasons and that the issuer of the check ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) would need to contact them directly. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, my account was permanently closed, and the deposited funds have remained withheld by Chase Bank since that time.

Following this confirmation, I was informed that Chase would issue and mail a check to my home address for the full amount. However, this never occurred.

Subsequently, I received a phone call from Chase advising me to visit a branch in person to retrieve the funds. After spending several hours at the branch, I was informed that the Fraud Department still retained control of the funds and that the branch was unable to issue a check to me.

Despite multiple phone calls and in-person visits, no resolution has been provided.

As a XXXX  newly relocated to the United States, I rely heavily on timely access to my funds to meet essential living expenses. The withheld amount was intended to cover my initial costs of living, including housing and basic monthly obligations.

The prolonged restriction of these funds has caused significant financial strain and disruption during a critical transition period.

Additionally, resolving this issue has required multiple in-person branch visits and extended phone calls, often exceeding one hour per interaction, with no resolution provided. This has resulted in a substantial and unreasonable burden on my time and professional responsibilities.

As of the date of this complaint, Chase continues to hold my funds without justification and without providing a clear resolution path.

On XX/XX/year> I deposited a check for $4500.00 via remote mobile deposit into my Chase XXXX checking account. I initially deposited the check without an endorsement signature, then signed it and deposited again believing the first attempt had not gone through. Chase 's system failed to reject the unendorsed check and failed to flag an obvious same-day duplicate deposit of the exact same check, same amount, same issuer. My account was credited $4500.00 twice totaling $9100.00 from one check. I was unaware this had occurred. 
On XX/XX/year> I was informed there may be an issue. I immediately called Chase the same day and then visited a Chase branch in person. A Chase employee reviewed my account on their system and explicitly told me everything was fine and there was nothing to worry about. I relied completely on that assurance.

That same night on XX/XX/year> Chase debited my account- $4500.00 as a MEMO DEBIT with no warning, no notice and no explanation, leaving my account overdrawn. Chase had multiple opportunities to catch this error and failed every time. Their branch employee told me everything was fine hours before taking my money overnight without any warning.

Reference Original Complaint : XXXX Chase Autos response is unsatisfactory and fails to address the core issues raised in my complaint. 

Chase is attempting to redirect responsibility entirely to XXXX XXXX XXXX. However, this is a lease agreement, and Chase Auto is the legal titleholder of the vehicle. The vehicle has been out of service for over 60 days following a charging-related incident, during which time XXXX retained possession and did not provide a timely resolution.

Only after escalation to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Arkansas Attorney General did XXXX provide a written response. That response did not determine a root cause, nor did it clearly accept or deny responsibility for the associated property damage. As a result, the underlying issue remains unresolved. 

XXXX has also taken the position that my residential solar-inverter system may fall under the category of a private power generator as referenced in the owners manual. This interpretation introduces uncertainty regarding acceptable charging conditions and raises concerns about the practical usability of the vehicle at my residence. XXXX has not provided clear, actionable guidance on this issue.

Chase Autos position does not resolve the central problem : the leased vehicle has been unavailable for an extended period and remains subject to unresolved questions regarding safe and approved operation. Despite this, Chase continues to require full lease payments.

Under the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a vehicle that is out of service for an extended period may qualify as nonconforming. At minimum, the circumstances raise serious concerns about the vehicles fitness for its intended use.

I respectfully request that the CFPB keep this complaint open and continue its review of Chase Autos handling of this matter, including their response to a prolonged loss of use and their refusal to provide any payment accommodation while the issue remains unresolved.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

The hotel itself approved an exception to the non refundable policy three times in writing on XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX XXXX and provided XXXX with a four step process to change my dates within a 12 hour window. XXXX failed to execute that process during the window and later admitted in writing on XX/XX/XXXX that modifications to the reservation were not possible and that changes to booking dates could not be processed within their system. In other words the merchant not the cardholder blocked use of the booking. 

On XX/XX/XXXX the hotel emailed me directly confirming that the exception had been extended as a special exception in consideration of my circumstances and stating that it had always been their intention to assist as much as possible within the limitations of the booking channels policies and procedures. They explained that the exception window could no longer be extended only because the original stay dates had passed. This confirms that the obstacle was XXXX or its intermediary not the hotel. 

XXXX meanwhile has put in writing that it is unable to process any refund while my chargeback is open but also stated that if the chargeback is formally withdrawn and the hotels stated conditions are fulfilled XXXX will proceed with the refund accordingly. XXXX requires me to withdraw my XXXX dispute provide an official withdrawal letter wait until payment returns to normal settled status and make a new non refundable replacement booking before it will consider refunding the original charge. This is a clear example of conditioning any remedy on my waiver of XXXX dispute rights and on a second non refundable purchase. 

I provided Chase with a complete evidentiary package including the hotels exception approvals XXXX system inability admission the hotels XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX emails and XXXX written demand that I withdraw my chargeback and rebook. On XX/XX/XXXX Chase issued a denial letter for Claim C XXXX XXXX stating that no billing error occurred and that the transaction is valid. The letter does not address any of the material evidence above. It simply states that the transaction is valid and that no billing error occurred.

I am a current XXXX credit card holder. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I received a promotional email from Chase Bank that was addressed to me by name. The offer was up to $900.00 for opening a new Chase Total Checking account and a new Chase Savings account and completing the qualifying activities. It included a specific offer code ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and was presented as a thank you to me as an existing Chase customer. 

Around that same time, I logged into the Chase Mobile app, applied for both accounts, and was approved. Chase opened a Chase Total Checking account ending in XXXX and a Chase Savings account ending in XXXX. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX roughly a week after the accounts were opened, I received an email from Chase titled " Account update. '' It said both accounts had been restricted to protect against potential fraud and may close soon. Both account numbers were referenced. The email stated, " Due to recent activity, or because we need more information from you, we have restricted your account ( s ) and may close it soon, '' and directed me to call XXXX. 

I called Chase. The representative told me that Chase 's terms and conditions allow the bank to terminate banking relationships at its discretion and that I would not be able to open new Chase deposit accounts. I was not given a specific reason for the closure. I was not told which database or flag triggered it. I was not given any opportunity to provide information or resolve whatever the underlying concern was. 

The part I find difficult to make sense of is the timing. The closure happened so quickly that I never had a chance to do anything with the accounts. I did not deposit any money. I did not set up direct deposit. I did not initiate a single transaction. I had no opportunity to complete any of the qualifying activities that would have earned the bonus. The accounts were effectively opened and closed before they were ever used. That tells me the closure could not have been based on actual account activity, because there was none. It strongly suggests a pre-existing internal flag or external consumer reporting check that Chase already had on me at the time it sent the solicitation. 

What has happened since the closure is also worth flagging. I am still receiving the same $900.00 promotional email from Chase, asking me to open the exact accounts I have just been told I am not allowed to open. Today, XXXX XXXX XXXX after the restriction notice and after my call with Chase confirming I can not have these accounts, I also received an email from Chase congratulating me on my new Chase accounts. The same accounts that have been closed.

This is not the first time something like this has happened either. Chase has opened and then closed deposit accounts I applied for on more than one prior occasion. That repeating pattern points to a persistent internal flag rather than anything tied to specific account behavior. 

I want to be clear about my goal in filing this complaint. It is not punitive. I value Chase as an institution and, given Chase 's national footprint, I am actively looking to transition my primary banking from the credit union I currently use to Chase. The promotional offer was meaningful to me because I was prepared to make Chase my primary bank, not because of the bonus itself. What I am asking for is a path forward to actually establish that deposit relationship and enough transparency about what happened so I can address the underlying issue.

I am actively trying to move my primary banking from my current credit union to Chase, and I am asking for a workable resolution that allows me to become a Chase deposit customer, not a refund or one-time payout.

2. A written explanation of the specific reason Chase closed accounts ending in XXXX and XXXX, so I can understand and, if possible, address whatever the underlying concern is. 

3. Disclosure of whether the closure was based on XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, another consumer reporting agency, or Chase 's internal risk database. If an external consumer reporting agency was involved, I need to know which one so I can exercise my dispute rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

4. Confirmation of whether Chase has reported the closure to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. If so, I want to know what was reported so I can address it with those agencies directly.

text:
I am filing this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. regarding material misrepresentations, deceptive business practices, failure to legally provide mandatory consumer disclosures, and systemic electronic fund access failures that resulted in actual financial damages totaling $7500.00. 
I am a XXXX veteran with documented memory-related cognitive limitations. To safely manage my finances and avoid the severe personal safety risks associated with handling large amounts of physical currency, I rely strictly on secure digital banking infrastructurespecifically mobile wallet functionality and electronic transfersas a necessary disability accommodation.

On XX/XX/year>, approximately one and a half hours before the branch closed, I opened a checking account at the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX. I explicitly informed the representative that I required immediate, reliable electronic access to my funds for scheduled international travel the following day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) because I could not safely carry physical currency. I was explicitly assured by Chase personnel that I would have immediate access to my deposited funds via mobile wallet functionality, electronic transfers, and ATM usage. These material representations directly induced me to open the account and deposit my funds.

At the time of account opening, Chase personnel failed to provide me with any physical account disclosures, fee schedules, or account terms. In an explicit admission to me, a Chase Escalations Manager stated that the only electronic signature on file from my branch session was solely to verify that my personal information was correct.

This constitutes a direct compliance failure by JPMorgan Chase. Under the Federal E-SIGN Act and Regulation DD, a financial institution can not legally substitute paper disclosures with electronic delivery without obtaining a separate, explicit, affirmative E-SIGN Consumer Consent Disclosure. Verifying identity or confirming that personal details are spelled correctly does not meet the legal threshold for electronic delivery consent. Because Chase failed to obtain valid electronic consent and failed to provide physical copies, they are in non-compliant violation of Regulation DD 's mandatory account-opening disclosure rules, leaving me completely unaware of hidden account holds or restrictions.

Immediately after leaving the branch, I experienced a catastrophic, total access failure. Every digital channel failed : transfers to my external XXXX account were blocked, mobile wallet transactions were declined, and ATM withdrawals failed.

Again I explicitly disclosed my status as a disabled veteran and detailed my memory-related cognitive limitations, reiterating that I could not safely handle or carry physical cash. Representatives stated that a flag existed on the account, but assured me they would contact XXXX to remove it and that the issue would resolve within approximately XXXX minutes in a brief phone call with the fraud department. I relied on this representation to my severe detriment ; the issue was not resolved, and the total electronic block remained. 
On XX/XX/year> ( the morning of my flight ), I returned to the XXXX XXXX XXXX. Chase personnel identified an alleged address mismatch with XXXX XXXX and stated it was completely corrected. A single $20.00 test transaction processed successfully inside the branch. However, immediately upon leaving the branch, the systemic failures resumed. The mobile wallet failed, ATM access was declined, and transfers remained blocked. This proves the access barrier extended far beyond a simple mobile wallet sync issue. 
On XX/XX/year>, I received my physical debit card. No disclosures were included. I spent over three hours on multiple calls with Chase escalation teams. A representative on a 50-minute call explicitly stated that my card was " functioning properly '' and that they " saw no declined transactions. '' Yet, at approximately XXXX XXXX  that same night, the physical card was systematically declined at an ATM. 
escalated this internally to the Chase Executive Office ( Case Reference : XXXX ). The final determination issued by reviewer " XXXX '' is a bad-faith, liability-shielding mischaracterization of events. 
Chases written response attempts to reduce this multi-day, multi-channel crisis to a routine " address mismatch. '' Their defense completely ignores the fact that the address was corrected on XX/XX/XXXX and that physical ATM and debit card declines continued days afterward. Furthermore, their response claims I " raised no concerns '' at account opening, disingenuously portraying me as dishonest ; I had no concerns to raise on XX/XX/XXXX because I had not yet attempted to use the non-functional product Chase marketed to me until only after banks closing hours. Neither was I aware that Chase does NOT HAVE A 24/hour customer service line. The fraud department is the only department 24 hours. As a direct result of Chases deceptive practices, electronic fund blockages, and total failure to accommodate my disability needs during a critical travel window, I suffered severe, measurable financial harm : 1. Travel Loss ( $1700.00 ) : Because Chase completely froze access to my travel capital, I was forced to miss my scheduled international flight on XX/XX/year>. 
2. Cash Loss ( $5800.00 ) : Because Chase paralyzed all electronic channels and provided no alternative digital access bridge, I was forced into a highly vulnerable physical security position. To access my own money, I had to physically enter a branch and withdraw massive physical cash reserves, forcing me to handle large amounts of physical currency despite my cognitive limitations, which directly resulted in a subsequent physical cash loss of $5800.00.

I possess corroborating audio recordings of Chase personnel and fraud supervisors admitting that I should have received physical disclosures, that this situation was highly unusual, and that they had " never seen anything like it. '' I advise the CFPB when looking into the matter to request phone recordings between myself and Chase staff to corroborate my affidavit. From XX/XX/year> - XX/XX/year>. This complaint is based on new developments after Chases prior CFPB response regarding my earlier complaint, CFPB complaint number XXXX, submitted on XX/XX/year>. Chase Executive Office has now issued a written denial of the remaining $3700.00 claim, and Chase still has not provided the records and documentation relied upon in denying that claim. 

I am submitting this complaint because JPMorgan Chase denied my claim for unauthorized electronic fund transfers after my phone was lost or stolen, and Chase still has not provided the investigative documentation, records relied upon, or electronic audit trail needed to explain that denial. 

On XX/XX/year>, my XXXX was lost or stolen. The device was protected by a passcode and XXXX XXXX Shortly afterward, unauthorized activity occurred involving my financial accounts. 

On XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX, 2026, unauthorized XXXX debits totaling $16000.00 were initiated from my JPMorgan Chase checking account ending in XXXX to XXXX. I did not authorize these transactions, did not initiate them, and received no goods, services, or benefit from them. I discovered the activity on XX/XX/year>, and reported it to Chase on XX/XX/year>. 

I filed a police report on XX/XX/year>, filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, and took steps to secure my accounts and credit profile after discovering the unauthorized activity. 

This same broader identity-theft episode also involved XXXX  / XXXX XXXX. Separate attempted ACH transfers totaling $4200.00 were tied to that activity, but those transfers did not settle and the funds never left my account. Even so, the amount was referred to XXXX for collection. I disputed that debt, and XXXX later confirmed in writing that the debt was forgiven, collection had ceased, and nothing had been or would be reported to any credit reporting agency. 

XXXX separately returned $12000.00 of the unauthorized withdrawals. After that partial recovery, the remaining unreimbursed loss was $3700.00. 

Chase received my supporting documentation, including the police report, FTC Identity Theft Report, replacement-phone receipt, and XXXX reimbursement check. Chase later confirmed in writing that it had reviewed those materials as part of its reconsideration of my claim. 

Despite that, Chase denied reimbursement of the remaining $3700.00. Chase stated only that it did not find evidence to support reimbursement and directed me to continue working directly with the merchant because the merchant initiated the transactions. 

That was not a real solution. Chase knew or should have known that sending me back to XXXX was a dead end, because XXXX had already returned only $12000.00, stated that the remaining funds were played through, and later repeated that it would not refund any further balance and considered the matter closed. 

My representative and I repeatedly asked Chase to identify the exact factual basis for its conclusion, to state whether Chase contends the disputed transfers were authorized, and to provide the specific records, materials, and information Chase relied on in denying reimbursement, including XXXX authorization records, merchant records, prior transaction history, device information, login information, and any other evidence. We also asked Chase to preserve and provide its claim-review materials and related records. Chase still has not provided that documentation. 

This is especially troubling because the related XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX matter arising from the same broader fraudulent episode was resolved in my favor as fraud / account takeover, with all related debts forgiven, collection ended, and no credit reporting. That outcome is consistent with my position that unauthorized activity occurred after my phone was lost or stolen. 

XXXX Requested : XXXX. Reimburse the remaining $3700.00 from the unauthorized XXXX transfers. 
XXXX. Provide the complete investigative file for Chases denial, including all documents, records, internal notes, merchant communications, and the electronic audit trail or equivalent materials relied upon in reaching its decision.

I am filing this complaint regarding a misleading and inadequately disclosed benefit restriction associated with my Chase Sapphire Reserve card and a hotel booking made through Chase Travel under The Edit hotel program.

I booked a hotel stay through Chase Travel and selected the Pay Later option during checkout. At no point during the booking flow was it clearly and conspicuously disclosed that selecting Pay Later would disqualify me from receiving the advertised $250.00 Chase Sapphire Reserve hotel credit benefit associated with the booking. 
The booking interface prominently advertised the premium benefits included with the stay and presented Pay Now and Pay Later simply as payment preference options. There was no clear warning, disclosure, or indication that choosing one payment timing option over the other would cause forfeiture of the advertised cardmember credit benefit. 

I have attached screenshots demonstrating the booking flow and wording presented during checkout. The screenshots are from a sample booking because the original trip has already occurred, but the booking flow and language were identical to the reservation in question. 

As a result of the unclear and misleading booking process, I completed the stay believing I would receive the advertised Chase Sapphire Reserve credit benefit, only to later discover that Chase denied the credit entirely due to the payment selection method. 

I contacted Chase customer service multiple times attempting to resolve the matter. Despite explaining that the booking failed to adequately disclose the restriction, I received no meaningful assistance or reasonable accommodation. 

I have been a loyal Chase customer for years and pay a substantial annual fee for the Chase Sapphire Reserve card specifically because of the premium travel protections and advertised benefits. Instead, I experienced what I believe was a material omission and misleading disclosure practice that caused financial harm to the consumer. 

The issue is not simply disagreement over policy. The issue is that the policy was not clearly disclosed during the booking process in a manner that would allow a reasonable consumer to make an informed decision. 

the booking flow is designed in a confusing and misleading way that can easily cause consumers to unintentionally lose major advertised benefits without proper notice.

I am requesting the following resolution : 1. That Chase manually honor and apply the $250.00 credit associated with my reservation.

2. That Chase review and improve the disclosure language and booking flow within Chase Travel and The Edit hotel program so customers are clearly informed, before completing checkout, that selecting Pay Later forfeits eligibility for certain advertised benefits or statement credits. 

I have attached supporting screenshots and records of my communications with customer service. 

Thank you for your review.

On XX/XX/XXXX, a company called XXXX XXXX XXXX electronically withdrew approximately $10000.00 without any authorization whatsoever from our XXXX checking account. XXXX XXXX XXXX is a Chase client that has nothing to do with us or XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

When XXXX asked Chase to reimburse the funds, Chase stated that legally, the condo had 48 hours to report the fraud. However, we did not receive the bank statement until XX/XX/XXXX. We reported the fraud to XXXX XXXX XXXX  immediately, but XXXX argued that if we reviewed our checking account daily, we would have discovered the fraud within the 48-hour period. We responded that it is unrealistic for us to review our checking account every day, as we operate a business with multiple accounts. The same fraudster attempted to withdraw an additional $14000.00 on XX/XX/XXXX but because we had reported the issue, the attempt failed. I contacted my Chase representative, who stated that Chase was not even going to investigate the matter. I then contacted a Chase Wealth Management representative and reminded them that the bank has a duty to know its customer and, if the customer has acted fraudulently, the account should be closed. The private banker stated that they had investigated and found no history of fraud associated with this client. I responded that this was ridiculous, since the client fraudulently withdrew funds from our account twice, on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. 

I also contacted XXXX XXXX, CEO of Chase. While I did not speak with him directly, one of his executives spoke to me. I explained the situation, and she acknowledged that the bank has a duty to know its customer. She stated that she would investigate and get back to me within a few weeks. 

I also contacted the Federal Consumer Protection Agency and explained the situation. They advised that we file a police report. XXXX from our office went to the local precinct and reported the fraud. The precinct stated that we should receive confirmation of the report within about a week.

text:
CFPB Complaint New Evidence / ECOA and Regulation B Concern Company : JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.

Prior CFPB Complaint : XXXX Executive Office Reference : XXXX Product : Credit card application Issue : Possible disparate treatment and inconsistent documentation practices involving a non-U.S. citizen applicant Complaint Narrative I am filing this complaint because JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A . has provided additional written information after my prior CFPB complaint, and that information raises further concerns regarding the handling of my credit card application and the documentation requirements imposed on me as a non-U.S. citizen.

My prior CFPB complaint, number XXXX, concerned my XX/XX/year> in-branch application for a Chase Freedom credit card at the XXXX XXXX branch in XXXX , Washington.

In Chases prior CFPB response, Chase stated that the application was reviewed under standard procedures and that the application XXXX  did not indicate that additional documentation or verification was requested. However, in the same response, Chase acknowledged that during the branch visit I provided my U.S. Employment Authorization Document and passport, that the banker requested my drivers license, and that my Social Security card was also requested. Chase further stated that four identification documents were recommended to be scanned in order to prevent possible issues or delays.

This creates a serious inconsistency. Chase can not fairly claim that no additional documentation or verification was requested while also acknowledging that multiple high-level identity and immigration-related documents were requested and scanned during the same application process.

After that CFPB complaint was closed, Chases Executive Office issued another written response dated XX/XX/year>, reference XXXX, again explaining that additional documentation was requested because I was a non-U.S. citizen, because my XXXX  did not show my current U.S. address , and because my Social Security number was not on file.

I understand that Chase has the right to verify identity, comply with banking requirements, and confirm information needed for a credit application. My complaint is not about lawful identity verification. My complaint is that Chases own written responses show that my non-U.S. citizenship status triggered a more burdensome documentation process connected to a credit application, while Chase has not provided a clear, consistent, and specific explanation showing that this process was applied equally to similarly situated U.S. citizen applicants.

Chase has also failed to explain whether the additional documentation process delayed, discouraged, affected, or contributed to the denial or adverse handling of my credit card application. Chases explanation focuses on identity verification, but it does not answer the core fair-lending concern : whether I was subjected to a materially different process because of my citizenship or immigration-related status.

This is particularly concerning because Chases earlier CFPB response relied on credit-related reasons for the denial, including alleged high credit usage, overdraft history, limited credit experience, and high balances. Yet during the actual branch application process, the focus was heavily placed on documentation and verification tied to my non-U.S. citizen status. Chase has never provided a complete explanation reconciling these two issues.

I respectfully request CFPB review because Chases responses appear internally inconsistent and raise concerns under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B regarding whether my credit application was handled fairly, consistently, and without unlawful disparate treatment.

Monetary Compensation Request I am also requesting monetary compensation for the harm caused by Chases handling of this credit application.

My request is based on Chases inconsistent written explanations, the additional documentation burden imposed during the in-branch credit application process, the hard credit inquiry generated from a process I believe was not handled fairly or consistently, the time and administrative burden required to pursue clarification, and the distress caused by what appears to be materially different treatment tied to my non-U.S. citizen status.

I understand that the CFPB complaint process is not a court proceeding. However, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act provides for actual damages and, in appropriate cases, punitive damages against a creditor that fails to comply with

ECOA requirements. For individual claims, punitive damages may be available up to $10000.00 under 15 U.S.C. 1691e. For that reason, I request that Chase provide monetary compensation in an amount up to $10000.00, or another fair settlement amount, to resolve the harm caused by the inconsistent and potentially discriminatory handling of my application. This compensation request is separate from, and in addition to, my request for a neutral manual review, inquiry removal, written explanation, and corrective action.

On XX/XX/year>, while traveling through XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, I was approached by an employee of a XXXX  XXXX  identified as XXXX XXXX. I was subjected to an extremely high-pressure sales presentation while attempting to board my flight home. 
During this encounter, I repeatedly stated that I needed to leave for my flight. However, multiple employees continued to pressure me to remain. Prices were not clearly disclosed before the transactions were processed. The products were never shown to me before purchase. Products were applied to my face and I was instructed to sit while they dried. The products were then packaged and placed into bags without my being shown what was being purchased. I did not knowingly agree to purchase more than $24000.00 worth of skincare products and beauty devices. 
Three transactions were charged to my Chase credit card on XX/XX/year> : $7200.00 $9300.00 $7400.00 Total disputed amount : approximately $24000.00. 
One employee ultimately escorted me to my gate carrying one of the bags while my family members were hearing final boarding announcements for me. The circumstances were confusing, intimidating, and did not allow me to make an informed purchasing decision. 
After returning home, I disputed the charges with Chase and provided detailed written statements, photographs of the products, supporting documentation, and additional evidence. I explained that prices were not properly disclosed, that the products were not shown to me before purchase, and that I believed the transactions resulted from deceptive and misleading sales practices. 
Chase initially denied the dispute. After I submitted additional evidence, Chase reopened the dispute. I provided further documentation, including photographs of the products, packaging, labeling, evidence of similar public complaints involving this merchant, information regarding FDA warning letters involving similar product branding and medical marketing claims, and other information relevant to the representations made during the sale.

Despite reopening the dispute and reviewing the additional materials, Chase denied the dispute again. In its denial letter, Chase stated that I may have a valid complaint with the merchant but nevertheless concluded that the transactions were valid and would remain my responsibility. 
In addition, I was informed by a Chase representative that there had been an attempted charge or suspicious activity of approximately $1900.00 associated with the same merchant group or location that Chase had detected and credited. Different Chase representatives later provided conflicting explanations regarding this transaction. One representative stated it was suspicious activity that Chase caught, while another representative stated it was a merchant credit but could not explain what it related to. This raised additional concerns regarding the security of my payment information and the accuracy of Chase 's investigation.

I also experienced multiple issues with Chase 's handling of the dispute, including conflicting information from representatives, dispute-related documents that Chase stated were mailed but were never received, and uncertainty regarding the impact of the disputed $24000.00 balance on my credit while the dispute was pending.

I am requesting that the CFPB review Chase 's handling of this dispute and determine whether Chase conducted a reasonable investigation of the evidence I submitted. I am also requesting that Chase provide all documents, merchant responses, receipts, and evidence relied upon in denying my claim. 
I do not believe Chase adequately addressed the evidence demonstrating that these transactions occurred under deceptive and misleading circumstances, without informed consent regarding the products and prices involved, and under significant pressure while I was attempting to board an international flight. I respectfully request assistance in obtaining a fair review of this matter.

'' The rental office called to tell me they hadn't received the XXXX payment. I checked my bank transaction and realized the payee 's name had been changed. text:
On or around XXXX XXXX XXXX, I made a payment of approximately $3000.00 to pay off my Chase Sapphire XXXX credit card. Shortly after making that payment, approximately $1600.00 was suddenly added back to my account without warning, explanation, or supporting documentation. 

On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Chase to determine why this balance had appeared. After reviewing my account, the representative expressly acknowledged that the charges did not appear to be valid. The representative apologized, stated that the issue appeared to be Chase 's fault and related to a system update, and assured me that the balance would be corrected by approximately XXXX XXXX. the following morning. Based on these statements, I reasonably believed Chase had identified an internal error and that the matter would be resolved. 

When the balance remained on my account, I called Chase again the following day. What followed was XXXX of the most frustrating customer service experiences I have ever encountered. During a call lasting approximately XXXX hours, I was transferred repeatedly and spoke with more than XXXX representatives and supervisors. Despite the fact that Chase had previously acknowledged that the balance appeared incorrect and was related to a system issue, I was suddenly told that the balance was valid. However, no one could clearly explain why. 

Throughout the call, I repeatedly requested a detailed itemized accounting of the approximately $1600.00 balance. I specifically asked Chase to identify every charge, adjustment, reversal, fee, and transaction that created the balance and explain why I was responsible for it. Representative after representative either stated they could not locate the information, could not explain the charges, or claimed the matter was outside their department 's authority. Some representatives suggested the balance was related to reversed disputes, while others stated they could not determine where the charges originated. The explanations were inconsistent, contradictory, and unsupported by documentation. 

What I found particularly troubling was what occurred during that call. While I was actively disputing the unexplained balance and repeatedly requesting documentation, a representative became dismissive and argumentative. During that exchange, I was abruptly informed that the balance had increased from approximately $1600.00 to approximately $2500.00. 

When I asked why the balance had suddenly increased by nearly another $900.00 while I was on the phone attempting to resolve the matter, no explanation was provided. No representative could identify the charges, adjustments, reversals, fees, or transactions responsible for the increase. Instead, I was transferred again and forced to repeat the same conversation with additional departments. 

From a consumer 's perspective, this was alarming. I contacted Chase because an unexplained $1600.00 balance had appeared after I paid off my account. Chase initially admitted the balance appeared incorrect and attributed it to a system issue. Less than XXXX hours later, Chase reversed its position, claimed the balance was valid, failed to provide any supporting documentation, and then informed me that the amount I allegedly owed had increased substantially while I was actively disputing it. 

At that point, I no longer had confidence that Chase 's records were accurate. Chase was demanding payment of a balance that its own employees could not explain, document, or itemize. The fact that the amount continued to change while representatives were unable to identify the underlying charges raises serious concerns regarding the accuracy of Chase 's account records, billing practices, and handling of consumer disputes. 

I also repeatedly requested escalation options, complaint procedures, reference numbers, and written documentation. Despite speaking with more than XXXX representatives and supervisors, I was unable to obtain a meaningful explanation, an itemized accounting, or a resolution. I was told on multiple occasions that documentation would be sent, but I never received it. Eventually, after hours of transfers and contradictory information, I was placed on hold and the call ended without resolution. 

I am requesting that Chase conduct a thorough investigation, review the recorded calls from XX/XX/year> and the following day, provide a complete itemized accounting of every charge, reversal, adjustment, fee, interest charge, and transaction that created this balance, remove any unsupported or inaccurate charges, refund any resulting fees or interest, and correct any adverse credit reporting associated with this dispute. If Chase can not provide documentation substantiating these balances, the charges should be removed from my account. 

Consumers should not be expected to pay balances that a financial institution can not explain, document, or consistently account for. I am seeking a complete explanation, correction of any inaccuracies, and appropriate relief.

text:
I am filing this complaint because JP Morgan Chase has now denied a legitimate billing dispute twice without ever examining the actual substance of my claim, and I am frankly appalled at how this has been handled. 

The disputed charge is $590.00, posted on or around XX/XX/year> to my account ending in XXXX, for a cash co-payment XXXX demanded on a XXXX award airline ticket. This is not a complaint about a price I simply disliked. It is a documented case of arbitrary, self-contradicting, and deceptive pricing by the merchant, and the evidence proving it has been submitted to the issuer and ignored. 

Below is exactly what happened, in the utmost detail : I held approximately XXXX points with XXXX ( another credit card ) and transferred them to XXXX XXXX at a XXXX ratio, giving me roughly XXXX XXXX. By XXXX 's own published valuation, those points were worth about $620.00 if I were to book a ticket on their portal. However, I transferred them to XXXX ( who, according to various travel websites had a better point valuation ) for XXXX specific purpose : to book a round-trip flight from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

The ordinary cash price for that exact itinerary, on those same airlines, was $ XXXX. I have screenshots documenting this. 

When I attempted to book that round trip as an award ticket on XXXX 's website, the merchant demanded ALL XXXX of my miles PLUS an additional $1100.00 in cash for the same exact flights. 

Consider what that actually means : - Buying the ticket outright with cash : $ XXXX. 
- Booking the very same seats using miles : about $620.00 worth of miles, XXXX $1100.00 in cash, resulting in an effective total cost of roughly $1700.00. 

In other words, XXXX required me to surrender XXXX miles AND pay $1100.00 ( more than double the cash price ) for a flight I could have simply purchased for $ XXXX. Redeeming my miles did not save me a single dollar ; it cost me far more than paying cash would have. That is the exact opposite of what an airline-miles program is represented to be, and it is the heart of why this is deceptive. 

At the same time, XXXX did not offer me the option of refunding my miles back to XXXX so I can at least book my ticket on their respective travel portal. This way, they effectively " trapped '' me into having to make a decision that I could have avoided. 

When I asked XXXX 's customer service to explain, the only answer I received was " dynamic pricing with partner airlines ''. That does not explain, and can not justify, charging a large cash premium far above the open-market cash fare for the same seats. In addition, this explanation was given to me verbally, through the phone, meaning that they carefully tried to avoid producing written documentation for it. 

Because the round-trip redemption was economically absurd, I booked the XXXX legs separately in an effort to find a way around the " trap '' to which they lead me with their deceptive advertising and arbitray pricing. The outbound leg ( XXXX to XXXX. Normal price $ XXXX ) redeemed for XXXX miles. The return leg ( XXXX to XXXX, a ticket worth again roughly $ XXXX in cash ) required only XXXX miles PLUS the $590.00 cash charge I am now disputing. The merchant 's own back-to-back pricing contradicts itself : XXXX miles covered a ~ $450.00 ticket, yet a comparable ~ $500.00 ticket cost XXXX miles AND an extra $590.00 in cash. There is no consistent, disclosed valuation that produces both of those numbers. I received no additional product, service, or benefit for that $590.00 ; I was charged it solely because of the merchant 's undisclosed and self-contradicting valuation of its own currency. In addition to all of that, the fact that I could use the XXXX miles on XXXX separate flights for a total of approximately $700.00 ( including the taxes I paid for the first of the XXXX flights which was covered with XXXX miles ) proves beyond any doubt the arbitrary and absurd demand of XXXX for $1100.00 on top of my XXXX, which they presented as the price to me as the option for booking a single round-trip ticket. 

This is not buyer 's remorse over a price I knowingly agreed to. It is a documented case of a merchant assigning arbitrary, inconsistent, and undisclosed value to its own currency in order to extract cash above the market fare. I relied on the represented value of these miles when I transferred them, and that reliance was defeated entirely by the merchant 's conduct. In addition, I could not avoid booking the ticket on XXXX, as that would mean my XXXX would just be wasted for no reason. 

Despite submitting this evidence, JP Morgan Chase denied the dispute twice, apparently treating it as generic " cardholder dissatisfaction '' rather than examining the inconsistent-pricing evidence. When the issuer contacted me regarding the denial, no substantive explanation was provided. That is not an investigation ; it is a rubber stamp, and it is unacceptable. 

I am confident I am right about this, because the merchant 's own records prove it. I have also filed a separate complaint with the XXXX Department of Transportation XXXX XXXX 's deceptive pricing. 

WHAT I CONSIDER A FAIR RESOLUTION : XXXX. A permanent credit of $590.00 to my account. 
XXXX. A written explanation of the specific factual basis and reason code used to deny my dispute on each occasion, directly addressing the pricing inconsistency described above. 

I expect this complaint to be reviewed on its merits, rather than dismissed without consideration as it has been twice already. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Subject : Complaint Against Chase Freedom Unlimited Credit Card Payment Processing Delays, Credit Reporting Concerns, and Potential Unfair Practices To Whom It XXXX Concern : I am filing a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . regarding the handling of my Chase Freedom Unlimited credit card account. 
I have been a Chase customer for several years and have made consistent efforts to maintain my account responsibly. However, Chase has repeatedly delayed the processing of my payments, which has interfered with my ability to pay my credit card balance in full and has negatively impacted my financial standing. 
My concerns include the following : Payment Processing Delays Chase has taken longer than expected to process payments made to my credit card account. These delays have prevented my available credit from updating in a timely manner and have interfered with my ability to manage my account effectively. I believe these delays may constitute an unfair practice if payments are not being credited promptly upon receipt.

Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666c, and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.10, creditors are generally required to credit payments as of the date of receipt when payments are made according to the creditor 's requirements.

Credit Reporting Accuracy Concerns I am concerned that Chase may not be accurately reporting my account history, payment history, utilization, and account status to consumer reporting agencies.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, requires furnishers of information to provide accurate information to credit reporting agencies and to investigate disputes regarding inaccurate reporting. 
If Chase has reported inaccurate payment information, balances, utilization, or account history, I request that such information be immediately corrected with all consumer reporting agencies. 
Potential Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices The repeated delays in payment processing and the resulting impact on my account may constitute an unfair practice under the Consumer Financial Protection Act 's prohibition against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ), 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536.

Consumers should be able to make payments and have those payments processed within reasonable and disclosed timeframes. Delays that interfere with account management, available credit, or credit reporting can create unnecessary financial harm.

I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require Chase to : Conduct a full review of my account history. Provide a detailed explanation of all payment processing delays. Correct any inaccurate information reported to consumer reporting agencies. Remove any negative reporting caused by improper payment processing delays. Provide written confirmation of any corrections made. Ensure future payments are processed in accordance with applicable federal law and regulatory requirements. 
I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including account statements, payment confirmations, screenshots, and correspondence with Chase. 
Thank you for your attention to this matter. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX Chase Freedom Unlimited Account Holder

I am filing this formal complaint regarding a fraudulent and materially altered check processed through my joint checking account at JP Morgan Chase Bank XXXX XXXX. 

Summary of key facts - Check XXXX XXXXXXXX was materially altered in a visibly obvious manner and cashed out of my bank account ; - The check was processed despite visible signs of tampering ; - The fraud was discovered on XX/XX/XXXX and reported immediately, without delay ; - The alteration was acknowledged by bank personnel as obvious ; - Printed statements were no longer delivered to me for many years ; - I had no effective access to online banking or electronic statements ; - No written responses were provided by the bank, only verbal communications. 

I request a full refund of amount $2300.00 unlawfully withdrawn from my bank account.

1. Fraudulent and materially altered check and discovery The check in question ( Check No. XXXX, dated XX/XX/XXXX, in the amount of $2300.00 ) was stolen and materially altered before being negotiated. 

The alteration is visually obvious on the face of the check, including an obviously whitewashed erasure and inconsistent handwriting in the payee field, which is clearly visible on the check copy. 
JP Morgan Chase employee XXXX XXXX first noticed and brought to my attention the fraudulent check, when she provided, at my request, a complete copy of my account which I needed and requested in anticipation of the upcoming tax season. 
I was shocked and officially informed the bank on XX/XX/XXXX. 

As a result of my diligence, I reported the matter to higher levels of bank management immediately upon discovery and without delay. 

A bank manager, XXXX XXXX ( Chase branch XXXX at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), acknowledged that the check was modified and that the fraud and alteration were obvious upon review of the check. 
That should have been identified during processing, which I understand is a core responsibility of the bank.

2. Failure to exercise ordinary care Despite the obvious and visible nature of the alteration, the financial institution processed the check. 

The facts support that the altered nature of this check was not detected at the time of processing, despite the institutions obligation to exercise ordinary care in reviewing negotiable instruments for obvious irregularities.

3. Lack of timely account statement access I have never maintained an online banking account and do not use online banking services. 
Historically, printed paper statements were provided to me in the distant past. However, printed statements stopped being delivered to me many years ago for reasons that are unclear. 
I never enrolled in electronic statements or maintained active online banking access. 
As a result, I did not have practical access to timely account statements for many years including during the relevant time period.

4. Lack of response and ineffective resolution attempts Despite multiple in-person visits to the bank regarding this issue, as well as multiple phone calls, I did not receive any written responses, in fact any meaningful in earnest response at all, addressing the substance of this matter. 

All substantive communication from the bank regarding this matter was verbal only. 

No formal written resolution, denial, rationale, or documented explanation was provided regarding the handling of this matter or specifically the fraudulent check. Bank managers assured me that I had a strong case and promised repeatedly that they would assist me with my claim in every way, that I would be able to reach them whenever needed, that they would return my calls, etc., but unfortunately I never received any follow up or practical advice ( other than to close my account and open a new one ) either by phone or in writing. 

6. Request for CFPB intervention I hereby respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and, in so doing, require the financial institution to provide : 1. A full investigation into the fraudulent and materially altered check ; 2. Copies of the processed check, including both front and back images ; 3. A formal review of the institutions handling of a materially altered negotiable instrument under applicable banking standards ; 4. Reassessment of any denial based on reporting timeframe in light of lack of practical statement access ; and 5. Full reimbursement of the funds associated with the fraudulent transaction. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX number ( XXXX ) XXXX
