I am submitting this complaint regarding the travel insurance benefit associated with my Chase credit card. My claim for rental vehicle damage ( Claim # XXXX ) was approved by Chase Benefits. However, the reimbursement I received was incomplete. 

The rental damage charge posted to my Chase credit card was $2500.00, but I was reimbursed only $2200.00, leaving an unpaid balance of $350.00. 

After receiving the reimbursement, I contacted Chase Benefits to report the discrepancy. During multiple phone calls, I was told that the reimbursement shortfall needed to be addressed through email, so I followed those instructions and repeatedly emailed them with all requested supporting documentation. 

My attempts to resolve this matter include : Phone calls : XX/XX/XXXX ; XX/XX/XXXX ; XX/XX/XXXX ; Emails : XX/XX/XXXX ; XX/XX/XXXX ; XX/XX/XXXX During each phone call, the Chase Benefits representative reviewed my concern and agreed that there was a reimbursement shortfall that required further review. However, rather than resolving it over the phone, I was repeatedly instructed to submit my request by email. I followed those instructions every time and provided all requested supporting documentation. Despite multiple emails and follow-ups over more than a year, I never received a response by email, and the reimbursement was never corrected. 

After exhausting everything, I filed a complaint directly with Chase on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Chase responded by providing me with the phone number for its Disputes Department and informed me that this department could only be contacted by phone, not by email. 

This was concerning for two reasons. First, after more than a year of unsuccessful attempts, I wanted to keep all communications in writing so there would be a complete record. '' In other words, Chase could not confirm whether it was directing me to the appropriate department. 

After spending more than a year following every instruction I was given, repeatedly submitting documentation, and waiting through the requested processing periods, I do not believe it is reasonable to continue pursuing another process that appears unrelated to my approved insurance claim simply to determine whether it might be the correct one. 

I have made every reasonable effort to resolve this matter directly with Chase Benefits and Chase. On XX/XX/year>, I purchased fabric represented as 100 % silk from a shop in XXXX. The shop displayed signage suggesting it was a government-affiliated store, which I later confirmed is false. I was charged through a business named " XXXX XXXX XXXX '', which is a different name than the XXXX displayed on the storefront ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) where I made the purchase. 

After returning home, I performed a burn test on the fabric, which confirmed it is polyester, not silk. I paid silk pricing for a synthetic product, sold to me through false claims about both the material and the seller 's government affiliation. 
I filed a dispute with Chase regarding this charge. I was initially told nothing could be done. I filed a follow-up dispute and was issued a provisional credit. Chase later reversed this credit and reinstated the charge after the merchant submitted a receipt as evidence. The receipt that itself shows a business name different from the storefront name, and that does not address or refute my claim that the goods were misrepresented. 

I am requesting that the CFPB review whether Chase adequately investigated the substance of this dispute, that the goods were fraudulently misrepresented, rather than relying solely on a receipt that does not match the storefront name and does not establish the authenticity of the product sold. The discrepancy between the storefront and the billing name is itself evidence of deceptive business practices, and the burn test result directly contradicts the merchant 's claims about the product. 
I am requesting that Chase reopen this dispute and properly evaluate the merits of my claim under the Fair Credit Billing Act.
